title: Client-Facing Chief Financial Officer - Manufacturing Focus
description:
Do you speak the language of the shop floor and the boardroom?

Have you spent your career helping manufacturers understand what their numbers are really telling them?

Are you ready to make an impact across a portfolio of growing businesses—not just one?

Join ALC, a fast-growing, fully remote CFO Advisory, Outsourced Accounting, and HR Services firm. We are on a mission to 'WOW professionally and CARE personally' by providing expert guidance, people centric service, and custom solutions. We believe the combination of unmatched strategic thinking and experience, coupled with a caring human touch, is the key to success and allows us to bring clarity, confidence, and peace of mind to the growing organizations and business leaders we serve.

We're Seeking:

  • Seasoned finance leaders with deep manufacturing roots who love helping owner-operated businesses grow.
  • Strategic thinkers who can connect cost accounting, inventory, and plant operations to the bigger financial picture.
  • Trusted advisors who are as comfortable walking the floor with an operations manager as they are presenting to a board or lender.
  • Leaders who light up when mentoring others and building strong, accountable teams.
  • Someone with a CAN-DO, positive attitude committed to continual growth for themselves and the team around them.

Who We Are:

We are a passionate team serving privately held, entrepreneurial businesses across the U.S. Our domains span property management, real estate, data management, professional services, non-profits, transportation & logistics, distribution, and more.

Core Values We Live By:

  • Speak Your Truth
  • Get Sh*t Done
  • Team Up
  • Be Curious
  • Choose Joy

RESPONSIBILITIES

As a CFO with ALC, you will be a trusted strategic partner to our manufacturing and production-based clients (and other types of clients as needed)—owning the full client relationship, analyzing financials, providing actionable recommendations, and helping owners and leadership teams navigate complex financial decisions with confidence. Leading client teams of Controllers and accountants, you will set the tone for each partnership and champion our brand promise: Wow Professionally, Care Personally.

We aim to be our client’s true strategic partner and an extension of their team. As such, as a CFO, you will:

  • Own the end-to-end client relationship, providing strategic guidance in financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, risk management, M&A, and capital investment decisions.
  • Build and maintain cost accounting structures—standard, job, or process costing; bills of material; labor and overhead absorption—and lead variance analysis that gives clients a true picture of margin by product, line, and customer.
  • Oversee inventory accounting across raw materials, work-in-process, and finished goods, including physical counts, costing methods, and obsolescence reserves, while driving improvements in inventory turns and accuracy.
  • Translate plant data—capacity utilization, throughput, scrap and yield, cost per unit—into financial decisions and KPI dashboards that connect the plant floor to the P&L.
  • Lead capital expenditure and equipment ROI analysis, make-vs-buy decisions, and working capital strategy; manage lender relationships, borrowing base reporting, and covenant compliance.
  • Build pricing and quoting models that account for raw material and commodity costs, tariffs, supplier terms, and demand shifts.
  • Help clients get the most from their ERP/MRP systems so costing, inventory, and production data flow accurately into financial reporting.
  • Lead structured, impactful client QBRs and deliver service that consistently earns outstanding client satisfaction.
  • Proactively manage client scope and margin, and contribute to firm growth by bringing manufacturing credibility to proposals and prospect conversations.
  • Lead, mentor, and develop client teams, sharing manufacturing know-how with Controllers and accountants to raise ALC’s capability as a whole.

  • Builds trusted relationships by offering clear, strategic financial guidance rooted in deep technical expertise.
  • Earns credibility on the plant floor as well as in the boardroom, making financial information accessible to plant managers and operations, purchasing, and sales leaders.
  • Operates as a steady and confident leader, especially in complex or high-pressure situations.
  • Thinks holistically—balancing short-term wins with long-term value and scalability for clients.
  • Demonstrates strong executive presence and communication skills, able to engage credibly with C-suite and board-level stakeholders.
  • Maintains a growth mindset and uses quarterly reviews, feedback, and KPIs to drive continual improvement.
  • Partners across departments and functions to provide integrated solutions that support business goals.
  • Proactively identifies financial and operational risks, offering creative, strategic solutions.
  • Guides and inspires team members, mentoring others and developing future leaders.
  • Embodies ALC's commitment to WOW professionally and CARE personally, ensuring clients feel valued, supported, and understood.

Requirements

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in financial advisory, strategic accounting, or CFO services, including 5+ years in a senior finance leadership role within a manufacturing or production-based company
  • Hands-on expertise in manufacturing cost accounting, including implementing and maintaining various costing methods, inventory valuation, variance analysis, and product/customer profitability
  • Experience working within manufacturing ERP/MRP systems and partnering with operations leaders on capacity, pricing, and capital equipment decisions
  • Proven leadership in guiding mid-market businesses through financial planning, capital strategy, lender relationships, and operational efficiency
  • Strong background in accounting principles, GAAP (including inventory accounting), and forecasting tools
  • Demonstrated ability to serve as a trusted advisor in complex business scenarios including M&A, restructuring, and risk mitigation
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills; able to simplify the complex and build trust with executives, operators, and team members alike
  • An uncompromising sense of integrity and ethics, and a passion for mentoring others and fostering a strong, value-aligned culture

Benefits

  • "Work Wherever" philosophy - independence, freedom and flexibility by working from your home office!!
  • Full benefits including health, dental, vision, accident, and pet insurance
  • Flexible vacation and a company close at the end of the year!
  • 401k plan with company match
  • No busy season!!
  • Fun, friendly, and collaborative culture that thrives on individual and team accountability

As part of our comprehensive recruiting process, we will include two short assessments, the results of which will be considered as part of your overall application. Additionally, there will be a live accounting test via Teams Screen Share to confirm your accounting skills. Passing this test is a mandatory requirement for this position. Please only apply if you are confident in your ability to successfully complete this test.

The salary range for this position is $175,000 - $185,000.

How We Determine Compensation:

As a fully remote employer, ALC determines pay for positions by considering national and industry-specific survey data. We assess external equity and the cost of labor/prevailing wage index in the marketplace for jobs comparable to those within our company.

For new hires, we aim to offer competitive compensation that allows room for future growth. title: Manager, Client Success
description:
Landmark Ventures is looking for a Manager, Client Success to join our Events & Experiences team.

We work with leading global brands and high-growth B2B companies to bring the right people together – through intimate VIP dinners, executive roundtables, curated experiences, summits and other high-impact gatherings.

Our clients come to Landmark because we know how to convene extraordinary people and create experiences that lead to meaningful relationships and business outcomes.

We're looking for someone who can help make that experience exceptional from the client's side.

As a Manager, Client Success, you'll become a trusted day-to-day partner to a portfolio of Landmark clients. You'll help them think through what they should do, where they should do it, when it should happen, who should be in the room and how to make each experience successful.

You'll also make sure things happen.

You'll navigate calendars, prepare for client calls, coordinate with our internal teams, answer operational questions, develop speaker materials, help recruit the occasional executive or speaker, track commitments and anticipate what's needed next.

And because you'll understand our clients deeply, you'll help identify where Landmark can support our partners to do more – another dinner, another city, another audience, another experience or another way to help them achieve their goals.

This is not traditional account management. And it isn't event production.

It's a relationship-driven role at the intersection of client success, executive experiences and execution.

What You'll Do

  • Own the Client Experience
    • Become someone our clients trust, rely on and genuinely enjoy working with.
    • You'll serve as a primary day-to-day contact for a portfolio of clients, developing a strong understanding of their businesses, people, priorities and objectives.
    • You'll lead and participate in client calls, keep everyone aligned on decisions and next steps, answer questions quickly and make sure clients always know where things stand.
    • You'll learn how each client likes to work and anticipate what they need before they have to ask.
    • Most importantly, you'll make Landmark feel easy to work with – responsive, thoughtful, organized and dependable.
  • Help Clients Build Great Experiences
    • Our clients don't always arrive knowing exactly what they should do.That's where you come in.
    • You'll help clients think through their calendars and advise them on opportunities for VIP dinners, executive roundtables, experiences and other gatherings.
    • Should they host something around a major conference? Which city makes sense? What audience should they bring together? Dinner or roundtable? Who should speak? What would make the conversation compelling? When should planning begin?
    • You won't need to know all the answers on day one. You'll learn from an experienced team that produces hundreds of events and experiences each year and gradually develop the judgment to become a trusted advisor yourself.
    • Over time, we want clients calling you not simply to ask "Where does my event stand?" but "What do you think we should do next?"
  • Be the Quarterback
    • Great client service requires great execution.
    • You'll sit between the client and Landmark's teams and help keep everyone moving in the same direction.
    • You'll coordinate with colleagues across event production, venues, programming, attendee recruitment, marketing, creative and leadership. You'll translate client conversations into clear actions, owners and deadlines and make sure commitments don't disappear between meetings
    • Depending on the engagement, that might mean helping to:
      • Build and maintain an event calendar or account plan
      • Prepare agendas, meeting briefs and client updates
      • Coordinate event concepts, dates, markets and venues
      • Develop speaker guides, briefing documents and talking points
      • Coordinate speaker outreach and preparation
      • Review invitation strategies and target attendee profiles
      • Work with our recruitment team on priority executives and attendee outreach
      • Gather client materials, branding, biographies, headshots and content
      • Prepare clients for their upcoming dinners and experiences
      • Track decisions, deliverables and outstanding questions
      • Support clients on-site when appropriate
      • Capture follow-up and help turn a successful event into meaningful next steps
    • You are not the event producer responsible for personally executing every detail.
    • You are the person who understands the client, understands the engagement, knows where things stand, anticipates what's coming and brings together the right people to make it happen.
  • Grow the Relationship
    • Client Success at Landmark isn't just about delivering what was sold.
    • It's about understanding what our clients are trying to accomplish and continually finding ways to create more value.
    • You'll learn their broader calendars, markets, audiences and priorities. You'll notice when a successful New York dinner could become Chicago and San Francisco. When an intimate executive gathering could become a larger program. When a client has another objective Landmark may be uniquely positioned to help solve.
    • You'll work alongside senior relationship owners to develop ideas, proposals, renewals and expanded engagements.
    • We are looking for someone with commercial curiosity – someone who understands that exceptional client service creates trust, trust creates opportunity and successful relationships grow.
  • Make It Better
    • We're building this function as we grow.
    • You'll help us continuously improve how Landmark manages client relationships – how we prepare for meetings, organize account information, communicate with clients, track calendars, capture institutional knowledge and move from one successful engagement to a broader relationship.
    • You'll also be encouraged to use AI, automation and modern tools to make our work smarter and our client experience better.
    • If there's a better way to do something, we want you to find it.

Who You Are

  • You're a relationship person and a details person.
  • That's an unusual combination, and it's the heart of this role.
  • You can comfortably join a call with a senior executive and represent Landmark well, then spend the next hour making sure every commitment from that conversation has an owner and a deadline.
  • You're warm without being overly casual. Polished without being corporate. Organized without being rigid. Commercial without being salesy.
  • You communicate exceptionally well and know how to turn a complicated conversation into a simple set of next steps.
  • You're curious. You want to understand the client's business and why they're hosting the dinner – not simply what time it starts.
  • You're proactive. If something doesn't look right, you ask. If a deadline is approaching, you don't wait to be reminded. If you see an opportunity, you raise it.
  • And you have exceptional follow-through.
  • You don't just write down the action item. You make sure it gets done.

What You Bring

  • We're less interested in finding someone with a perfect background than someone with the right combination of judgment, relationship skills and drive.
  • You likely bring 3-5 years of experience in client success, account management, experiential marketing, events, hospitality, consulting, partnerships or another high-touch client environment.
  • You should be an exceptional communicator, highly organized and comfortable managing multiple clients and engagements simultaneously. You should have the judgment and confidence to interact with senior executives while remaining willing to roll up your sleeves and handle detailed work.
  • Experience working with B2B technology companies, executive audiences, events or experiential programs is valuable, but not required.
  • You should also be comfortable with presentations, spreadsheets, CRM systems and modern productivity tools, and curious about how AI can make you better at your job.
  • Above all, we're looking for someone who is thoughtful, resourceful, dependable, low-ego and hungry to grow.

Why Landmark

Landmark sits at an unusual intersection of relationships, innovation and execution.

For more than 25 years, we've helped extraordinary founders, brands and enterprises reach new customers, enter new markets, build strategic relationships, accelerate pipelines, create extraordinary events and experiences, execute M&A transactions, raise capital and unlock new opportunities.

Our Events & Experiences team produces more than 200 gatherings each year – from intimate VIP dinners and executive roundtables to industry summits, conferences and bespoke experiences.

You'll work directly with leading companies and senior executives while learning from a team that has spent years building relationships and bringing extraordinary people together.

You'll also have room to grow.

Success in this role can mean managing larger and more strategic client relationships, developing deeper expertise in executive experiences, taking on commercial responsibility and becoming an increasingly important part of Landmark's client leadership.

We want this to be a place where talented people can build careers, not simply do jobs.

The Details

Our headquarters is located in New York City and we primarily work in the Eastern Time Zone. But we will happily consider exceptional candidates working remotely within the United States or Europe.

Because events happen when events happen, this role requires flexibility, occasional travel and some work outside traditional business hours.

Candidates must be authorized for employment in the United States.

Compensation will be based on qualifications and experience, and Landmark offers a competitive benefits package.

  • Execute technically sound templates and motion production-ready graphics that scale across a variety of digital platforms and event applications.

  • Work closely with the creative, brand, paid and social media teams to understand audience segments and performance data, translating insights into full funnel visual concepts that support performance marketing initiatives.
  • Stay current with design, social media, video and motion graphics trends.
  • Share knowledge of AI tools and apply best practices to improve creative quality, efficiency, and speed to market.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • An accredited degree in Graphic Design, Visual Communications, Fine Arts, or a related field; or 8+ years of professional design experience supported by a strong portfolio demonstrating skill requirements.
  • Professional experience in graphic design, and creating for motion and video.
  • Advanced proficiency in design, photography, and creative software, including Canva and Adobe Creative Cloud applications such as Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, Adobe Express, Bridge and Lightroom. Ability to design in Microsoft Office suite such as Powerpoint and Word on a macintosh platform.
  • Intermediate proficiency in motion graphics software, including Canva, Adobe Express, After Effects and similar tools.
  • A strong portfolio demonstrating exceptional design concepts, strong typography, short form motion and video creative work across social media, paid media, digital, web, and performance marketing.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively with diverse teams in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet competing deadlines.
  • A team-oriented, adaptable mindset with a willingness to contribute across graphic design, video, and motion graphics projects as needed.
  • Demonstrate understanding of AI in the creative process, using AI tools daily to explore concepts, generate iterations, and support final production.
  • Experience with tools such as Google Flow, Gemini, Claude, ElevenLabs, ChatGPT, CapCut Pro, or similar platforms.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Advanced knowledge of design and user experience principles, image optimization applied to digital, event and motion graphics best practices.
  • Fundamental video editing and production experience using After Effects and related motion graphic tools to create short form content.

Bonus:

  • Prior experience building interactive spaces in web platforms like Foleon, Instapage or Ceros
  • Figma or Adobe XD knowledge
  • Agency experience

Working Conditions & Hiring Process

  • U.S. Work Location Requirement: All employees must reside and perform work within the United States. International remote work arrangements are not supported for this role.
  • Travel Expectations: This is a remote position, though occasional travel may be required for team meetings, company events, conferences, summits, and similar activities. Candidates must be willing and able to travel as needed.
  • On-Camera Work Environment: Penn Foster Group operates in a highly collaborative, remote, on-camera culture. Employees are expected to be on camera during meetings unless extenuating circumstances apply.
  • Recorded Video Interviews: Video interviews conducted during the hiring process will be recorded to support internal hiring consistency and process improvement.
  • Background Checks: Employment with Penn Foster Group is contingent upon successfully completing applicable pre-employment screening requirements. These may include verification of employment history, education, and criminal background, where permitted by law.
  • Identity Verification (Form I-9): As part of the onboarding process, all hires must complete employment eligibility verification in compliance with federal law. This includes remote Form I-9 verification, which may require an in-person identity verification step with an authorized representative.

About Us:

At Penn Foster Group, we are transforming online learning to help learners by uniting Penn Foster, CareerStep, Ashworth College, James Madison High School, the New York Institute of Photography, the New York Institute of Art and Design, and other education platforms. Together, we create an accelerated path to greater economic mobility through real-world skills and knowledge that enable them to achieve long-term success in the workplaces of the future. Our history dates back to 1890 when our founder, Thomas Foster, pioneered distance education by offering training by mail for coal miners to get the necessary skills for safer jobs. Today, with the partners who use our education and training programs, we continue that mission of providing accessible training and education for in-demand skills and are building a workforce that’s prepared for the future job market.

Equal Employment Opportunity:

We strive toward Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion at Penn Foster Group by intentionally building teams that are diverse – in identities, lived experiences, and ideas to create a culture where people feel connected to each other and have a sense of belonging. We value diversity, equity, and inclusion because it is the foundation that enables us to achieve what we set out to do as an organization – from maximizing the number of learners who can reach their goals while giving them the kinds of experiences we want them to have, to becoming the type of company we want to work in.

What We Offer:

We offer a robust benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, flexible spending, generous paid time off, sponsored volunteer opportunities, a 401K with a company match, plus free access to all of our online programs.

title: Program Manager, Release & Delivery  | ELN Platform
description:
Our Why At Dotmatics

At Dotmatics, a Siemens company, we believe science, data, and decision-making must be deeply intertwined for innovation to thrive. Our Portfolio includes Luma, LumaLab Connect, ELN Platform, Graphpad Prism, Geneious, SnapGene, Protein Metrics, OMIQ, FCS Express, LabArchives, NQuery, EasyPanel, SoftGenetics and Virscidian.

We have a vision for a new Lab of the Future that will change the future of scientific research.

We have created the world’s most comprehensive digital science platform – best-of-breed software applications already used by more than 2 million scientists, together in a single ecosystem united by a powerful, flexible enterprise data platform. This is not flat data buried away in digital graveyards. This is dynamic, multi-dimensional decision-making.

Scientific enterprises need a new level of effectiveness to achieve tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Illness will not wait. The biosphere will not wait. We are tireless in our vision, because the time for innovation is now.

Shaping the Future of Science At Dotmatics

Our global team of more than 800 colleagues are dedicated to supporting our customers in over 180 countries. Together, with our scientific community of users, we accelerate scientific innovation in order to make the world a healthier, cleaner, and safer place to live.

You’ll join a collaborative, global team pushing the boundaries of scientific innovation. Your ideas and efforts will have a tangible impact, accelerating scientific progress and discovery. We offer a dynamic, remote-friendly environment that fosters high integrity and collaboration, empowering you to excel. Dotmatics is a company built by scientists, for scientists. Combined, we are now the world’s largest cloud-based scientific research R&D platform. We need your help to keep growing and pioneering the future.

We are Science Driven. We are Customer Centric. We are Better Together.

What do we need

We are looking for a Program Manager to lead our release management and broader program delivery for the Dotmatics ELN Platform. This is a high-impact role that combines hands-on release execution with strategic program oversight, sitting at the intersection of planning, delivery, and cross-functional alignment. You will have the opportunity to have real influence over how program and release management operate across the business, gaining broad visibility across the organization, working with and presenting to stakeholders from engineering teams through to executive leadership, and supporting notable impact.

You will bring the operational precision of a release manager alongside the governance and rigor of a program manager, ensuring that releases are delivered with quality and consistency and that the wider program of work is well-planned with dependencies clearly visible. You will work closely with Engineering, Product Management, Quality Assurance, Customer Operations, Services, Marketing, and Sales, operating as a trusted collaborative and strategic partner with a clear, decisive voice across all stages of delivery.

In this role you will get to

Release Management

  • Own the end-to-end release management process. Refine, lead, and continuously improve practices that deliver high-quality, timely releases. Champion a release culture aligned to business and customer objectives, and actively replace practices that do not serve those goals
  • Lead a core group of representatives from Product Management, Engineering, Quality Assurance, and Customer Operations through the release process from planning to external release, ensuring capacity and risk are part of the equation
  • Track, monitor, and drive execution of release plans with pace and accountability. Escalate and hold others accountable when needed
  • Define and maintain a clear release calendar. Provide timely updates on release readiness, risk, and post-release adoption metrics across all relevant audiences
  • Lead coordination of in-flight work across Jira (our system of record). Identify and mitigate release risk, flagging unrealistic plans early and ensuring alignment with Product Management and Services to support escalations and customer-specific builds
  • Align release artifacts across Product, Engineering, Marketing (including tier 1 and tier 2 launches), Sales (enablement), and Services (training)
  • Lead cross-functional release meetings and asynchronous processes as the definitive voice driving the holistic release process forward

Program Management

  • Lead program-level planning and governance across the ELN Platform. Manage dependencies, milestones, and delivery roadmaps across multiple concurrent workstreams
  • Translate company and customer objectives into a clear execution strategy. Ensure teams understand priorities and how their work connects to broader business goals
  • Identify, track, and mitigate program-level risks and issues early. Escalate where needed and hold stakeholders accountable for resolution
  • Provide regular, audience-appropriate reporting to stakeholders from engineering teams through to executive leadership. Cover progress, risk, and strategic alignment
  • Support the rollout of Solution Area Initiatives. Play an active role in embedding this new operational model across the company as it is defined and scaled
  • Build and maintain strong relationships across functions. Practice influence without authority and drive alignment across a wide range of internal and external stakeholders

Ways of Working

  • Champion agile delivery across the release and process. Align with and actively influence agile methodology to support effective product and engineering execution
  • Enable and coach product and engineering teams. Listen to day-to-day challenges and incorporate their input into how the teams plan and deliver
  • Apply a growth mindset. Embrace operational improvements and lead collaborative processes where team members feel heard and empowered

We are looking for people who have 10 + years of experience in program management and/or enterprise SaaS product release management. Agile SCRUM, Product Owner, SCRUM Master, or PMP certification is strongly preferred.

The keys skills we are looking for

  • Proven track record of leading and executing release and program management strategies through agile leadership, cross-functional collaboration, and proactive follow-through
  • Strong program governance skills, including milestone planning, dependency management, risk tracking, and executive-level reporting
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, clear and consistent across all audiences and deliverables, from engineers to executive stakeholders
  • Ability to bring structure and calm to a fast-paced environment with competing priorities across multiple workstreams
  • Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills across functions and seniority levels, internally and externally
  • Advanced Jira and Confluence skills, including creating and maintaining custom reports, dashboards, and program views
  • Proficiency in diagramming and planning tools such as Visio, Lucidchart, or Miro
  • Experience planning and executing long-term, multi-phase programs spanning development, configuration, and deployment
  • Openness to embracing how AI can improve you in your role. We are all learning how AI can help us be more efficient and collaborative, creating space for us to grow. We use Claude

Nice to have:

  • Background or relevant work experience in life sciences or scientific software
  • People management or mentorship experience

Total Rewards

Dotmatics utilises a national market-based approach to base pay benchmarking and pay band development. The candidate's final starting pay is based on job-related skills, experience, job specific qualifications & location. In addition to base salary, Dotmatics has implemented a total rewards strategy, which is the combination of compensation, benefits and recognition.

Certain positions are also eligible for variable pay; your recruiter will discuss the full compensation package details.

Other Total Rewards Offered

  • Private Medical
  • Wellness Benefits (Mental Health Apps and Fitness Perks)
  • Company-paid Life cover
  • EAP (Employee Assistance Program)
  • Pension/Retirement Plan

This is the range that we, in good faith, believe is the range of possible compensation for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range. This range may be modified in the future.

Base Pay Range
£66,104—£89,435 GBP

Research shows us the confidence gap and imposter syndrome can get in the way of meeting outstanding candidates, so please don’t hesitate to apply — we’d love to hear from you.

By submitting your application, you agree that Dotmatics may collect your personal data for recruiting, global organization planning, and related purposes. Dotmatics Privacy Notice explains what personal information we may process, where we may process your personal information, our purposes for processing your personal information, and the rights you can exercise over Dotmatics use of your personal information.

Dotmatics is an equal opportunity employer. We are a welcoming place for everyone, and we do our best to make sure all people feel supported and connected at work.

title: SAP Front-end Developer
description:
Bright Vision Technologies is a forward-thinking software development company dedicated to building innovative solutions that help businesses automate and optimize their operations. We leverage cutting-edge technologies to create scalable, secure, and user-friendly applications.

As we continue to grow, we’re looking for a skilled SAP Front-end Developer to join our dynamic team and contribute to our mission of transforming business processes through technology.

This is a fantastic opportunity to join an established and well-respected organization offering tremendous career growth potential.

Job Title: SAP Front-end Developer
Location: 100% Remote (Continental United States)
Position Type: In-house Bright Vision Technologies SOW engagement (no third-party client or vendor)
Salary: $130K- $180K
Experience: 5+ years

Employment Terms & Visa Policy
This is a 100% remote, full-time, direct W2 position with Bright Vision Technologies.
This role is part of Bright Vision Technologies’ in-house Statement of Work (SOW) engagement. The client, end customer, and employer for this position is Bright Vision Technologies — there is no third-party client, vendor, or implementation partner involved.
We do not engage in C2C, 1099, or third-party arrangements for this role.

Candidates must be willing to work directly as a full-time W2 employee of Bright Vision Technologies and contribute to our in-house SOW deliverables.
No new H1B sponsorship is available for this role.

However, candidates who are currently on a valid H1B visa and require a transfer are welcome to apply. We will support H1B transfers for qualified candidates.
For every role, a technical coding assessment is mandatory. Please apply only if you are confident in your technical abilities and hands-on experience.

Job Summary
We are seeking an experienced SAP Front-end Developer to design, build, and enhance modern, user-friendly SAP applications that meet enterprise standards for usability, performance, and maintainability. In this role you will own the full Fiori/UI5 development lifecycle, working closely with functional consultants, ABAP developers, and UX teams to deliver responsive Fiori applications across desktop, tablet, and mobile devices. The ideal candidate will combine deep expertise in SAPUI5, Fiori elements, and OData with a strong sense of UX, accessibility, and clean-architecture principles, and will adhere to SAP Fiori Design Guidelines while delivering business value through well-designed user experiences.

Key Responsibilities
  • Design and develop SAP Fiori applications using SAPUI5, Fiori elements, and the Fiori Launchpad, ensuring adherence to SAP Fiori Design Guidelines.
  • Build and consume OData v2/v4 services, including model definitions, navigation properties, expansions, and batch operations.
  • Implement custom controls, formatters, fragments, and reusable components in line with internal coding standards.
  • Develop role-based Fiori Launchpad configurations, including catalogs, groups, tiles, and target mappings.
  • Optimize Fiori applications for performance, including bundling, caching, lazy loading, and reduction of network round trips.
  • Build adaptive applications using flexibility services and key-user adaptation features of S/4HANA.
  • Implement strong authentication and authorization patterns aligned with SAP security guidelines.
  • Integrate Fiori applications with SAP BTP services, including XSUAA, Workflow, and Document Service.
  • Support deployment of Fiori applications to both ABAP frontend servers and BTP-hosted runtimes.
  • Collaborate closely with ABAP developers to define backend OData services and CDS views that support efficient Fiori applications.
  • Conduct thorough functional, regression, and cross-device/cross-browser testing of applications, including edge-case validation and accessibility checks, to ensure consistent user experience across the supported platform matrix.
  • Provide hypercare and post-go-live support, including issue triage, performance tuning, and continuous improvement.
  • Maintain comprehensive, current technical documentation — including architecture diagrams, design decisions, configuration references, runbooks, and operational procedures — so that the system remains supportable, auditable, and easy to onboard new engineers onto over time.

Required Qualifications
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • Five or more years of SAP Fiori / UI5 development experience.
  • Strong hands-on experience with SAPUI5, Fiori elements, and the Fiori Launchpad.
  • Solid experience with OData v2/v4 modeling and consumption.
  • Hands-on experience with HTML5, JavaScript (ES6+), and CSS.
  • Working knowledge of ABAP CDS views, BOPF, and gateway service development.
  • Experience deploying Fiori applications to ABAP frontend and BTP runtimes.
  • Strong understanding of authentication, authorization, and SAP security patterns.
  • Excellent attention to UX, accessibility, and performance.
  • Strong communication and documentation skills.
Preferred Qualifications
  • SAP certifications in Fiori / UI5 development.
  • Hands-on experience with SAP Build Apps / Low-Code platforms.
  • Experience with SAP Mobile Services or hybrid mobile applications.
  • Familiarity with CI/CD tooling for SAPUI5 (Project Piper, GitHub Actions).
  • Exposure to TypeScript-based UI5 development.
How to Apply

For immediate consideration, please send your resume to or contact us at (908) 505-3544. Learn more about Bright Vision Technologies at www.bvteck.com.

title: Head of HR
description:
WHO ARE WE?

Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company. We reach tens of millions of people every month through our brands, including FinanceBuzz, All About Cookies, and OnlyInYourState. We turn that attention into real outcomes for our partners, some of the world's leading companies.

Our mission: create predictable, high-value customer acquisition at scale by connecting discovery, intent, and performance across category-leading consumer brands in finance, travel, and entertainment.

We run profitable and bootstrapped, with a South Florida HQ and a remote-first team across 18 countries.

WHY JOIN US?

You own outcomes here, not tasks. We measure work by impact, not activity. The pace is real, and change is constant, so the people who do best turn change into opportunity instead of waiting for it to settle. Feedback runs direct and lands with respect. Ordinary people make themselves extraordinary at Launch Potato.

Base salary: $170,000 to $190,000. Plus an annual bonus paid as a flat amount rather than a percentage of base.

Launch Potato is about 200 people, profitable, and growing. The performance management system that got us here was built by our SVP of Talent, and he still runs it. That system becomes yours.

You're inheriting something that works. There's a levels framework, a rating scale, a calibration process, and managers who have been through several cycles. It got us to 200 people. Your job is deciding what carries forward and change-managing the rest, across an org that moves fast and adopts new processes.

We want someone who'll find the version that works and then hold it there while the company gets good at it.

If you want to own a function, make it extraordinary, and be judged on whether it actually got better, keep reading.

Why This Seat

  • Real ownership, immediately. Performance, total rewards, and compliance are yours to own rather than support. You'll defend a compensation number in front of a CFO who checks it.
  • An SVP who wants to hand this over. Not one who says that and then rewrites your deck. The explicit goal is that the HR function runs without him.
  • Executive reach by default. Calibration and leveling decisions live with the C-suite, and you present your own work. You won't spend year one convincing anyone that performance management matters.
  • Leverage is part of the mandate, not a side project. We are tech-first and AI-forward, which means we can run lean teams and do more with less. You'll push that further, build the tooling managers actually open, and make everything easier without taking substance out of it. Nobody will ask you to do it the slow way.

How This Team Is Led

From Kris Osborne, SVP of Talent.

I'll tell you what I want and what the constraints are and then get out of the way. I don't rewrite people's work. If I disagree with where you landed you'll hear it from me early, and if you still think you're right then push back, because I'd rather change my mind than have you go quiet and build something you don't believe in.

I ask before I decide. When something changes the shape of this team the people on it hear it from me first and they get a real say in it, not a heads up after it's done.

I care about the outcome and I'm not going to do your job for you. Bring me a problem and I'll work it with you, but I'm not going to take it off your plate and hand it back finished.

I'm hiring this seat because I want someone we can all learn from. Bring me a better answer than mine and I'll take it.

What You'll Bring

All required.

  • A full performance cycle you owned end to end, not supported. Owned more than once, at 150 people or more. Design, timeline, manager prep, calibration, rollout, retro.
  • Compensation and benefits you've owned. Band design, benchmarking methodology, benefits renewals, the annual comp cycle. You can defend a number to a CFO.
  • HR compliance as standing scope, not as a project. Multi-state registration, I-9, handbook, classification, postings. You've inherited a backlog and cleared it.
  • A people system that outlasted you. Built, adopted, and still recognizable two cycles later.
  • Leverage you built that people adopted. You've automated or rebuilt part of a people process so it ran faster, the quality held or improved, and the team actually used it. Adoption is the test here, the same way durability is the test above.
  • Experience taking a company our size to materially larger, on headcount or revenue, more than once. You know what breaks first at the next stage because you've watched it break.
  • Empowered your team to raise the bar. You have clear examples of coaching, mentoring, and growing a team that created extraordinary outcomes.

This is a player-coach seat. Managers here lead a team and deliver work personally, at every level.

Nice to Have

  • You have opinions about what performance management gets wrong, and specific examples of what you changed
  • You can tell a process problem from a manager-capability problem, and you fix the right one
  • You're the person who says the uncomfortable thing in a calibration room

What You'll Own

Performance management. The mid-year and annual cycles end to end: design, timeline, communication, execution. What the cycle needs to produce and what to cut. A timeline published early enough that managers plan around it. The retro after each one, and the judgment about when a change is warranted and when to leave it alone.

Total rewards. Band design and the benchmarking methodology behind it. Benefits renewals and the economics underneath them. The annual comp cycle, with leveling and pay kept connected.

Compliance. Multi-state registration, I-9, handbook, classification, postings. The current backlog, plus the escalation and coverage protocols that follow it.

Manager enablement. Preparing managers for real performance conversations, including the one where someone rated themselves higher than their manager did. The calibration process, including where two managers apply the same bar differently. Playbooks and self-service resources so a manager gets an answer without booking a meeting. Standing support for the roughly three dozen front-line managers who get it reactively today.

Leverage and tooling. Finding the parts of everything above that shouldn't be done by hand, and fixing them. Building what a manager will actually open rather than what looks good in a demo. Taking time out of the cycle while the conversations get better rather than thinner.

The team. An HR Business Partner and a Total Rewards and People Analytics lead. Both are strong at what they do and both have room to grow. You set their decision rights: where they decide, where they recommend, where it comes to you.

What Great Looks Like

In your first year:

  • The annual cycle ships on your timeline and you own it
  • Managers are calibrated before the cycle rather than corrected after it
  • Every person leaving a check-in has one clear thing to work on, and the conversation that produced it was a real one
  • The compliance backlog is closed and stays closed
  • The cycle costs managers less time than the year before, and the conversations are better rather than thinner
  • Your two reports hold more decision authority than they did at the start

This Isn't the Right Seat If

  • This would be your first Director-level people role
  • You lead with policy and risk. Compliance is required here and it isn't the center of the work
  • You want to redesign the cycle every year
  • You see tooling and automation as somebody else's job
  • You're looking for a recruiting role. Recruiting sits elsewhere in the function

Want to accelerate your career? Apply now!

We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

description:
About Sezzle:

With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with a wide range of flexible payment options designed to give customers more choice, accessibility, and a smarter overall experience. We're not just transforming payments; we're redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we're building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you're excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping!

About the Role:

We are seeking a curious, driven, and thoughtful Product Intern to join our Payments & Fees team. This role presents an exciting opportunity to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment within a growing team, with abundant prospects for career advancement.

If you want to truly understand how fintech works, there's no better place to start than payments — and no better seat than product. The Payments & Fees team sits at the intersection of technology, data, and business, working with payment processors, payment method providers, and cross-functional partners across the company. As a product intern here, you won't be watching from the sidelines. You'll be in the room (or the channel) where decisions get made, picking up context fast and contributing to a team that moves quickly and takes its craft seriously.

You'll support the product manager across a high-throughput environment: helping keep the backlog organized, digging into data to understand payment flows, and working alongside an efficient and technically sharp engineering team, as well as Design and Data teams. Product management is one of those rare roles where no two days look the same — you're constantly context-switching between technical conversations, business problems, and user needs, and that's exactly what makes it exciting.

What You'll Do:

Ticket Management & Product Support

  • Assist the product manager in drafting, organizing, and tracking tickets for changes and improvements to the payments service. Help ensure work is well-documented, properly prioritized, and moving through the backlog. Follow up on status and surface blockers when needed.

Context Gathering & Stakeholder Support

  • Help the product manager stay on top of inputs from multiple stakeholders by gathering background context, summarizing key information, and preparing materials ahead of provider meetings. Respond to routine internal questions by pulling the right information from available resources.

Payment Workflow Analysis

  • Learn and apply SQL to query payment data and support the creation and maintenance of dashboards that track payment performance, processing failures, and operational health. Help flag anomalies in payment flows and assist in assembling data for reviews and investigations.

Documentation & Process Tracking

  • Maintain clear internal documentation for payment flows, fee structures, and operational processes. Help keep cross-functional teams aligned with concise, well-structured written updates.

Agile Meetings

  • Participate in agile meetings and collaborate with engineering, operations, compliance, and support teams. One of the most valuable things a product manager does is serve as a bridge between tech and the business — translating technical challenges into clear language and business needs into actionable requirements. You'll get hands-on experience doing exactly that.

What We Look For:

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Business, Computer Science, Economics, Finance, or a related field
  • A genuine interest in payments, fintech, and how complex financial systems work under the hood
  • Natural curiosity and a logical mindset — you enjoy working through problems, aren't afraid to ask questions, and get satisfaction from figuring things out
  • Strong attention to detail — you notice when something's off and follow through until it's resolved
  • Comfort working with data and a willingness to learn SQL; prior experience is a plus but not required
  • Effective written and verbal communication — you can summarize a complex topic clearly and ask the right questions to fill in gaps
  • Prior experience in internships, projects, or extracurriculars related to product, fintech, data analysis, or startups is a plus — but we hire for potential, not just pedigree.
  • Demonstrated experience working with Claude or equivalent large language model tools is required; candidates must be comfortable leveraging AI to enhance productivity, research, and communication.

About You:

  • You have relentlessly high standards — many people may think your standards are unreasonably high. You are continually raising the bar and driving those around you to deliver great results. You make sure that defects do not get sent down the line and that problems are fixed so they stay fixed.
  • You're not bound by convention — your success and much of the fun lies in developing new ways to do things.
  • You need action — speed matters in business. Many decisions and actions are reversible and do not need extensive study. We value calculated risk-taking.
  • You earn trust — you listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully.
  • You have backbone; disagree, then commit — you can respectfully challenge decisions when you disagree, even when doing so is uncomfortable or exhausting. You have conviction and are tenacious. You do not compromise for the sake of social cohesion. Once a decision is determined, you commit wholly.
  • You deliver results — you focus on the key inputs and deliver them with the right quality and in a timely fashion. Despite setbacks, you rise to the occasion and never settle.

What Makes Working at Sezzle Awesome:

At Sezzle, we are more than just brilliant engineers, passionate data enthusiasts, out-of-the-box thinkers, and determined innovators. We believe in surrounding ourselves with only the best and the brightest individuals. Our culture is not defined by a certain set of perks designed to give the illusion of the traditional startup culture, but rather, it is the visible example living in every employee that we hire.

Compensation: The salary for the Product Intern is $800 USD Gross as an independent contractor.

This internship is designed to develop the next generation of technology professionals through direct exposure to enterprise application development, agile methodologies, software design, and modern engineering practices.


As a member of the software engineering team, the intern will work closely with developers, architects, business analysts, product owners, and scrum team members to support the design, development, testing, and delivery of business-critical applications. title: SEO and Web Dev Specialist
description:
SEO and Web Dev Specialist

Role Overview

We are looking for an SEO Specialist with hands-on Web Development skills to improve organic visibility, website traffic, and qualified lead generation. This role is primarily focused on SEO, with the remaining time dedicated to website design and development. Responsibilities include keyword research, on-page and technical SEO, writing SEO-optimized copy, designing page layouts, and building and optimizing landing pages using WordPress, Elementor, and/or Oxygen. The ideal candidate can independently manage SEO initiatives while translating those strategies into functional, well-structured, and conversion-focused web pages, using tools such as SEMrush, Screaming Frog, AccuRanker, and BrightLocal.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute SEO strategies aligned with business goals, focusing on organic visibility, traffic, and qualified lead generation.

  • Conduct keyword research and map target keywords to landing pages and website content.

  • Write SEO-optimized copy, design page layouts, and develop high-performing landing pages using WordPress, Elementor, and/or Oxygen.

  • Implement on-page SEO best practices, including metadata, headings, URL structure, internal linking, and content optimization.

  • Conduct technical SEO audits to identify and resolve issues related to crawlability, indexation, site structure, and website performance.

  • Use SEMrush, Screaming Frog, AccuRanker, and BrightLocal to monitor rankings, identify opportunities, and track local and organic SEO performance.

  • Optimize existing web pages and content to improve search visibility, user experience, and conversion rates.

  • Monitor SEO performance through analytics and reporting, identifying actionable opportunities to increase organic traffic and qualified leads.

  • Stay up to date with search engine algorithm updates, SEO trends, and industry best practices.

Requirements

  • 2–3 years of hands-on SEO experience, preferably in an agency or in-house environment.

  • Strong understanding of on-page SEO, keyword research, search engine ranking factors, and technical SEO fundamentals.

  • Experience writing SEO-optimized copy, designing page layouts, and developing landing pages.

  • Hands-on experience with WordPress and page builders such as Elementor and/or Oxygen.

  • Proficiency with SEMrush, Screaming Frog, AccuRanker, and BrightLocal.

  • Experience optimizing website content, metadata, internal linking, and page structure.

  • Basic understanding of HTML/CSS and website architecture.

  • Understanding of website performance, crawlability, indexation, and mobile optimization.

  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interpret SEO data and recommend actionable improvements.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple projects, prioritize tasks, and meet deadlines.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with content strategy, copywriting, or blog management.

  • Familiarity with marketing automation and CRM tools.

  • Experience optimizing websites for multiple markets or languages.

  • Knowledge of link-building strategies and local SEO best practices.

KPIs

  • Organic traffic growth.

  • Growth in non-branded keyword rankings.

  • Organic leads and goal completions.

  • Technical SEO health, including crawl errors, Core Web Vitals, and indexation.

  • Landing page performance and organic conversion rates.

Contractor Perks

  • Work with international clients while maintaining your independent contractor status.

  • Minimum 5 paid days off annually, plus US holidays.

  • Free access to career growth learning modules through Hyre Academy.

  • Scheduled rate increases based on applicable contract terms and performance.

title: Bilingual (Spanish/English) Transitions of Care Advanced Practice Provider
description:
Job Description

Schedule

This is a full-time, 5-day, 8-hour position (8:30 AM – 5:00 PM CST/MST/PST). Candidates must be able to consistently work within Central (CST), Mountain (MST), or Pacific (PST) time zone hours.

A bit about this role

Our Devoted Medical Transitions of Care (TOC) Advanced Practice Provider (APP) roles include both Nurse Practitioners (APRNs) and Physician Assistants (PAs) — candidates for both will be considered. This is an opportunity for an experienced APP to help build the TOC Program. The TOC program provides virtual care during the 30-day window after a patient is discharged from a hospitalization. Our goal is to prevent readmissions by delivering exceptional, comprehensive, wrap-around care during this high-risk period. The team is highly interdisciplinary — care coordinators, nurse case managers, social workers, APPs, and physicians collaborating together.

This role demands two distinct skill sets in one provider. Roughly 70% of your time is spent on comprehensive initial post-discharge visits, and 30% on follow-up and acute/urgent symptom visits. That means you need the acute clinical judgment to recognize and manage a decompensating, medically complex patient in real time, and the longitudinal depth to build and adjust a whole-person, complex chronic-care plan over 30 days. You should be equally comfortable deciding whether a patient needs an immediate intervention today and managing the slower arc of their chronic disease across the continuum. You'll also help build the program itself — shaping team culture, fostering safe and open communication, contributing to quality-improvement work, and giving feedback on our homegrown EHR as we grow.

Responsibilities and impact will include:

  • Perform comprehensive initial TOC visits. Conduct a thorough post-discharge assessment of the patient's medical conditions, medications, functional status, and psychosocial needs. Complete a full post-discharge medication reconciliation — including identifying duplicate, inappropriate, or contraindicated therapy and optimizing guideline-directed medical therapy. Place appropriate orders (prescriptions, labs, imaging, referrals, home health, DME), provide disease-specific education, and communicate clear contingency plans and red flags for worsening symptoms.

  • Perform acute / virtual urgent-care TOC visits. Independently assess, diagnose, and manage new or worsening symptoms in medically complex patients, determine the appropriate level of care, and escalate when needed — with a clear bias to action.

  • Manage the clinical trajectory across the 30-day window. Reinforce and adjust each patient's plan of care in response to their evolving clinical picture, their priorities, and the barriers they face — including chronic disease management, symptom management, and timely changes to the medical regimen.

  • Participate in interdisciplinary TOC rounds to discuss patients at highest risk of readmission, and collaborate closely with RN case managers, care coordinators, social work case managers, pharmacy, and patients' PCPs and specialists.

  • Enhance team culture by facilitating safe, open communication across roles and supporting clear patient escalations.

  • Assist with clinical education of the broader team, participate in quality-improvement projects and pilots, and provide feedback to improve our EHR.

  • Embrace a build environment. As our service needs evolve, this role may expand to support new clinical and organizational initiatives. We seek people who are adaptable, eager to learn, and comfortable in a fast-paced, dynamic setting where change is constant.

Required skills and experience

  • 5+ years of direct patient care managing primarily geriatric populations with multiple chronic, complex, comorbid conditions — across both acute and chronic presentations.

  • Demonstrated comfort across the continuum: acute management of chronic illness and longitudinal outpatient chronic-disease management, with a strong understanding of how the two connect.

  • Strong, independent clinical decision-making and bias to action in a virtual setting — comfortable being the clinician who recognizes deterioration and decides the next best step.

  • Proficiency with complex medication reconciliation and guideline-directed medical therapy, especially for heart failure, COPD, diabetes, atrial fibrillation/anticoagulation, and hypertension — including recognizing duplicate, inappropriate, or contraindicated medications and adjusting regimens safely.

  • Comfort diagnosing, managing, and monitoring decompensating patients with common high-readmission conditions such as heart failure, COPD, diabetes, hypertension, pneumonia, cellulitis, and urinary tract infections.

  • Ability to work the full-time 5-day, 8-hour schedule (Monday-Friday 8:30 AM – 5:00 PM within CST/PST/MST hours).

  • A strong, collaborative team player who thrives in an interdisciplinary environment.

  • Proficiency in English and Spanish is required.

Desired skills and experience

  • Experience in internal medicine, hospital medicine, post-acute/SNF medicine, urgent care or emergency medicine, geriatrics, palliative care, and/or primary care with a strong chronic disease management focus.

  • Experience managing acute and chronic disease exacerbations, including CHF exacerbations, COPD exacerbations, diabetic emergencies, and hypertensive emergencies, and identifying the need for immediate intervention.

  • Experience performing visits over telehealth video platforms.

  • Experience working with frail, complex, or vulnerable populations, including in the skilled nursing facility (SNF) setting.

  • A continuous-improvement mentality, can-do attitude, and the ability to adapt quickly to new workflows and changes.

Licensure and certification

  • For Nurse Practitioners: active and in-good-standing RN and APRN licenses.

  • For Physician Assistants: an active and in-good-standing Physician Assistant license.

  • Licensure and good standing required in existing or future Devoted states; able and willing to obtain required state licenses within 60-90 days of hire. We are

  • Licensure in FL TX AZ OH and/or GA required to start.

Salary Range:$120,000-$150,000/year plus performance based bonus paid out quarterly or annually ($10K-$20K) for a total comp range of $130,000-$170,000/year.

Employer-sponsored health insurance and dental and vision plan with low or no premium

Responsibilities 🤓

  • Design, run, and analyze A/B tests and multivariate experiments (sample size and power calculations, randomization, guardrail metrics, interpretation of results).
  • Apply causal inference techniques (Difference-in-Differences, Synthetic Control, Propensity Score Matching, Instrumental Variables, Regression Discontinuity, uplift modeling) to estimate the impact of marketing campaigns, promotions, pricing, and loyalty initiatives when randomization is not possible.
  • Measure and optimize marketing performance: incrementality, attribution, ROI/ROAS, customer lifetime value (CLV), and marketing mix modeling (MMM).
  • Translate business questions from growth and marketing teams into well-defined analytical problems and experimental designs.
  • Develop analyses, features, and models on Databricks (notebooks, Spark, Delta Lake), collaborating with Data Engineers and Analytics Engineers on data pipelines and analytical datasets.

About this Role:

The Medical Device Software Quality Engineer reports to the Quality and Regulatory Affairs Manager, supporting software quality for medical device product development, day-to-day Quality Management System (QMS) operations to ISO 13485:2016 and MDSAP requirements, and assisting with regulatory compliance activities for medical software (including AI-assisted diagnostic tools) primarily in the US and Canadian markets.

Responsibilities:

Software Quality for product development

Software lifecycle & AI model governance:

  • Software Testing oversight: Own QA oversight of testing activities by reviewing and approving strategies, plans, and reports for software and AI verification and validation, ensuring adequate coverage of safety‑critical and AI‑critical functions, bias/robustness checks, and complete, audit-ready test documentation.
  • Support validation activities for software and processes: assist in the preparation of IQ/OQ/PQ documentation, test protocols and validation reports for IVD software and regulated tools used in US and Canadian GxP environments.
  • Provide QA oversight across the full software and AI model lifecycle (requirements, design, implementation, V&V, release, maintenance), ensuring robust governance of datasets, training/validation, versioning, and risk‑based change control that maintains approved clinical performance.

Risk management:

  • Lead and maintain end‑to‑end risk management for software and AI (hazard identification, analysis, control, and ongoing review), ensuring AI‑specific risks are mitigated and risk files are continuously updated using test results, post‑market data, and CAPA outputs.
  • Assist with compilation and maintenance of the design history file (DHF) and technical documentation under manager oversight, including traceability records, design inputs/outputs, and review records in line with ISO 13485 and FDA 21 CFR 820.
  • Support control of nonconforming products: document, track and follow up on nonconformances; assist with linkage between complaints, incidents, and risk management records.
  • Support labelling and instructions for use (IFU) review: check compliance of product labelling and user information with FDA and Health Canada requirements; maintain labelling records and track review status.

Quality Management System (ISO 13485 / MDSAP)

  • Maintain and update QMS documents and records under the direction of the Quality and Regulatory Affairs Manager, ensuring compliance with ISO 13485:2016 and MDSAP requirements.
  • Support document and record control processes: issue, review, revise and retire controlled documents; maintain registers and ensure version control per procedure.
  • Assist with CAPA and complaint handling: log, track and follow up on corrective actions, complaints and non-conformances; prepare records and support root cause analysis activities under manager guidance.
  • Support preparation and execution of internal audits: compile audit evidence, coordinate schedules, record findings, and track closure of audit actions under the direction of the Manager.
  • Coordinate and track QMS training: maintain training records and competency matrices; schedule and confirm delivery of QMS and role-specific training across the organisation.
  • Collect and compile quality metrics and KPI data (e.g. CAPA status, complaint trends, audit findings); prepare regular quality dashboards and summary reports for the Manager and management review inputs.
  • Support post-market surveillance (PMS) activities: collect and collate post-market data from complaint records, adverse event reports and product feedback; assist in the preparation of PMS reports for US and Canadian markets.

Supplier and process control

  • Support the supplier control process: maintain the approved supplier list; assist with supplier questionnaires, quality agreement records and incoming inspection/acceptance documentation under manager direction.

Regulatory Affairs Support

  • Support Regulatory Affairs with maintenance update to FDA establishment registration and device listing records in FURLS/GUDID; ensure listing information is current and accurate, and flag renewal deadlines to the Manager.
  • Support preparation and maintenance of Health Canada medical device licence applications and MDSAP documentation; assist with tracking licence renewal timelines and correspondence with Health Canada.
  • Assist in the preparation of global regulatory submissions to FDA, EU, UK and Health Canada (e.g. 510(k) support packages, De Novo requests, medical device licence applications): compile documentation sections, format submissions, and maintain submission trackers and correspondence records.
  • Support vigilance and post-market regulatory reporting for US and Canadian markets: track timelines for adverse event and MDR reporting (FDA 5/30-day, Health Canada); prepare draft reports for Manager review; maintain reporting records per FDA 21 CFR Part 803 and Health Canada Medical Device Regulations.

  • Experience with digital pathology systems and AI based digital pathology diagnostics is a distinct advantage
  • Good working knowledge with ISO 13485 QMS requirements or FDA 21 CFR Part 820; exposure to UK, EU, MDSAP or Health Canada medical device regulations is desirable.
  • Good working knowledge with software as a medical device (SaMD) or IVD software concepts including IEC 62304, is desirable.
  • Experience with document control, CAPA, complaint handling, or audit support processes in a regulated environment is an advantage.
  • Exposure to FDA regulatory databases (e.g. FURLS, GUDID) or Health Canada device licensing portal is desirable; willingness to learn these systems is essential.
  • Experience with eQMS or quality management software tools is an advantage.

  • Working knowledge of or willingness to develop proficiency in ISO 13485:2016 and FDA 21 CFR Part 820; ability to apply requirements to day-to-day quality operations in a software/IVD environment.
  • Basic familiarity with US FDA medical device regulatory pathways (510(k), De Novo) and Health Canada medical device licence requirements; willingness to develop working knowledge of MDSAP and applicable US/Canadian regulations.
  • Exceptional attention to detail in maintaining controlled documents, records and registers; proficiency in managing version-controlled documentation in an eQMS or equivalent system.
  • Proficiency in tracking and reporting quality metrics (e.g. CAPA closure rates, complaint volumes, audit findings); ability to build and maintain dashboards or summary reports using spreadsheet tools or quality software.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks, track deadlines and maintain accurate records simultaneously across QMS and regulatory activities.
  • Ability to communicate clearly with cross-functional teams, suppliers and the Quality and Regulatory Affairs Manager in a remote or hybrid environment.
  • Demonstrated willingness to develop technical knowledge and take on increasing responsibility within the quality and regulatory function under the guidance of the Manager.

At Step, design is one of our biggest competitive advantages.

We're looking for an experienced Visual Designer to define and evolve how Step looks and feels across every customer touchpoint. From our product and marketing campaigns to physical cards, merchandise, social media, and brand experiences, you'll own the visual identity that makes Step instantly recognizable.

This role sits at the intersection of brand, product, and marketing. You'll work closely with Product Design, Marketing, Engineering, and Leadership to ensure every interaction with Step feels cohesive, intentional, and unmistakably ours.

We're looking for someone who obsesses over typography, color, composition, illustration, motion, and craft. Someone who can zoom out to define the visual language for an entire company, then roll up their sleeves to design the details that bring it to life.

title: Head of People
description:
About Us

There are 55 million Americans over 65 living at home, and their families are anxious in ways that go far beyond "I hope mom's alright." We built a phone that works out of the box, AI check-in calls that surface how she's really doing, and a family app that replaces daily dread with peace of mind. Families tell us they used to wake up with a knot in their stomach. They don't anymore.

We are customer-obsessed to an unusual degree. When we had a major network outage, everyone, including recruiters, engineers, and marketers, got on the phone with customers. That's not a policy. It's just who we are. It is working, with tens of thousands of families trusting us.

We are looking for an executive partner on people: a peer to the co-founders who owns talent, culture and recruiting across the company. There is plenty still to build here, but this is not an HR business partner role. You will co-author, with the co-founders, who we hire, who we keep and grow, who we part ways with, and what it feels like to work here. If building the team that brings peace of mind to millions of seniors and their families is how you want to spend the next few years, we'd love to talk.

What you'll own

Hire the top 1%

  • You know what extraordinary looks like. You can explain why someone is exceptional rather than merely good, and hold every hiring manager, including the co-founders, to that bar.
  • You'll build and lead the recruiting team: at least two recruiters, one for technical and senior roles and one for high-volume customer-facing roles. Initially you run searches yourself while you build out your team. Down the line, you may be hands on recruiting for executive roles.
  • You'll grow us to about 150 to 160 people by the end of 2027, adding 12 to 20 non-rep roles and 25 to 30 reps. You'll run your recruiters to tight funnel metrics like pass-through rates and time to hire, and you'll also measure the quality of hires after they start: are the people your team hired still here and excelling a year later?
  • You'll make sure we hire the right people at the right time, not just the roles hiring managers announce they need, and that the people we hire are connected to our mission and likely to grow and succeed here.
  • You'll be well-networked and able to deliver world-class hiring, not just high-volume recruiting. You bring in people we couldn't otherwise reach, you know what sells the best people on Community Phone and what keeps them here, and you make sure every candidate hears it.

Keep extraordinary people, and only them

  • You'll be the primary voice of culture alongside the co-founders. You'll make sure everyone understands the mission, what part of the system they're in, what their work feeds into, how their performance is evaluated, and why it matters.
  • You'll make sure our most remarkable people stay: that they have the space, control and authority to do great work, that they feel pushed, capable and cared for, and that they get bigger scope before someone else offers it.
  • You'll make sure we don't keep the people we shouldn't. You'll run a talent review with every leader each quarter (who is exceptional, who is solid, who should not be here in six months), track regretted and non-regretted attrition by team, and push managers to part ways when they need to, fairly and clearly, coaching them through direct feedback, clear expectations, performance plans and well-documented exits.
  • You'll tell any leader, including the CEO, when they're hiring below the bar, protecting a weak performer, or avoiding a hard conversation.
  • You'll ensure our culture scales as we scale globally. You believe in the value of international and remote work. Our team is distributed across 12+ countries.

Build the leadership bench and the systems behind it

  • You'll partner with the executive team to build a bench of phenomenal leaders. We're building our leadership bench; your job is to make sure that in 18 months we have the leaders we need, whether we grow them or hire them.
  • You'll keep the leadership team on the same page: what stage each department is in, what it needs most right now, and where we need to align.
  • You'll make our four (typically international) offsites per year count. You'll understand why we're there, what each department would benefit most from, and how we make the most of our time together. The executive assistant, who reports to you, runs the logistics.
  • You'll make onboarding phenomenal, especially for leaders, so new people are effective and feel the mission in their first weeks.
  • You'll build the strategies and systems that let us do all of this at scale: how we level and compensate people, replacing case-by-case decisions; how we review performance; and how we part ways fairly, predictably and without delay. Our recruiters, our executive assistants, and our (now-fractional) HR Business Partner will report to you.

What we're looking for

  • You have 8+ years in people leadership, including a seat at the executive table at a company of 250+ people, where you owned talent and culture rather than administered them.
  • You can identify extraordinary talent and explain what makes it so. You've personally brought in people other companies couldn't get, you're well-networked enough to do it again, and you've hired and managed recruiters who could too.
  • You're an author of culture, and you take that responsibility seriously. You know what a strong culture feels like from the inside, you can name the handful of things that make it so, and you hold the company to them. You're direct, firm and hard to talk out of a position, and you want to push and be pushed by the co-founders as a peer.
  • You're a strategic, systematic executive, not an HR business partner. The ATS, HRIS and payroll are already running; your work is the thinking behind compensation, leadership, performance and retention, and the judgment to make clear calls and see them through. You've designed comp philosophies, grown first-time managers into real leaders, and made exits fair and fast.

How we work

We're a fast-growing, YC-backed company built on curiosity, a bias toward action, and a founder mindset. We'd rather ship something small and learn than debate it for a month. You'll report directly to Ellie Lasater-Guttmann, a cofounder. You will sit on the leadership team.
