title: Senior Product Marketing Manager
description:
Hi 👋 I'm Emily, Director of Growth Marketing at Pinpoint.

We build and sell software that helps in house recruitment teams attract, hire and onboard the right people. We're a team of about 100 across the UK and the US, with a mature product, strong product market fit and happy customers.

Pinpoint ships fast. Our product team releases new features every few weeks, and some of them change how we talk about the whole product. That pace is one of our biggest advantages, but only if customers, prospects, and our own team actually hear about it. Today most launches get positioned after they've gone live, so good work lands late and quietly.

We need one person to close that gap and be the connection between Product and the rest of the company. That's why we're hiring a Senior Product Marketing Manager. You'll know what's coming before it ships, decide how each feature is positioned, and make sure every launch is ready on day one. That way Sales can sell it and customers adopt it.

What you should know up front
  • Fully remote and UK based, with London coworking sessions, quarterly strategy days, and the occasional industry event.
  • You'll join a marketing team of 6, including you, covering growth, content, customer marketing, events, and marketing ops. You report to me, and as our sole dedicated product marketer, you'll set how product marketing works here.
  • The pace is the hard part. Something meaningful ships most weeks, so you'll be working ahead of the roadmap, chasing dates and detail with product managers, and deciding which launches get a big push and which get a light touch.
  • The team runs the website, customer campaigns, and events, and Sales owns the deck. You set the positioning and the plan (what's launching, what we call it, why it matters, and who does what), and make the core launch pieces yourself, from the launch copy and one pager to the enablement pack and whatever else the campaign needs.
  • We're AI forward. Everyone here uses AI every day to research, write, and build faster, and we'd expect you to bring that into how you plan and make launches.
  • This isn't a strategy only role. If you're used to a big team doing the making for you, it won't suit you.
  • Our values actually matter here. We hire people who reflect them in how they work, collaborate, and make decisions.

What you'll do

  • Feature level positioning. Own how we describe every significant feature: what it is, who it's for, the problem it solves, what we call it and how it compares. Bring a clear recommendation to Product and leadership, take their input, then make the call, and keep it consistent everywhere it shows up.
  • Outcome based stories. Translate what we ship into the results customers get, tying features together to show what's possible, backed by proof points and customer stories.
  • The Product and Marketing relationship. Sit close enough to Product that nothing is ever released as a surprise. Live in the roadmap in Fibery, read the specs and early designs, keep dates honest with product managers, and decide which launches get a big push and which get a light touch.
  • Launch planning and execution. Plan and run each launch with the rest of marketing: agree the customer adoption plan with our customer marketer, brief content on feature and integrations pages, and line up events, podcasts and social. Build the core launch assets yourself, then keep good features in market so they don't fade after a week.
  • Sales enablement. Give Sales what they need to sell what's new: messaging, talk tracks and enablement packs, plus briefs to keep the sales deck current.
  • Company wide product awareness. Make sure everyone who talks to customers (Sales, CS, Implementation, Support) knows what's shipped, why it matters and how to talk about it.
  • Product messaging across every asset. Be the source of truth for product messaging. After every priority release, flag what's out of date and get it fixed, briefing the owner or doing it yourself.
  • Making the pieces. Make what plays to your strengths yourself (product video, social, ad creative, simple designs, launch copy) and brief the rest. If you're great at one of them, it's yours.

What you'll bring

  • Product marketing experience in B2B SaaS, with features positioned and launched end to end and the work to show for it.
  • Launch and campaign management experience: a track record of running launches across lots of people (product, content, sales, customer marketing), with briefs that bring the work back right first time.
  • Technical depth: comfortable getting into how the product actually works, and able to explain technical features simply to any audience.
  • Startup or scale up experience: small teams, few handoffs, and a willingness to do whatever the launch needs that week.
  • Strategist and doer in the same day: writing the positioning in the morning and making the launch banner in the afternoon, with no direct reports to hand the work to.
  • Embedded early with product teams: in the roadmap and the specs before anything ships, and trusted by product managers because their launches get better for it.
  • The knack of turning a spec, a roadmap entry or a rough demo into positioning people actually use.
  • A doer who runs with a goal: sets it up, plans it and delivers it without hand holding or a big team behind them.
  • The judgement to stop and ask why: what a launch is meant to achieve, whether it's working, and when to change course.
  • A high bar for quality. Fast matters, but what goes out has to be good, and past work shows it.
  • Writing that's a real strength: clear, simple and straight to the point. Plain copy over clever copy, fewer words over more.
  • Good taste and the skills to make things without waiting on a designer or an agency: a banner, slide, page or short video that looks right. No need to be a designer.
  • An AI forward way of working: using AI every day to research, write and make things faster, even building simple tools to make launch assets.
You may not enjoy this role if
  • You'd rather write the strategy than ship the launch
  • You need a big team, a designer or an agency to get things out the door
  • You want a predictable roadmap with launches planned months ahead
  • You don't enjoy chasing people for dates and detail
  • You can't get to London for quarterly strategy days and in person meetings

What we offer

We want Pinpoint to be the best place you've ever worked, somewhere you feel valued, supported and excited to grow. Here's what you get:
  • Comprehensive healthcare: excellent medical, dental and vision coverage for you and your family
  • Unlimited holidays: take the time you need to rest and recharge
  • Mental health support: unlimited, immediate access to professional counselling via Spill
  • Retirement contributions: 401k or pension contributions depending on your location
  • Remote first: work where you're most productive, with flexibility and trust as the default
  • Equity with real upside: share in the long term value you help create
  • Fully paid parental leave: up to 16 weeks of paid leave for new parents
  • Learning budget: annual funds for courses, books or anything that supports your growth

title: Director, Demand Generation
description:
KPA has spent over four decades earning a reputation as the company automotive businesses trust with compliance. More than 15,000 of them count on us to protect their people, their customers, and their operations across Environmental Health & Safety (EHS), Sales, Advertising, Privacy, and HR.

Underneath it is one conviction: that documented is not the same as safe. A binder of current paperwork has never prevented an injury, so we built the company to close that gap. Software that's always watching out, training that reaches the newest person on the floor, and 150 consultants who keep finding what actually goes wrong. We think that work is worth doing somewhere people want to be, and Built In Colorado has named KPA one of the state's Best Places to Work seven years running.

Why This Role Exists

Automotive retail is consolidating, and the groups leading it are choosing the partners they'll run on for the next decade. More of their research now starts inside AI answer engines, and KPA's growth is concentrated in those multi-rooftop groups and in clients who already trust us adding coverage. That calls for a deliberate growth model, not a busier campaign calendar.

This role sets that model. You'd own the vision and strategy for demand generation across the company: the go-to-market model Marketing, Sales, and Client Success run together, the playbook behind it, the plan and investment case for the pipeline number, and the multi-year build-out of the team, technology, and measurement that will carry it at scale. While the team help you run the engine, you decide what it's built to do, where it points, and how big it gets.

If you've built a demand function before and want to design the next one from the model up, with the mandate to make it the way the whole company grows, this is it.

The Role

The Director, Demand Generation owns KPA's demand strategy and marketing's contribution to lead pipeline and revenue. You report to the Chief Marketing Officer, sit on the marketing leadership team, and lead the demand team and its agency partners.

The mandate runs in order: make the funnel measurable, make the engine repeatable, then scale it. The team is lean, so you'll definitely be hands-on and in the trenches, and will stay close enough to the work to pressure-test it. But your leverage is the model, the people, and the decisions.

Success is measured in pipeline against the company plan, a funnel all commercial functions trust, and an engine that gets more efficient as it grows, with a clear answer to where the next dollar goes and where we should be consistently testing and learning.

What You'll Do

Set the Vision and the Go-to-Market Model

  • Define KPA's demand generation vision and multi-year strategy, and turn it into an annual plan the company aligns to: targets, budget, channel mix, and capacity.
  • Design the go-to-market model by segment: single-rooftop dealers, multi-rooftop groups, fleet and adjacent segments; new logo, account-based, and expansion. Decide which plays each gets and what each should return.
  • Own the demand playbook as a company standard: the plays, the stage definitions, and the handoffs and service levels between Marketing and Sales (and Client Success). Codify it so it outlasts the current team.
  • Partner with Product Marketing and Product so every launch has a pipeline plan, not just an announcement.

Own the Pipeline Number and the Investment Case

  • Own marketing's sourced and influenced pipeline and revenue targets and the forecast behind them. Report against them candidly - including when the number is short.
  • Own the demand budget and make the case for it: reverse-funnel models, scenarios, and a defensible return on every line across channels, agencies, events, and technology.
  • Represent marketing performance to the executive team and the board with numbers that hold up under questioning.

Set the Measurement Standard

  • Decide KPA's funnel definitions (lead, MQL, SAL, SQL, opportunity) and attribution approach with Revenue Operations and Sales, align the organization, and hold every team to them.
  • Move KPA from counting engagements to counting true net-new demand, and be candid with leadership about what changes when the denominator does.
  • Define the reporting the business runs on (pipeline, velocity, CAC, CPL, and payback by segment, motion, and program) and the roadmap to a proper BI layer.

Build the Engine to Scale

  • Write the multi-year build-out plan: team structure and hiring sequence, what we build in-house versus buy from agencies, and the order in which new capabilities are deployed.
  • Set the marketing technology roadmap with Marketing Operations and Revenue Operations: what the stack must do at twice our size, what we consolidate, and what we retire.
  • Set the operating model for AI in demand gen, including where it helps compound output, where a person stays in the loop, and guardrails on accuracy, claims, brand voice, and data handling that a compliance company can defend.

Lead the Account-Based and Expansion Strategy

  • Set the strategy for the multi-rooftop groups consolidating the market: tiering, named-account coverage with Sales, and one coordinated marketing and SDR motion against each account.
  • Build the expansion strategy with Sales and Client Success. Growing coverage among the more than 15,000 clients who already trust KPA is the largest near-term growth lever we have.
  • With the Product, Product Marketing, Consulting, and Revenue Operations, turn KPA's field and incident data into proof the market can see: what our consultants found and the outcomes we helped prevent, stated in numbers.

Lead the Team and the Partnerships

  • Develop and retain a small team, starting with the Manager, Demand Generation and the Marketing Operations Manager. Set clear ownership, clear numbers, and a high bar for execution.
  • Direct the agency roster as the strategy owner with the CMO: set the brief and the targets, judge the work on outcomes, and decide what comes in-house.
  • Build the partnership with Sales leadership so the pipeline conversation is a working session rather than a negotiation.

What You Bring

Experience

  • 10–15 years of progressive B2B demand generation or growth marketing experience, ideally in SaaS or technology, with at least 3 years leading a team or function.
  • Demonstrated experience building a demand function and scaling it. You set the strategy, designed the model, implemented it, and hired the team, rather than inheriting one that already worked.
  • Ownership of a pipeline target and the budget behind it, defended in front of a CFO, an executive team, or a board.
  • Bachelor's degree in marketing, communications, business, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Deep Expertise: The Core of the Job

  • Go-to-market strategy. Segmentation, motion design, and channel mix, tied together by the economics: CAC, payback, pipeline coverage, and where the next dollar goes.
  • Revenue planning and measurement. Reverse-funnel planning, forecasting, funnel governance, and real command of attribution methodology, including its limits.
  • Building and leading teams. Org design, hiring, coaching managers, and directing agencies so a lean team performs like a much larger one.
  • AI and automation as an operating model. A track record of applying AI and other automation to real marketing workflows for measurable gains, with the judgment to set the strategy and guardrails for a whole team.

Strong Working Knowledge

  • Marketing technology. HubSpot (or Marketo, Pardot, or similar) and Salesforce, deep enough to set the roadmap, make changes, and audit how the stack is run.
  • Channels and programs. Paid search and social, SEO and visibility in AI answer engines, ABM and intent platforms, events, and lifecycle, deep enough to direct a manager and an agency rather than accept their report.

Nice to Have

  • Automotive retail, fleet, insurance, EHS, HR, or another regulated B2B category.
  • Demand generation for a multi-product portfolio sold into the same buyer.

The Intangibles

  • Vision with the math attached. Your strategy comes with a model, and you can make a dealer principal, a sales leader, and a board member each understand it.
  • Intellectually honest. You'd rather report a bad number accurately than a good number loosely. When the attribution is ambiguous, you’re candid and upfront about it.
  • Builds leaders. You measure yourself by how good your team gets, and you hire people who will outgrow the job you hired them for.
  • Comfortable with unfinished ground. Much of what this role needs doesn't exist quite yet. To you, that’s the reason to take it!
  • Opinionated, and warm about it. You have a point of view and you argue it without making anyone smaller.

Physical Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

This is a primarily sedentary role performed at a workstation, requiring extended periods of computer use and frequent verbal and written communication. Occasional travel is required as needed.

Compensation

  • Annual base salary between $150-180k commensurate with experience
  • Bonus potential up to 10% annually

Don’t meet every job requirement? At KPA, we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace. Studies have shown some people are less likely to apply unless they meet every requirement. If you’re excited about the role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification, we still encourage you to apply! You might just be the right candidate for this or other roles.

As a growing company KPAvalues its employees by supporting them with a full benefits package including Medical, Dental, Vision, Flexible Spending Accounts, PTO, Paid and Floating Holidays, 401k with Company match and immediate vesting, Company-funded Life Insurance, Employee Assistance Programs, and No-cost Mental Health Benefits.

These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. We serve approximately 9,000 clients and generated approximately $74 billion in FY26 revenue. Visit us at accenture.com.


We Are:

Accenture is recognized as a global leader in AI and cloud transformation, helping businesses across industries reimagine the digital core for an AI-native operating model. Through partnerships with frontier AI labs such as Anthropic and OpenAI, and the leading cloud providers, Accenture delivers end-to-end services that drive innovation and business agility.

The Digital Core Reinvention practice builds the enterprise ontology — the semantic layer that turns raw data into contextualized enterprise knowledge, and the knowledge agents that maintain, evolve, and query it. Where our problem-scoped ontology work wields meaning against a single problem, this discipline builds the meaning the whole enterprise stands on.


You Are:

A senior knowledge engineer ready to own the discipline: scaled ontology creation, the semantic layer, and the public technical argument for why AI without engineered meaning is guesswork.

This is the senior technical track at Accenture: we hire people here who would rather own a methodology than carry a number.


The Work:

As an Associate Director in this family you are the technical owner of our enterprise knowledge engineering services. Concretely, that means three things at once:

You own the methodology.

  • Scaled ontology creation, semantic-layer design, knowledge-agent patterns — yours to defend, evolve, and sign off on, including the boundary with problem-scoped ontology work (build the ontology here; wield it there).

You own the asset portfolio.

  • Ontology templates, entity-resolution patterns, semantic serving reference architectures — every engagement consumes or produces one.

You own the technical point of view.

  • You can explain the value of the semantic layer to a CFO and defend an OWL modeling decision to an architect in the same meeting — and the market hears the argument from you.

Travel may be required for this role. The amount of travel will vary from 0 to 100% depending on business need and client requirements.

Here's what you need:

This is not a “run the test plan someone else wrote” role. Until now, engineers have checked their own releases. The product has grown into a web app, connections to outside systems and AI chat features, so each release now needs someone who can say whether it’s ready, with evidence. New federal Medicaid rules start January 1, 2027, and the team is building tools that help states keep eligible people covered through them. You’ll start by building the automated tests and the ready-to-ship check for the releases closest to that date. It’s a hands-on, senior seat with no direct reports.   • Test strategy and automation

    • Decide where the product is most likely to break and what gets tested first

    • Pick the tools and run everything in GitHub Actions

  • Release verdicts

    • Give engineers a “ready / not ready” note before each release: what passed, what failed, what nobody checked

    • Write a plain-language summary for non-engineers of what’s verified, and push back on a risky date with evidence

  • Testing inside delivery teams

    • Sit with customer-facing teams and test features while they’re being built, moving between teams as workload shifts

    • Set a shared definition of “done” and coach engineers on testing their own work

  • Web app, services and outside systems

    • Make sure the product behaves sensibly when a dependency is slow, down or returns wrong data

  • AI chat features

    • Build evaluation suites with golden datasets for chatbots and assistants, rerun them on every prompt or model change, and test guardrails

    • Use AI tools to write, maintain and triage tests

  • Test data and security

    • Seed realistic test data for a complex system, inside strict access and data-protection rules

  • Strong test code in Python or TypeScript across API, browser and pipeline, including headless browser runs and integration tests for failing dependencies

title: Revenue Operations Engineer
description:
As a Revenue Operations Engineer at vCluster Labs, you aren't just keeping the CRM tidy; you are building the automated engine that tells our sellers which accounts matter and why. You will design Clay pipelines, enrichment workflows, and AI agents that surface the right accounts to sales and SDRs, and you will make sure they keep working long after launch. You own the GTM stack for our EMEA team, from Salesforce workflows to the integrations that tie HubSpot, Notion, and Slack together.

As a Revenue Operations Engineer, your role will include:

  • Account intelligence and enrichment: You will build and extend Clay tables, enrichment, and discovery pipelines that find new accounts and surface the right ones to sales and SDRs. You will push the tool well past its current setup and get the full value out of it.

  • AI agents and automation: You will turn manual GTM workflows into automated ones using agents in Clay, Salesforce, and Claude. You build them to run end to end and stay useful, not to demo once and break a month later.

  • Data quality that stays clean: You will design repeatable processes that keep account and contact data accurate over time. When a cleanup happens, it happens once, and the workflow behind it prevents the mess from coming back.

  • Scoring and top-of-funnel signals: You will own account and MQL funnel scoring and the signal workflows that route intent to the right seller at the right time.

  • Systems and integrations: You will build Salesforce workflows and maintain integrations across Salesforce, HubSpot, Momentum, Chili Piper, Notion, and Slack. When a new tool or feature beats what we built six months ago, you will make the call to replace it.

  • EMEA RevOps support: You will own the RevOps ticket queue during EMEA hours, partnering with our US-based RevOps teammate for follow-the-sun coverage. That includes helping reps with live opportunity questions, not only systems work.

This role could be a fit for you if you bring:

  • Hands-on Clay experience: You have built Clay tables, enrichment waterfalls, and pipelines yourself, and can explain what you would build next.

  • Salesforce depth: You can build Salesforce flows and automation, not just run reports. HubSpot fluency is expected alongside it.

  • AI-forward building: You have built AI agents or automations that run in production, using tools like Claude, Clay agents, or Salesforce automation, and you can show what they do today.

  • Systems thinking for GTM: You understand how scoring, routing, enrichment, and CRM hygiene connect, and you design for the whole loop rather than one fix.

  • EMEA-based and self-directed: You are based in EMEA, comfortable owning a queue without a teammate in your time zone, and you decide what to fix next without waiting to be told.

Bonus points for:

  • Salesforce Admin certification: Or equivalent admin-level experience owning an org.

  • Code and CLI comfort: Experience with scripting, APIs, the Claude CLI, or MCP integrations.

  • Startup scaling experience: You have helped a company grow from Series A toward later stage and built the systems that growth needed.

  • Advanced Clay or Anthropic tooling: You are the person others ask when they want to know what Clay or Claude can actually do.

About vCluster Labs

We're the #1 platform for AI infrastructure, trusted by the world's fastest-growing AI cloud builders. We're a venture-backed startup that's raised over $28M from top-tier investors including Khosla Ventures (first investor in OpenAI, GitLab, Stripe, and DoorDash), and we're in a hyper-growth phase looking for motivated people to join our team. Our headquarters are in San Francisco (Salesforce Tower), but our team is distributed around the globe with a remote-first culture.

We give AI Cloud providers and AI factories a hyperscaler-like experience on their own GPU infrastructure. Our platform runs the full stack an operator needs, from bare metal provisioning and node lifecycle management up through managed Kubernetes, Slurm, Ray, and inference clusters, so they can turn raw GPUs into cluster products they can sell in days instead of spending 12+ months building it themselves. Today we power over 100,000 GPUs and 1 million CPUs across 50+ AI clouds and Fortune 500 companies, backed by a team of 40+ infrastructure engineers who build alongside our customers rather than just shipping them software.

We're the company behind vCluster, the open source technology for tenant isolation on Kubernetes, with 11,000+ GitHub stars and 40M+ tenant clusters created since 2021. Open source is part of our DNA. At KubeCon North America 2025, we launched our Infrastructure Tenancy Platform for AI, a Kubernetes-native framework built for running AI, ML, and GPU-intensive workloads anywhere, with an NVIDIA-validated reference architecture for DGX systems.

Benefits

We offer the following benefits:

  • Competitive Salary: We offer a competitive compensation package, including equity.

  • Premium Insurance: Health, dental, vision, and life Insurance, including plans for you and eligible dependents (benefits vary depending on country).

  • Flexible Working Schedule: You have a doctor’s appointment or need to head to the supermarket to get groceries at 2pm? We won’t have an issue with that. To us, results matter more than clocking in and out at the same time every day.

  • Workplace Flexibility: We’re very flexible about where you work. We know things can change in life and we’re happy to adjust the work environment for you along the way.

Culture & Values

At vCluster Labs, we value and stand for:

  1. Make it Happen: We have a relentless bias for action and the grit to push through obstacles. We do whatever it takes to figure it out, put in the work, and ruthlessly prioritize the actions that drive measurable impact for the business.

  2. Own the Outcome: We understand that our responsibility doesn't end when a task is checked off; it ends when the value is delivered. We connect our daily individual actions to the broader success of the company and our customers.

  3. Create Wow: We measure success by the experience we generate, both inside and outside the company. For our customers, this means impressive speed and intuitive experiences. For our team, this means going the extra mile to support one another and to continuously drive each other to new heights.

  4. Open Source, Open Mind: We are actively contributing to and maintaining open-source projects. Internally, we foster meritocracy — the strongest ideas win, no matter who or where they come from.

  5. Build Tomorrow’s Standards, Intentionally: We don't just ship software; we define the state-of-the-art of tomorrow. We are fearless in tearing down old approaches to build something better, but we are disciplined in how we do it because we know our users rely on our technology to run mission-critical infrastructure platforms.

title: Senior Strategic Account Executive, Southeast
description:
Who We Are

Spectro Cloud helps platform teams and cloud providers modernize and manage infrastructure for the AI era without adding more tools or operational complexity.

With PaletteAI, enterprises, public sector organizations, neoclouds and sovereign clouds can build, govern and operate full-stack environments across VMs, Kubernetes, edge, regulated and air-gapped locations, and AI infrastructure. PaletteAI Launchpads help teams start quickly with urgent outcomes such as VMware migration, token cost control or edge modernization, then scale into enterprise-wide lifecycle management, governance and fleet operations on the same platform.

Who We Are Seeking

We are looking for a seasoned Senior Strategic Account Executive based in the US Southeast area to own and grow a strategic Midwest territory.

This is a high-impact, new-logo-focused role for an experienced infrastructure seller who knows how to create opportunities, navigate complex enterprise organizations, develop executive relationships, and close strategic deals.

This person will be expected to own the success of their region from both a revenue and go-to-market perspective. That means building the territory, developing the right ecosystem, creating pipeline, establishing executive relationships, working closely with channel and technology partners, and helping determine how Spectro Cloud wins in the region.

We want someone who is willing to participate in their own success. You will have support from Marketing, Sales Engineering, leadership, and our partner ecosystem, but you are ultimately accountable for building and executing the plan that makes your territory successful.

The ideal candidate understands modern infrastructure and can sell across multiple lines of business—not simply into one technical team. You should be able to navigate infrastructure, cloud, platform engineering, virtualization, AI, security, application, and executive organizations while connecting Spectro Cloud's technology to measurable business outcomes.

What You Will Own

As the Senior Strategic Account Executive for the region, you will operate like the CEO of your territory.

You will:

  • Own the overall go-to-market strategy and revenue success of your region.

  • Develop and execute a strategic territory plan across named and target enterprise accounts.

  • Build pipeline through direct prospecting, executive relationships, marketing programs, channel partners, technology partners, and industry relationships.

  • Drive new-logo acquisition while identifying opportunities to expand across additional business units and lines of business.

  • Build relationships across multiple organizations within each account, including infrastructure, cloud, platform engineering, virtualization, AI, DevOps, application teams, security, finance, and executive leadership.

  • Establish relationships with CIOs, CTOs, Chief AI Officers, infrastructure executives, platform leaders, and other senior decision-makers.

  • Develop multiple champions within strategic accounts rather than relying on a single point of entry.

  • Create account strategies that expand Spectro Cloud's footprint across divisions, geographies, teams, and use cases.

  • Work closely with channel partners, VARs, systems integrators, cloud providers, OEMs, and technology alliances to develop and execute joint account strategies.

  • Recruit, enable, and activate the right partners within the territory.

  • Build joint pipeline with channel partners rather than treating the channel solely as a fulfillment mechanism.

  • Identify strategic regional events, partners, communities, and customer relationships that can help accelerate Spectro Cloud's market presence.

  • Serve as the voice of the region back to Sales, Marketing, Product, and executive leadership.

What You Will Sell

You will position Spectro Cloud's portfolio across a broad set of enterprise infrastructure and AI initiatives, including:

  • Enterprise Kubernetes management

  • Hybrid and multi-cloud infrastructure

  • Virtualization modernization

  • VMware alternatives and modernization initiatives

  • Data center modernization

  • Edge and distributed computing

  • Platform engineering

  • GPU infrastructure

  • AI infrastructure

  • AI workload orchestration

  • Infrastructure efficiency and economics

  • Tokenomics and AI inference economics

You will be expected to uncover opportunities across multiple lines of business and connect Spectro Cloud capabilities to broader enterprise transformation initiatives.

Strategic Selling

This is not a role where pipeline is simply handed to you.

Successful candidates know how to create a market within their territory and build opportunities from the ground up.

You will be expected to:

  • Proactively create pipeline within strategic enterprise accounts.

  • Maintain strong pipeline coverage for current and future quarters.

  • Develop executive relationships early in the sales process.

  • Run effective discovery across technical, operational, financial, and executive stakeholders.

  • Identify and develop multiple strong internal champions.

  • Establish access to the Economic Buyer.

  • Develop relationships across multiple buying centers and lines of business.

  • Navigate complex enterprise buying committees, procurement processes, and technical evaluations.

  • Connect technical capabilities to measurable business outcomes, TCO, risk reduction, operational efficiency, and infrastructure economics.

  • Use MEDDPICC and Mutual Action Plans to maintain control of complex opportunities.

  • Build compelling executive-level business cases.

  • Orchestrate internal Spectro Cloud resources and external partners around strategic opportunities.

  • Drive late-stage opportunities with urgency, accountability, and clear next steps.

  • Maintain disciplined forecasting and demonstrate complete command of your business.

Channel & Partner Leadership

Channel success is an important component of this role.

You will:

  • Build strong relationships with strategic channel partners throughout the region.

  • Identify partners that can open doors into targeted enterprise accounts.

  • Develop joint GTM strategies and account plans with key partners.

  • Create and manage partner-generated pipeline.

  • Work with VARs, systems integrators, cloud providers, OEMs, and technology partners.

  • Help partners understand how Spectro Cloud fits into infrastructure modernization, Kubernetes, virtualization, GPU, and AI initiatives.

  • Coordinate partner, customer, and Spectro Cloud resources to accelerate strategic opportunities.

  • Hold partners accountable while making Spectro Cloud a company they want to bring into their most important accounts.

What You Bring

  • 10+ years of successful enterprise technology sales experience.

  • Proven success selling complex infrastructure technology into large enterprise organizations.

  • Consistent history of meeting or exceeding quota.

  • Strong new-logo acquisition experience.

  • Demonstrated ability to build a territory rather than simply manage an existing book of business.

  • Experience developing and executing regional GTM strategies.

  • Strong experience working with channel partners and building partner-generated pipeline.

  • Experience selling across multiple lines of business within large enterprise accounts.

  • Ability to develop relationships from technical practitioners through C-level executives.

  • Experience selling technologies involving cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes, containers, virtualization, data centers, platform engineering, GPU infrastructure, AI infrastructure, or adjacent enterprise infrastructure technologies.

  • Working knowledge of Kubernetes and the cloud-native ecosystem.

  • Strong understanding of virtualization and the evolving VMware landscape.

  • Familiarity with AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud.

  • Understanding of GPU infrastructure and the enterprise AI ecosystem is highly desirable.

  • Ability to discuss infrastructure economics, TCO, operational efficiency, AI economics, and business value.

  • Strong MEDDPICC skills and experience managing complex enterprise buying processes.

  • Excellent territory planning, pipeline generation, forecasting, and opportunity management discipline.

  • Established enterprise and partner relationships within Chicago and the broader Midwest are highly desirable.

  • Ability and willingness to travel throughout the region as required.

Why Spectro Cloud

Enterprise infrastructure is undergoing one of its largest transformations in decades.

Kubernetes, virtualization modernization, distributed infrastructure, GPU computing, and AI are converging and changing how organizations design, deploy, and operate technology.

Spectro Cloud sits at the center of that transformation.

If you want to own a strategic market, build meaningful executive and partner relationships, and sell technology addressing some of the most important infrastructure and AI challenges facing enterprises today, we'd like to hear from you.

description:
ABOUT KLED

Kled is building the largest opt-in human data network in the world.

We are not a labeling firm. We are not a task marketplace.

We are a consumer application where people upload their real photos, videos, and documents and get paid continuously.

We then filter, standardize, and license that data to frontier AI labs and enterprises that need fresh, rights-aware training data.

Since launching our mobile app in 2026, we have:

• Reached #1 on the App Store (Finance) with 0 paid marketing
• Scaled to 600,000+ active data contributors

• Processed 5M uploads per day

• Raised $15M+ from investors behind SpaceX, Airbnb, Coinbase, xAI, OpenAI, Anthropic, Spotify, Lyft, Uber, and more

Our mission is to let anyone download the app and earn a real living wage from uploading their data.

This listing is for one paid task in the Kled app: "Narrate What You Are Doing While You Do It". There is no interview and no minimum hours: download the app, open the task, and you are paid per accepted submission.

What you will do

Film any everyday task with your hands in shot, and say out loud what you're doing as you do it.

Steps

  1. Prop your phone or hang it round your neck so your hands are in shot

  2. Start recording in Kled and begin the task

  3. Say what you are doing as you do it, 'now I'm loosening this screw', 'this bit always sticks'

  4. Keep going to the end without stopping the recording

  5. Upload

What gets rejected

  • Do not narrate afterwards, talk while you work

  • Do not stop and restart the recording

  • Do not film with your hands out of shot

  • Do not read from a script

Accepted: One unbroken take, hands visible throughout, continuous speech describing the action as it happens.

Pay

$2.60 per accepted clip. At a typical pace of about 7 minutes per clip, that is about $22 per hour. A 20-minute session of about 3 clips pays about $7.80. One clip of 3 to 5 minutes per submission. You are paid per accepted submission (piecework, independent contractor); submissions that break the rules are not paid. Payouts are made in the app (PayPal, Venmo or a Solana wallet).

Where and when

Open worldwide: the task runs in 100+ countries. Remote, on your own schedule. Independent contractor, piecework; this is not an employment position.

What you need

  • An iPhone running iOS 18.6 or later (the Kled app is iPhone-only right now)

  • 18 or older

  • Somewhere to prop your phone so it sees your hands and the work

How to start

  1. Download Kled from the App Store: (also at kled.ai/app).

  2. Create your account and open Tasks.

  3. Search "Narrate What You Are Doing While You Do It", read the brief and follow the on-screen steps.

  4. Submit. Accepted submissions are paid in the app.

title: Endpoint Engineer (Journeyman)
description:
Overview

DecisionPoint seeks an Endpoint Engineer to develop, maintain, deploy, and support standardized endpoint capabilities for the USMEPCOM ENLIST program. This position supports endpoint images, application packaging, device provisioning, software deployment, patching, configuration baselines, and Virtual Desktop Infrastructure.

The Endpoint Engineer supports physical and virtual endpoints throughout their lifecycle, including testing, deployment, configuration, patching, troubleshooting, refresh, recovery, and retirement. The engineer works with the Senior Endpoint Engineer and other technical teams to deliver secure, consistent, and supportable endpoint services across USMEPCOM Headquarters, MEPS, Remote Processing Substations, COOP locations, and remote-user environments.

This role maintains a clear division of responsibility with Task 6 cybersecurity personnel. Task 6 identifies, prioritizes, and validates security findings. The Endpoint Engineer evaluates assigned findings, tests the approved correction, implements the operational change through established change-control procedures, and provides deployment evidence for cybersecurity validation.

This position is remote, with Chicago-area candidates preferred. Occasional after-hours maintenance, incident response, on-site support, or travel may be required.

Note: By applying to this position, you acknowledge and consent to having your resume included in an active competitive government contract bid.

Duties & Responsibilities

The Endpoint Engineer will:

  • Develop, test, maintain, and document standardized endpoint images.
  • Maintain image components, operating-system settings, drivers, firmware dependencies, security baselines, required software, and deployment configurations.
  • Support image versioning, testing, approval, release, rollback, and retirement processes.
  • Validate endpoint images for functionality, compatibility, security, performance, and operational readiness.
  • Develop and maintain automated device-deployment task sequences, provisioning workflows, enrollment processes, and configuration profiles.
  • Support endpoint deployment using approved Microsoft and Government management platforms.
  • Administer approved endpoint-management capabilities involving Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Configuration Manager, Windows Autopilot, or comparable technologies.
  • Develop, test, maintain, and deploy application packages.
  • Package commercial, Government, and internally developed software using approved formats and standards.
  • Develop installation, detection, dependency, requirement, upgrade, repair, and removal logic.
  • Test application packages for silent installation, accurate detection, compatibility, security, and clean removal.
  • Troubleshoot package failures, dependency problems, application conflicts, detection errors, and deployment issues.
  • Develop approved scripts and automation for provisioning, packaging, configuration, deployment, validation, and remediation.
  • Maintain endpoint-management scripts and configurations in approved documentation and version-control repositories.
  • Support patching of endpoint operating systems, applications, drivers, firmware, and management components.
  • Configure and maintain pilot groups, deployment rings, production waves, maintenance windows, deadlines, and exception processes.
  • Test operating-system updates, security patches, vendor patches, and application updates before production deployment.
  • Monitor patch and deployment progress, failure rates, compliance status, endpoint health, and approved exceptions.
  • Investigate failed patches and coordinate corrective actions, redeployment, rollback, or exception documentation.
  • Engineer and support Virtual Desktop Infrastructure capabilities.
  • Develop and maintain VDI base images, desktop pools, application delivery, user-profile configurations, and endpoint-access policies.
  • Troubleshoot VDI login, profile, application, display, performance, peripheral, and connectivity problems.
  • Support VDI refreshes, upgrades, capacity activities, deployment, testing, and optimization.
  • Coordinate VDI dependencies with virtualization, storage, network, identity, application, and cybersecurity teams.
  • Support endpoint deployment and refresh projects across geographically dispersed USMEPCOM locations.
  • Assist with device provisioning, enrollment, configuration, testing, deployment, replacement, recovery, and retirement.
  • Support operating-system upgrades, application migrations, technology refreshes, and endpoint-management transitions.
  • Provide advanced engineering support for complex endpoint, image, application-packaging, deployment, patching, and VDI incidents.
  • Analyze endpoint logs, deployment status, policy results, management-platform data, and other technical evidence.

title: Senior Software Engineer - Machine Learning Platform
description:
About Upstart

At Upstart, we’re united by a mission that matters: to radically reduce the cost and complexity of borrowing for all Americans. Every day, we bring creativity, experimentation, and advanced AI to reshape access to credit, helping millions move forward financially with clarity and confidence.

As the leading AI lending marketplace, we partner with banks and credit unions to expand access to affordable credit through technology that’s both radically intelligent and deeply human. Our platform runs over one million predictions per borrower using more than 3,000 signals, powering smarter, fairer decisions for millions of customers. But the numbers only hint at the impact. Every idea, every voice, and every contribution moves us closer to a world where credit never stands between people and their financial progress.

We’re proudly digital-first, giving most Upstarters the flexibility to do their best work from wherever they thrive, alongside teammates across 80+ cities in the US and Canada. Digital-first doesn’t mean distant. We’re intentional about in-person connection through team onsites, planning sessions, and moments that spark creativity and trust. And whether you choose to work primarily from home or collaborate in-person from one of our offices in Columbus, Austin, the Bay Area, or New York City, you’ll have the support to work in the way that works best for you.

If you’re energized by tackling meaningful problems, excited to innovate with purpose, and motivated by work that truly matters, we’d love to hear from you.

The Team:

The Machine Learning and Simulations Platform (MLSP) team builds and operates the core infrastructure that powers ML model training,feature engineering, inference, and marketplace simulation at Upstart. Every underwriting, fraud, conversion, and verification model runs on this platform. We own the full production path: the data and features that feed a model, the infrastructure that serves it at decision time, the tooling that deploys it, and the simulation systems that predict business impact before a change goes live.

We are reimagining that platform to keep pace with our ML teams. That work spans low latency and GPU model serving, self-service model deployment, a feature platform that gives ML one place to define and serve production features, and high fidelity marketplace simulation. The team partners closely with ML, Engineering, Product, Data Platform.

As a Senior Software Engineer on the ML and Simulations Platform team at Upstart, you will be responsible for building an MLOps platform to support machine learning model inference, process automation, model deployment, and observability. Machine Learning is critical to Upstart’s core business, and our greatest competitive advantage lies in the fact that we’re able to innovate on our AI engine quickly. You will also help build a marketplace simulation platform to support rapid innovation across ML and Finance teams.

How you’ll make an impact

  • Build, maintain, and optimize Upstart’s next-generation machine learning and simulation platform, enabling increased scale, performance, and confidence in decisioning.
  • Develop high-quality software applications that enable machine learning models to be applied to the ever-evolving needs of the business
  • Build self-service tooling so ML teams can register features and deploy models independently, and reduce the manual work the platform team absorbs today.
  • Deliver the data and feature infrastructure behind every model, including feature definition, storage, serving, and offline to online parity.
  • Design and contribute to our simulation systems to more accurately reflect production environments, reducing simulation cost and enabling broader usage across teams.
  • Communicate closely with cross-functional partners from ML, Engineering, Product, and Data Engineering teams, keeping all stakeholders informed
  • Mentor engineers across the team, sharing expertise on distributed systems,MLOps, and scalable architecture.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 6+ years of software engineering experience.
  • Experience building and maintaining backend software services and APIs.
  • Experience with distributed systems or large scale data processing, using Spark, Databricks, Ray, or an equivalent.
  • Experience with an ML platform or the ML production path, such as training pipelines, model serving, feature pipelines, or a training data platform.
  • Proficiency with some or many of the following: Python, Kotlin, Databricks, and AWS.
  • Exhibits a growth mindset. You pick up new technologies that fit the task, and you learn from others.
  • Ability to quickly comprehend complex requirements from ML, product, or engineering leadership, and translate them for both technical and non-technical partners.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Skill with Metaflow, MLflow, gRPC, Spark/PySpark, dbt, Ray, GPU
  • Knowledge of simulation, experimentation, or backtesting systems.
  • Experience building self-serve or configuration driven tooling for internal users.
  • Excellent quantitative reasoning skills with interest in working at the intersection of engineering and machine learning.
  • Strong sense of ownership and accountability for the quality and timely delivery of work.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with partners, peers, and product owners.
  • Ability to thrive in self-directed work and in collaborative settings, contributing positively to team dynamics.

Position location This role is available in the following locations: Remote

Time zone requirements The team operates on the East/West coast time zones.

Travel requirements As a digital first company, the majority of your work can be accomplished remotely. The majority of our employees can live and work anywhere in the U.S but are encouraged to to still spend high quality time in-person collaborating via regular onsites. The in-person sessions’ cadence varies depending on the team and role; most teams meet once or twice per quarter for 2-4 consecutive days at a time.

At Upstart, your base pay is one part of your total compensation package. The anticipated base salary for this position is expected to be within the below range. Your actual base pay will depend on your geographic location–with our “digital first” philosophy, Upstart uses compensation regions that vary depending on location. Individual pay is also determined by job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for your preferred location during the hiring process.

In addition, Upstart provides employees with target bonuses, equity compensation, and generous benefits packages (including medical, dental, vision, and 401k).

United States | Remote - Anticipated Base Salary Range
$166,900—$230,000 USD

What you'll love

At Upstart, our benefits are designed to support your health, financial well-being, family, and personal growth. Here’s what you can expect:

  • Competitive compensation, including base pay, bonus opportunities, and annual equity grants that vest quarterly
  • Retirement benefits to help you plan for the future, including a 401(k) or Group Retirement Savings Plan with a company match of $2 for every $1 contributed, up to $15,000 annually (USD in the US, CAD in Canada)

Congress Coordinator
Singapore

The Congress Coordinator is responsible to support all activities associated with logistics planning and attendee management of various International congresses. The position requires a high level of attention to detail, strong customer service skills, a can-do attitude, and a desire to get the job done. The Congress Coordinator will regularly partner with internal planning team members to ensure timely service delivery, manage strong working relationships with Professional Congress Organizers (PCO) and suppliers handle compliance and contracting documentation of assigned congresses, preparing print materials, and sending post congress surveys.

The Congress Coordinator works closely with the Congress Project Manager (CPM) and is typically a behind-the-scenes role; however, there may be instances where it makes sense for the Congress Coordinator to interact directly with the client. An example might be that the client requires a complicated web-build and wants to speak to the Congress Coordinator directly or the client requires frequent attendee status updates and wants to communicate with the Congress Coordinator directly. Most of the time, the Congress Coordinator is NOT client facing.

Your responsibilities :

Core Responsibility 1: Meeting Planning

• Secure and manage hotel room blocks in accordance with Congress rules and procedures
• Oversee securing congress registrations for attendees
• Ensure all compliance requirements and guidelines are followed and properly documented
• Reconcile meeting in accordance with Client audit standards/maintain an audit ready environment

Core Responsibility 2: Supplier Management
• Prepare and submit Travel Engagement Forms to Group Travel provider
• Partner with internal planning team members to source DMC/Ground Transportation Company options
• Secure and manage all dinner arrangements in compliance with country requirements and meal threshold spend limits
• Handle day to day client and supplier inquiries/information related to logistics, dinners and ground transportation including country meal threshold exceptions and flight information
• Ensure all compliance requirements and guidelines are followed and properly documented
• Act as primary contact with local suppliers and client stakeholders to ensure open communication
• Review all supplier proposals, contracts and invoices in accordance with Client audit standards/maintaining an audit ready environment
• Gather and accurately communicate flight information from each country to supplier(s) for Airport Transfers
• Prepare all Printed Material/Communications (Welcome Packet, Front Desk letter, etc.) and ship to congress locations
• Coordinate on-site job responsibilities with on-site logistics team (Dinners, ground, logistics, etc.)

Core Responsibility 3: Technology Tools
• Oversee the creation and sending of registration forms and other communications
• Correctly upload and maintain attendee data required for logistics and reporting
• Review client congress database for accuracy
• Oversee accuracy for all assigned congresses in the technology tool (Cvent)
• Experience using Cvent attendee, hotel, and reporting modules
• Correctly import and maintain attendee data in Cvent
• Keep data and savings information accurate in Cvent at all times
• Ensure internal and external reporting requirements are met accurately and on time
• Create and maintain a master response chart for each assigned congress
• Oversee the creation and sending of final confirmation emails and other communications
• Create shared drive folder for assigned congresses
• Partner with internal planning team members to start Congress Workbook and continually update throughout the planning process
• Oversee the creation and sending/upload of restaurant descriptions and request forms and other pertinent communications, and save in the proper shared drive(s)
• Update Event Emails as needed in technology tool (Cvent)
• Correctly advise internal planning team members of changes to attendee data required for logistics and reporting

• Maintain current records of all communications (i.e. TEF, Country Meal Summary, Manifests, etc.) in the proper shared drive(s)

• Overall fiscal responsibility for congress activities

Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice or as required by local regulations.

We're looking for you if your profile matches the following:

  • Bachelor’s Degree strongly preferred

Flexible Working

We believe that a flexible working environment is key to getting the best out of our teams. We will support you to work where you need to and when you need to, depending on how you work best.

Our line of work and business structure challenge our people in a way that inspires growth, with learning and development built into every role. We give individuals ownership over the direction and speed in which they grow.

Everyone has a voice

We thrive on conversations that spark curiosity and empathy. No matter how big or how small, every voice is heard, considered and respected.

Make your move

The diversity of roles across BCD M&E’s global locations means that our people often find new adventures during their time with us.

We’ve got you covered

Our extensive benefits include comprehensive healthcare, continued education support, diverse work locations, travel and hotel discounts, volunteer and sustainability opportunities and a successful employee recognition program.


We’re positive. You’ll love it.

title: Financial Access Spclst
description:
Our Mission

All of us, for each of you, every time.

Our Vision

Together, serving as the trusted regional healthcare partner.

Our Values

Listen~Love~Respect~Excel~Innovate

At Samaritan, we do more than deliver healthcare—we make a meaningful difference in the lives of our community every day. We’re committed to creating an exceptional workplace where professionals feel valued, supported, and inspired to provide outstanding care to every patient we serve. The Financial Access Specialist serves the Hospital and Clinic by performing pre-service financial screening and clearance of scheduled patients, including benefit verification and price estimation. This position will maintain a proficient understanding of insurance plans, including State Medicaid, employer-sponsored plans, Medicare Advantage plans and Qualified Health Plans offered via the State Exchange. The Financial Access Specialist will determine benefit coverage levels and connect patients with alternate assistance resources as needed. The Financial Access Specialist interacts in a customer-focused and compassionate manner to ensure patients’ needs are met, and that they understand the hospital and clinic policies for the resolution of patient financial responsibilities and various payment options, including Financial Assistance. In all encounters with patients and families, the Financial Access Specialist will strive for the highest level of customer service.

This is a full-time remote position that will be required to come on-site for onboarding and equipment pick-up (3-4 DAYS ONLY). This is a full-time role working Monday-Friday from 8:30 AM – 5:00 PM PST.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

  1. Review schedules for future dates of service on a revolving basis.
  2. Answer patient financial inquiries via phone and in-person regarding scheduled and/or future planned visits.
  3. Identify patients’ financial needs and align with appropriate resources.
  4. Communicate patient financial obligation, provide estimate, and pursue pre-service deposit.
  5. Collects from patients who have ability to pay, including past balances, down payments, co-payments and/or deductibles.
  6. With the assistance of person(s) responsible for pre-authorization and/or Pre-Registration Specialists, ensures authorization is secure prior to services and maintain accurate record of authorizations.
  7. Verify service-specific insurance benefits and provide benefit/coverage review. Accurately explain concepts such as deductible, coinsurance and/or co-payments and how they may affect the cost of care.
  8. Explain payment expectations for non-covered and out-of-network services.
  9. Review and explain all forms prior to obtaining signatures from patient or appropriate representative.
  10. Ensures appropriate forms are signed prior to services (i.e., sterilization permit, No Surprises Act, non-covered waiver, ABN, etc.).
  11. Collaborate with Case Management, Billing, Admitting, person(s) responsible for pre-authorization, and pre-registration with the goal of securing payment for services provided.
  12. Discuss financial arrangements for newborn(s); informs patients of the timeframe for enrolling a newborn in coverage, provides any documentation or guidance for the patient to enroll their child prior to or after the anticipated delivery date.
  13. Keep current with specific insurance rules and changes, including State Exchange.
  14. Aid patients in completion of Medicaid application via Washington Healthplan Finder.
  15. Promptly notifies insurance company of admissions and discharges per insurance company requirements.
  16. Communicate via phone, email, mail, and in-person regarding payment expectations.
  17. Comply with HIPAA regulations, maintaining confidentiality and utilizing information only as necessary to complete work.
  18. Utilizes appropriate strategies, including phone calls and online databases to verify the insurance coverage of scheduled patients to ensure services are provided and reimbursements are ultimately obtained.
  19. Documents all information obtained during patient financial screening to ensure a streamlined process for financial assistance needs.
  20. Strong organizational skills, ability to work independently and prioritize tasks.
  21. Ensures patient have logistical information necessary to receive their service (e.g., appointment place, date and time, directions to facility).
  22. Performs other duties as assigned. Ensures additional accountabilities, as may be required by management, be handled in a manner necessary to meet organizational standards.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

The professional in this position reports to the Director of Revenue Cycle. This position works closely with Scheduling (Hospital and Clinic), Financial Counselors, Case Management, Billing, Admitting professionals and Physician offices to ensure completion of all pre-service financial clearance functions.

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE

  • Education:
    1. Minimum High School Diploma or equivalent required.
    2. Associate’s degree in healthcare administration or equivalent college coursework preferred.
  • Experience:
    1. 1-3 years of work experience with insurance verification, revenue cycle functions, hospital/physician offices or related area’s preferred.
    2. 1-3 years customer service experience required.
  • Skills/Competencies:
    1. Demonstrates competency on equipment listed on department specific checklist.
    2. Critical thinking skills: Seeks resources for direction when necessary.
    3. Performs independent problem solving. Decision-making is logical and deliberate.
    4. Performs actions that demonstrate accountability. Exercises safe judgement and practices within legal and ethical guidelines.
    5. Demonstrates competency in ability to care for customers/patients across the age continuum.
    6. Demonstrates strong organizational skills.
    7. Provides high quality customer service.
    8. Familiarity with statutes and regulations that can impact financial conversations with patients (e.g., 501(r).

As a Samaritan professional, you will be asked to commit to being part of a culture grounded in our Mission, Vision, Values, and Strategy that brings service and operational excellence to life each day while creating an exceptional experience for our patients, professionals, physicians, and students. Additionally, how we present ourselves matters, and adherence to our Professional Appearance Policy reflects the pride, respect, and professionalism we bring to those we serve.

We are seeking a Product Counsel to join the legal team of a mature, but still fast-growing SaaS business. You will partner closely with Product, Engineering, Security, and Go-to-Market teams throughout the product lifecycle, providing practical legal guidance on product development, AI, data privacy, emerging technologies, and global regulatory requirements. The successful candidate will serve as a trusted, business-embedded legal partner, helping to identify and manage legal risk while enabling innovation and supporting the development and launch of market-leading SaaS products.

Who you are:

  • A minimum of 3 years of substantive legal experience, preferably within the in-house legal department of a SaaS company.
  • Demonstrated knowledge in AI and data privacy law and regulations, with a strong understanding of emerging technologies.
  • Experience working with, and advising on, AI-powered products and services.

  • Strong project management skills and a collaborative and proactive approach, with a passion for innovation and a desire to be a strategic partner.
  • An understanding of the SaaS industry, its unique legal challenges, and the global regulatory landscape.
  • The ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and thrive in a fast-paced environment.
  • Curiosity and a willingness to tackle new challenges.

Bonus points if you have:

  • Experience working with financial services customers.
  • A coding background or a strong understanding of technical concepts.
  • Experience working at a startup or fast-paced growth company.

What you'll be doing:

  • Serve as a trusted business partner and work closely with product and engineering teams throughout the entire product lifecycle, from concept development to go-to-market strategy.
  • Proactively identify and assess potential legal and global regulatory risks associated with our products and services.
  • Develop and implement strategies to address and mitigate legal and compliance risks in our products.

title: Backend Developer
description:
About the role

We are seeking a proactive, technically strong Backend Developer to keep a live, business-critical microservices platform healthy while delivering meaningful improvements on top of it.

This is a hands-on role with a high degree of autonomy: you’ll take a bug report or change request, investigate it across the codebase, and see it through to production. You’ll balance production support with feature engineering, backed by a supportive team, and we’re embracing agentic development with AI coding agents to ship efficiently without compromising quality.

Key responsibilities

  • Resolve production issues: Triage, diagnose, and resolve issues across distributed microservices, tracing a request from the user-facing API down to the services that talk to external systems.
  • Support incident response: Investigate root causes, apply fixes, add regression tests, and document findings so issues don’t recur
  • Deliver enhancements: Build improvements to existing services, including new versions of certification programs, scorecard and scoring changes, payment adjustments, and integration updates
  • Work within the architecture: Follow established patterns and shared internal libraries in a layered service architecture, from the API gateway through the business logic services down to the adapters that integrate with external systems
  • Maintain integrations: Maintain and extend integrations with external platforms for performance data, CRM, enterprise resource planning (ERP), payment processing, email, and cloud file storage
  • Manage data changes: Write and update database migration scripts and investigate data-related production issues carefully against live data
  • Partner with QA and product: Answer testers’ questions, clarify expected behavior, help reproduce issues, and support verification so fixes and features can be signed off smoothly. Ask product clarifying questions early and confirm intent and edge cases
  • Improve observability and documentation: Contribute structured logging, masking of sensitive data, and clearer production visibility, and take part in code review while keeping documentation current as the platform grows

Required qualifications

  • Proven ability to take ownership of a problem from start to finish, from initial bug report or change request through to a tested, deployed solution
  • Production experience building and maintaining backend services with Node.js and TypeScript
  • Strong experience with NestJS (or a comparable structured backend framework), including modules, controllers, services, dependency injection, and middleware
  • Solid REST/HTTP fundamentals, including service-to-service communication, API contracts, versioning, and error handling
  • Comfortable with relational databases, writing and reviewing PostgreSQL queries, and safe migration practices
  • Experience debugging distributed systems where a single feature spans several services, reading logs and metrics to find root causes rather than symptoms
  • Sound judgment about risk, including the difference between a safe local fix and a change that calls for a rollout plan, particularly for payments, authentication, and live data
  • Experience integrating third-party systems (payment providers, CRMs, ERPs, identity providers) behind a clean internal interface
  • Understanding of authentication patterns: OAuth 2.0, JWT verification, single sign-on (SSO), and service-to-service (machine-to-machine) authentication
  • Comfortable with agentic development, using AI coding agents and tooling to investigate, build, and ship work efficiently while keeping a careful eye on quality
  • Ability to write tests that confirm fixes and prevent regressions
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including clear status updates, incident notes, pull request descriptions, and documentation others can act on

Nice to have

  • Experience supporting a platform through the transition from active build to maintenance-and-enhancement mode
  • Familiarity with adapter patterns that isolate external systems from core business logic
  • Experience with webhook-driven integrations, including verifying signatures, scoped service-to-service authorization, and safely handling repeated inbound events
  • Familiarity with containers and orchestration (Docker and Kubernetes) and services deployed on a major cloud provider such as AWS
  • Experience with observability practices such as structured logging and masking of sensitive data

title: Talent Acquisition Partner - South Region
description:
Company Overview

Throughout our worldwide network of experts, clients and communities, we are renowned for our leadership in fire protection engineering – a legacy of responsibility we have proudly upheld since 1939. Today, our expertise extends broadly across closely related security and risk-based fields – from accessibility consulting and risk analysis to process safety, forensic investigations, security risk consulting, emergency management, digital innovation and more.

Our engineers and consultants collaborate to solve complex safety and security challenges, ensuring our clients can protect what matters most. For over 80 years, we have helped mitigate risks that threaten lives, property and reputations. Through technology, expertise and industry-leading research, we remain dedicated to our purpose of making our world safe, secure and resilient.

At Jensen Hughes, we believe that creating and sustaining a culture of trust, integrity and professional growth starts with putting our people first. Our employees are our greatest strength, and we value the unique perspectives and talents they bring to our organization.

Our wide range of Global Employee Networks connect people from across the organization, supporting career development and providing forums for individuals to share experiences on topics they're passionate about. Together, we are cultivating a connected culture where everyone has the opportunity to learn, grow and succeed together.

Job Overview

Jensen Hughes is seeking an experienced Talent Acquisition Partner to join our North America team. This role will support priority hiring needs for specialized engineering and technical positions across multiple states in our South region. Candidates should ideally be based in the Mountain, Central or Eastern time zones and be available to collaborate during the hiring team’s core business hours.

The Talent Acquisition Partner will own the full recruiting process, from translating hiring requirements into targeted sourcing strategies to engaging and qualifying candidates, coordinating interviews, managing candidate communications, supporting offers, and facilitating successful placements.

The ideal candidate is a resourceful, persistent, and data-minded talent acquisition professional who excels at finding specialized, hard-to-reach talent, building credibility with passive candidates, and converting sourcing activity into qualified candidate pipelines.

Responsibilities

Strategic Sourcing & Talent Pipeline Development

  • Develop and execute targeted sourcing strategies for priority engineering and technical positions across multiple states in the South region
  • Identify and engage passive candidates through LinkedIn Recruiter, professional associations, industry networks, referrals, and other relevant channels
  • Conduct talent mapping to identify target organizations, geographic talent pools, adjacent industries, and candidates with transferable skills
  • Build and maintain qualified pipelines aligned with current and anticipated hiring needs
  • Create personalized outreach campaigns and test alternative approaches to improve candidate engagement and response rates
  • Refine sourcing strategies based on market conditions, candidate feedback, and pipeline results

Recruiting & Candidate Engagement

  • Conduct initial outreach and qualification conversations to assess candidates’ experience, career interests, location or mobility considerations, compensation expectations, and alignment with available opportunities
  • Present the Jensen Hughes employee value proposition and provide an accurate, engaging overview of the opportunities
  • Maintain timely, professional follow-up with prospective candidates to sustain engagement and deliver a positive candidate experience
  • Coordinate interviews, manage candidate communications, support offers, and facilitate successful placements while continuing to develop qualified talent pipelines
  • Actively participate in university recruiting efforts, including attending career fairs within the South region

Collaboration & Stakeholder Partnership

  • Partner with hiring leaders to understand technical requirements, target candidate profiles, hiring priorities, and market constraints
  • Recommend target organizations, professional networks, geographic markets, and sourcing channels based on talent market intelligence
  • Provide concise, regular updates on sourcing activity, pipeline health, candidate feedback, market insights, and barriers to hiring
  • Use hiring leader feedback to refine candidate profiles and adjust sourcing strategies promptly as hiring needs or market conditions change

Data Management & Reporting

  • Maintain accurate and timely candidate records, outreach activity, qualification notes, and pipeline status in Greenhouse and LinkedIn Recruiter
  • Track and report sourcing metrics, including outreach volume, response rate, qualified-candidate submissions, pipeline conversion, and candidate progression
  • Use sourcing data and market feedback to identify trends, evaluate effectiveness, and recommend changes to the sourcing approach
  • Comply with applicable recruiting policies, data privacy requirements, and employment regulations

Qualifications

Required

  • 5+ years of experience in technical recruiting and sourcing, preferably in a corporate or agency environment
  • Experience recruiting and sourcing engineering, architecture, construction, consulting, or other technical professionals
  • Demonstrated success identifying, engaging, and qualifying passive candidates for specialized or hard-to-fill positions
  • Advanced proficiency with LinkedIn Recruiter, AI-assisted search techniques, Boolean search, and alternative sourcing methods
  • Experience building targeted sourcing strategies and managing candidate pipelines against defined hiring priorities
  • Strong written and verbal communication, relationship-building, and candidate engagement skills
  • Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and deliver results in a fast-paced remote environment
  • Experience using applicant tracking systems (preferably Greenhouse or similar) and maintaining complete, accurate candidate data
  • Analytical approach to measuring sourcing effectiveness and adjusting strategy based on results

Preferred

  • Familiarity with fire protection, mechanical, electrical, or related engineering disciplines
  • Experience sourcing senior-level engineering professionals, licensed Professional Engineers (PEs), and niche technical specialists
  • Experience conducting talent mapping, competitor research, and talent market analysis
  • Experience supporting geographically dispersed hiring teams and multiple business priorities

description:

Senior Finance Business Partner, AOS Finance
