Position Overview

One of the adjacencies that Autodesk is expanding into is Operations, by extending our AI-powered clouds into the entire lifecycle of buildings, factories and infrastructure. Autodesk Operations Solutions (AOS) is the group building that business, and it will grow through both organic investment and acquisition.

We're hiring a Senior Finance Business Partner to join the AOS finance team to help build and grow this business into a significant part of Autodesk’s portfolio. You'll report to the Director of AOS Finance and work with the AOS leadership team. You'll partner with AOS leaders on planning, forecasting, and financial insights, and you'll support the financial modeling for M&A opportunities and the integration of acquired companies into Autodesk.

You'll influence senior leaders on strategic, investment, and operational decisions through financial analysis. You're comfortable with ambiguity, you adapt quickly, and you solve problems across cross-functional teams.

Responsibilities

  • Business partnering. Advise the AOS leadership team on investment trade-offs, resource prioritization, and ROI. Prepare quarterly business reviews and executive and Board materials that turn the numbers into a clear message.
  • Financial analysis and modeling. Develop financial analyses and models to influence business decisions (pricing & packaging for subscription and consumption models, business cases, etc.)
  • Planning and forecasting. Run annual plan, quarterly and monthly forecasts, and long-range model for ARR, ACV, revenue, headcount, and expense.
  • M&A financial modeling. Build and own financial models for acquisition, partnership, and build-versus-buy opportunities, including scenario and sensitivity analysis. Support projections for acquisition targets, including expansion, retention, pricing, and synergies. Partner with Corporate Development, and AOS leadership on the business case and financial due diligence.
  • Post-close integration. Lead the FP&A workstream for newly acquired companies: align financial structure, ARR and other metric definitions, and reporting; bring the acquired team into Autodesk's planning and forecast cadence; and report integration progress and deal performance against the original thesis to leadership.
  • Topline reporting and analysis. Develop and report on topline financial metrics to measure financial performance. Analyze financial results, distilling/synthesizing key trends
  • Spend management. Track AOS spend and headcount against plan, explain variances, and support the business on budget management.
  • Process and tooling. Improve the models, reporting, and automation that AOS finance relies on, and make acquired-company data easier to onboard each time. Look for practical ways to use AI to speed up analysis, reporting, and forecasting

Minimum Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience in financial planning & analysis, strategic finance, investment banking, or management consulting, ideally including time at a software company
  • Proven ability to influence and collaborate with cross functional leaders, including senior executives
  • Advanced financial modeling skills including experience building M&A financial models
  • Strong experience with SaaS metrics and revenue modeling (ARR, retention, bookings and billings, pricing and packaging); consumption-based model experience a plus
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with a knack for distilling complexity into executive ready insights
  • Experience working in a global, matrixed environment
  • Solution-driven, innovative, and creative mindset
  • Proven track record of financial systems, process & tools improvement/automation
  • Curiosity about AI and an interest in using it to improve how finance works
  • Bachelor’s degree in finance, business, accounting, economics; MBA preferred

Partenaire d’affaires principal en finance, AOS Finance


Aperçu du poste

L’un des secteurs connexes dans lesquels Autodesk se développe est celui des opérations, en étendant nos solutions cloud basées sur l’IA à l’ensemble du cycle de vie des bâtiments, des usines et des infrastructures. Autodesk Operations Solutions (AOS) est le groupe chargé de développer cette activité, qui se renforcera à la fois par des investissements organiques et par des acquisitions.

Nous recherchons un partenaire d’affaires principal en finances pour rejoindre l’équipe financière d’AOS afin de contribuer à l’établissement et à la croissance de cette activité, qui deviendra un élément important du portefeuille d’Autodesk. Vous relèverez du directeur des finances d’AOS et travaillerez avec l’équipe de direction d’AOS. Vous collaborerez avec les dirigeants d’AOS en matière de planification, de prévisions et d’analyses financières, et vous contribuerez à l’élaboration de modèles financiers pour les occasions de fusion et d’acquisition ainsi qu’à l’intégration des entreprises acquises au sein d’Autodesk.

Vous influencerez les hauts dirigeants dans leurs décisions stratégiques, d’investissement et opérationnelles grâce à vos analyses financières. Vous êtes à l’aise avec l’ambiguïté, vous vous adaptez rapidement et vous résolvez des problèmes au sein d’équipes interfonctionnelles.


Responsabilités

  • Partenariat d’affaires. Conseiller l’équipe de direction d’AOS sur les compromis en matière d’investissement, la hiérarchisation des ressources et le rendement du capital investi (RCI). Préparer des revues d’affaires trimestrielles ainsi que des documents destinés à la haute direction et au conseil d’administration qui transforment les chiffres en un message clair.
  • Analyse et modélisation financières. Élaborer des analyses et des modèles financiers pour orienter les décisions d’affaires (tarification et offres pour les modèles d’abonnement et de consommation, analyses de rentabilité, etc.)
  • Planification et prévisions. Établir le plan annuel, les prévisions trimestrielles et mensuelles, ainsi qu’un modèle à long terme pour le chiffre d’affaires récurrent annuel (ARR), la valeur contractuelle annuelle (ACV), les revenus, l’effectif et les dépenses.
  • Modélisation financière des fusions et acquisitions. Élaborer et gérer des modèles financiers pour les acquisitions, les partenariats et les opportunités « faire soi-même ou acheter », y compris des analyses de scénarios et de sensibilité. Appuyer les projections relatives aux cibles d’acquisition, notamment en matière d’expansion, de fidélisation, de tarification et de synergies. Collaborer avec le service de développement d’entreprise et la direction d’AOS sur l’analyse de rentabilité et la vérification financière préalable.
  • Intégration post-clôture. Diriger le volet FP&A pour les entreprises nouvellement acquises : harmoniser la structure financière, les définitions de l’ARR et d’autres indicateurs, ainsi que le reporting; intégrer l’équipe acquise au rythme de planification et de prévision d’Autodesk; et rendre compte à la direction des progrès de l’intégration et de la performance de la transaction par rapport à l’hypothèse initiale.
  • Rapports et analyses des résultats financiers globaux. Élaborer et présenter des rapports sur les indicateurs financiers globaux afin de mesurer la performance financière. Analyser les résultats financiers, en identifiant et en synthétisant les tendances clés
  • Gestion des dépenses. Suivre les dépenses et l’effectif d’AOS par rapport au plan, expliquer les écarts et soutenir l’entreprise dans la gestion budgétaire.
  • Processus et outils. Améliorer les modèles, les rapports et l’automatisation sur lesquels s’appuie le service des finances d’AOS, et faciliter l’intégration des données des entreprises acquises à chaque fois. Rechercher des moyens pratiques d’utiliser l’IA pour accélérer l’analyse, la production de rapports et les prévisions

Qualifications Minimales

  • Au moins 8 ans d’expérience en planification et analyse financières, en finance stratégique, en services bancaires d’investissement ou en conseil en gestion, idéalement avec une expérience au sein d’une entreprise de logiciels
  • Capacité avérée à influencer et à collaborer avec des dirigeants de divers secteurs fonctionnels, y compris des cadres supérieurs
  • Compétences avancées en modélisation financière, y compris une expérience dans l’élaboration de modèles financiers liés aux fusions et acquisitions
  • Solide expérience des indicateurs SaaS et de la modélisation des revenus (ARR, fidélisation, prises de commandes et facturation, tarification et offres); une expérience des modèles basés sur la consommation constitue un atout
  • Excellentes compétences en communication écrite et verbale, avec un talent particulier pour transformer des informations complexes en aperçus clairs et prêts à être présentés à la haute direction
  • Expérience de travail dans un environnement international et matriciel
  • Esprit axé sur les solutions, innovant et créatif
  • Expérience avérée en matière d’amélioration et d’automatisation des systèmes, des processus et des outils financiers
  • Curiosité à l’égard de l’IA et intérêt pour son utilisation afin d’améliorer le fonctionnement des services financiers
  • Baccalauréat en finance, en administration des affaires, en comptabilité ou en économie; un MBA est un atout

title: Staff Security Operations Specialist
description:
About ShareGate

ShareGate is the leading Microsoft 365 migration and governance platform, trusted by over 100,000 IT pros for its unmatched simplicity.

It offers the simplest, most reliable, and most affordable way to move business data to Microsoft 365.

Whether migrating from Google Workspace, file shares, Exchange Online, SharePoint On-Premises, or tenant-to-tenant, ShareGate gets the job done, without surprises. From cloud transformation to M&A integration, it keeps things just damn simple.

ShareGate also helps organizations stay in control once their data is migrated. Its powerful governance features let users assess environments, uncover issues, and apply fixes on the spot, so everything stays clean, secure, and optimized. It lays the groundwork for safe Microsoft Copilot deployment within organizations.

ShareGate is developed by Workleap Technologies, a Montréal‑based software company.

Your role

You will own how Workleap detects, investigates and responds to threats across Workleap and ShareGate, and you will build the AI layer that runs it. Our security tooling generates more noise than a small team can work, and too many findings are ambiguous or wrong. This role exists now to turn detection and response into a system where agents triage, enrich and investigate, and people make the calls that genuinely need judgment. It is a hands on Staff individual contributor role with no direct reports.

Your impact:

  • Build the pipeline that runs security operations end to end: integrations that pull alerts and findings out of every source tool, an agentic system that triages, enriches, correlates and drafts the investigation, and a connection into Jira that routes each result to the owning team with evidence and a fix path, so no finding is ever copied by hand.
  • Define the trust model for those agents, deciding what they close alone, what they recommend and what always goes to a human, backed by evals and secured against prompt injection and permission abuse.
  • Drive false positives and misrated findings out of our security tooling, so every finding that reaches a person is real and correctly prioritized.
  • Own detection engineering end to end, written as code and mapped to MITRE ATT&CK, so coverage survives any change of platform.
  • Lead security incident response from triage to postmortem, with agents gathering the evidence, and hold our managed detection partner to a measurable standard.
  • Make security a partner developers want to work with, delivering findings in their workflow with clear evidence and a fix path.

Your team

Over the next 12 months, LeapSec is delivering two strategic bets: putting security inside product squads, with agents carrying vulnerability and detection work, and automating SOC 2 evidence so nobody gathers it by hand. You will own the detection and response side of that work: cleaning up the tooling, building the agents, and proving how much they can be trusted to do alone.

LeapSec covers Security Operations and Compliance across Workleap and ShareGate. You will report to the Director of Infrastructure and Security and work daily with our Staff Application Security Specialist and security tooling team, and as needed with Infrastructure, ITX and product engineering. We are a small team with a wide mandate: we track work honestly in Jira, deliver on fixed dates, and expect people to own outcomes end to end.

Our environment is Azure first, with a cloud native SIEM and XDR stack, Zscaler, Cloudflare and a managed detection partner today. We choose tools on merit and expect to keep choosing.

What you'll bring

  • 7+ years in security operations, incident response or detection engineering, with recent hands on time in a cloud SaaS environment;
  • Deep experience working findings that are not clean: validating what tooling flags, tuning false positives out at the source, and deciding with incomplete evidence whether something is real;
  • Years of working directly with developers, getting fixes shipped without authority and keeping the relationship intact when the answer is no;
  • Built and shipped agent systems for security work that others depend on, such as MCP servers, Claude skills, subagents or custom tools, with evals that decide when the output is trusted;
  • A working model of how agentic systems fail and get attacked, including prompt injection, tool permission scoping and credential handling;
  • Detection engineering as a discipline: detections as code, a SIEM query language you write fluently, and false positive rates you actually measure;
  • Strong grasp of identity and cloud attack paths, ideally in Azure and Entra ID;
  • Bonus: experience directing a managed detection partner, threat hunting or forensics, and working proficiency in French.

Most of this sounds like you? Apply.

What the job comes with

  • Base salary: $125 000 - $160 000.This range reflects our Canada-wide compensation scale.Final offers may be adjusted based on the candidate's region to align with local market conditions.
  • Annual bonus program.
  • LTIP program, share in Workleap's long-term growth.
  • RRSP + Family health insurance + telemedicine + annual wellness budget.
  • Flexible vacation policy.
  • Remote work, with access to our Montreal office.
  • In-person gatherings twice a year.
  • Claude access, for everyone.

What drives us

We build software that sits at the center of how people experience work, every day, at every level.

We move fast. Priorities shift, decisions get made with the information we have, and we iterate. If you thrive on intensity and ambiguity doesn't slow you down, you'll feel right at home.
We're builders. We do what it takes to move forward. AI is part of our toolkit. We use it to go faster and decide smarter, not to replace judgment.

If you want real impact and a place where your decisions matter, this is it.

How we hire

Transparency is how we hire — for you as much as for us.

Here's how it works: a first call with a recruiter, then a virtual interview with the hiring manager. You'll then complete a take-home case study, followed by a meet with future colleagues to discuss it together. Depending on the role, the process may vary slightly — your recruiter will walk you through it on your first call.

We use AI to support certain steps of the process, but every hiring decision remains human.

We can't wait to meet you.

By applying, you confirm that you have read and agree to our privacy policy.

title: Head of Anti-Fraud
description:
Hi! We'reMercuryo, and we’re on a mission to redefine finance by blending the best of traditional banking with the power of decentralized finance (DeFi). We believe everyone deserves seamless access to Web3 and traditional financial services, so we're building the platform that makes it real: one that simplifies crypto and integrates it into the broader financial ecosystem.

Since launching in 2018, we've grown into a recognized force in the industry, named one of Europe's Fastest-Growing Startups 2025 by Sifted and awarded Best Crypto On-Ramp & Payments Solution 2025 by Cryptonomist. We've partnered with leading brands including Visa, Mastercard, MetaMask, Trust Wallet, Ledger, and Jupiter, powering over 200 products and collaborating directly with major ecosystems like Solana, Consensys, and BNB Chain.

Why Mercuryo?

Industry Impact

Join us in helping world-class Web3 projects onboard millions of new users into the next generation of finance.

Innovative Environment

Collaborate with more than 300 talented professionals from diverse backgrounds — including banking, SaaS, and Web3 — all united in delivering outstanding user experiences.

AI-First Culture

We actively integrate AI across the company, from operations and analytics to marketing and product workflows. It helps teams move faster, improve productivity, and focus on high-impact work - while maintaining human oversight and accountability at every step. We see AI as a core part of how our teams innovate, collaborate, and scale.

Growth and Learning

Our expanding network of 200+ B2B partnerships and a user base of over 7 million means there’s always room to grow your skills, tackle new challenges, and push boundaries.

Flexible Culture

We’re remote-first, celebrating diversity across 30 countries. At Mercuryo, you’ll be empowered to take ownership of your work, spark creativity, and shape how we move forward together.

About the role

The Head of Anti-Fraud runs Mercuryo's fraud prevention function and reports directly to the Head of AML Operations. The role owns fraud risk across the on/off-ramp widget, wallet, swaps and card acquiring pay-ins and pay-outs: detection rules, investigations, chargeback and card scheme exposure, and checking that partners and merchants use our products only where we approved them.

We need an experienced, hands-on leader who has run large-scale fraud investigations, can find weaknesses in controls, and can redesign the procedures, rules and tooling to close them. Detailed knowledge of Visa and Mastercard rules is essential, in particular the programmes covering merchant integrity, fraud and dispute ratios, and transaction laundering.

Your Role:

Investigations

  • Lead complex and large-scale fraud investigations: linked-account networks, card testing, mule activity, account takeover, scams, and merchant or partner collusion.
  • Set the investigation standard: one case record per subject with linked history, closure deadlines, root-cause analysis, and evidence that stands up to an acquirer, a card scheme or an auditor.
  • Act on findings by changing rules, restricting or offboarding merchants and partners, and escalating suspicion to Transaction Monitoring and the MLRO.

Rules, controls and procedures

  • Own the anti-fraud rule set: design, impact testing before release, documented approval, a rule register, and regular effectiveness and false-positive reviews.
  • Find where controls fail or can be bypassed, and redesign them.
  • Write and maintain the anti-fraud procedures and the fraud risk assessment, and be able to show that each control works as written.
  • Build and run the AML alert and block rules that Transaction Monitoring and Compliance request on the anti-fraud platform, including for card acquiring, with fraud and AML rules kept separate in the register and each assigned an owner.

Card schemes, acquirers and chargebacks

  • Keep every acquirer relationship and MID within Visa and Mastercard fraud and dispute thresholds, with early warning before a limit is reached.
  • Lead the anti-fraud response to Visa and Mastercard notices and programme identifications within scheme deadlines.
  • Act as the anti-fraud lead with our acquiring partners: respond to RFIs with evidence, agree remediation plans, and complete due diligence questionnaires.
  • Own chargebacks and disputes: representment, pre-arbitration, deadlines and win rates, supported by tooling and pre-dispute alerts.

Merchant and partner integrity

  • Build and run the programme that detects and stops partners and merchants offering our widget or payment links on websites we have not approved, including through resellers, aggregators, iframes and redirects.
  • Select and manage a merchant monitoring and transaction laundering detection provider, and set how its alerts are triaged, actioned and evidenced.
  • Agree with KYB, Integrations, Legal and Acquiring what follows confirmed misuse (blocking, takedown, contractual remedies, offboarding and reporting), and check that each action has taken effect.

Leadership and reporting

  • Lead and develop the Anti-Fraud team of specialists, analysts, chargeback and fraud operations staff, based in several countries.
  • Report fraud losses, chargeback and fraud ratios, scheme exposure, incidents and control status to the Head of AML Operations, senior management and the Board.
  • Keep the incident register, and close audit, QA and compliance monitoring findings with evidence.
  • Work with Product and Engineering so new products, markets and merchants have fraud controls in place before launch.

What We're Looking For:

  • At least 8 years in fraud prevention in payments, card acquiring, a PSP or EMI, or crypto, including at least 3 years leading a fraud team or function, preferably one spread across several countries.
  • Has personally led large-scale fraud investigations from detection to resolution, such as card-testing attacks, mule networks, account takeover rings or merchant collusion, and produced evidence for acquirers, card schemes or law enforcement.
  • Has redesigned fraud controls and procedures after an audit, a scheme notice or a major incident, and can show the effect on losses and ratios.
  • Has handled acquirer RFIs, remediation plans and scheme programme cases directly.

Visa and Mastercard programmes

  • Visa: VAMP, VIRP, TC40 fraud reporting, dispute rules including Compelling Evidence 3.0, and the pre-dispute tools Order Insight and RDR.
  • Mastercard: ECP, EFM, the Global Merchant Audit Program (GMAP) due in April 2027, BRAM, GRIP, the Scam Merchant Monitoring Program, the Merchant Monitoring Program and its registered providers, Fraud and Loss Database (SAFE) reporting, MATCH and Ethoca alerts.
  • How these rules apply to a crypto merchant of record (MCC 6051) whose payments are offered through partners and resellers, including exposure from transaction laundering.
  • 3-D Secure and Strong Customer Authentication, including exemptions and liability shift.

Fraud controls, data and detection

  • Has owned a rules-based fraud engine: rules, lists, velocity limits, device fingerprinting, BIN and geo controls, with back-testing or shadow mode before release.
  • Writes SQL, builds dashboards in Metabase or a similar tool, and analyses large transaction datasets personally.
  • Has designed detection for transaction laundering and unauthorised website use, including test purchases through multi-step checkouts, redirect and referrer analysis, and measurement of a monitoring provider's detection rate and false positives.
  • Has run a fraud risk assessment covering external and internal fraud, using COSO or ACFE fraud risk guidance.

Governance and AML

  • Writes clear procedures that pass internal audit and regulator review, and keeps evidence that controls operate as written.
  • Understands where fraud meets AML, including mule networks, SAR escalation and sanctions screening, and has built AML controls on a fraud platform.
  • Gets engineering priority for control work by presenting clear data on losses and scheme exposure.
  • Fluent written and spoken English.

Nice-to-have:

  • Crypto on/off-ramp, exchange or wallet experience, including blockchain analytics such as Chainalysis in fraud and scam investigations.
  • Merchant risk experience at an acquirer or payment facilitator: underwriting, ongoing merchant monitoring and terminations.
  • Chargeback management platforms and automated dispute evidence.
  • Website takedowns through hosting providers and registrars.
  • Scam victim handling, including authorised push payment fraud.
  • CFE, CAMS or an equivalent qualification.

What We Offer:

  • Competitive market rate salary and performance-based incentives.
  • 22 days annual leave with an additional 6 company days, plus bank holidays.
  • Comprehensive health insurance plans.
  • Maternity & Paternity leave support.
  • Extensive benefits program.
  • Flexible work schedule and remote work options.
  • Modern offices and co-working spaces across 6 countries.
  • Working equipment.
  • Professional development and training opportunities.
  • Opportunity to shape the initiatives you’re working on.
  • Diverse and friendly team.
  • We are open-minded to new ideas.

Join Us!

If you're driven to be a part of the Web3 forefront and are keen to leave your mark on this rapidly evolving field, Mercuryo is an excellent choice. Discover our open positions and see how you can contribute to shaping the future!

Who We Are

We match standout professionals across Latin America with high-impact opportunities at leading U.S. companies. Joining Jobsity is about finding a rewarding remote role and working with innovative teams. It also means you get to become part of a community that values your experience, supports your ambition, and invests in your ongoing professional growth.

Whether you are looking for your next challenge, seeking greater flexibility, or ready to elevate your career, Jobsity gives you the platform and partnership to thrive on your terms.

Job Description

We are looking for a Go Backend Engineer to own projects end-to-end, building event-driven backend services and integrations between the client's systems and third-party partners. You’ll work directly with product to break down requirements, design and deliver solutions, give timelines, and escalate only when truly blocked, while also reviewing code and mentoring junior and mid-level engineers. The role requires 8+ years of backend experience, deep expertise in asynchronous systems and Kafka, and production experience with AWS, GraphQL, and Datadog.

Responsibilities

  • Own projects end to end, from breaking down requirements with product to design, delivery and follow-up in production

  • Design and build backend services and event-driven integrations between the client's systems and third-party partners

  • Design event schemas and data models that keep asynchronous systems reliable and consistent

  • Review AI-generated and peer code with a focus on correctness, maintainability, and data quality

  • Produce design docs and diagrams, and explain technical tradeoffs to product and non-technical stakeholders

  • Provide timelines and effort estimates, and escalate risks early

  • Switch between languages and codebases as priorities shift, including fixing urgent defects outside your primary stack

  • Support less senior engineers through pairing and code review

Key Requirements

  • 8+ years of professional software engineering experience building production backend systems

  • 5+ years of backend development in GO and at least one more language like .NET, Node.js, or Python, plus a proven willingness to pick up the others when the work requires it.

  • Hands-on production experience with AWS, including Lambda, S3, EKS (Kubernetes) and CloudFront, plus infrastructure as code with Terraform or CloudFormation.

  • Production experience with Kafka or equivalent event streaming platforms, including partitioning strategy, consumer group scaling, and schema registries.

  • Hands-on experience designing and serving GraphQL APIs with Apollo or Hasura, including schema federation and resolver performance optimization.

  • Strong relational data modeling with production experience in PostgreSQL or MySQL and NoSQL stores such as DynamoDB or MongoDB.

  • Experience implementing observability with Datadog or comparable APM tooling (dashboards, alerting, SLO/SLI tracking).

  • Experience building and maintaining Jenkins CI/CD pipelines, including pipeline as code and deployment automation.

  • Practical, daily use of AI coding tools such as Claude Code in development workflows.

  • Strong system design and architecture skills, including leading design reviews and RFCs.

  • Experience mentoring junior and mid-level engineers.

What We Offer

At Jobsity, we know that a positive professional experience goes beyond the role itself.

Depending on the position, client, country, and type of contract, professionals may have access to different benefits, programs, and resources designed to support their well-being, development, and remote-work experience.

These may include:

● Paid time off or vacation days

● Paid holidays, depending on the client and country

● Professional development and learning opportunities

● Ongoing support from our People Experience team

● Recognition initiatives and internal activities

● Remote-work flexibility

● Opportunities to collaborate with international teams

● Access to tools and resources that support your work

● Career growth opportunities based on performance, business needs, and available roles

Because each opportunity is different, the specific benefits associated with a position will always be communicated during the recruitment process.

title: Operations Associate (Hiring or Client Delivery)
description:
Grow our AI image service.

The role

We are Drop Zero Digital, a lifecycle marketing agency. We are hiring one person who is good at deciding. Our AI image service is our fastest-growing service, and whichever area you own, you will be helping it grow.

You will own one named area. Which one is decided during the trial rather than now, based on what you turn out to be strong at. It will be one of these two:

  1. The hiring machine. How we find, screen and hire people. Running the funnel end to end, sourcing, chasing, scheduling, keeping our tracker honest, and telling us when the process itself is broken.
  2. Client delivery operations. How work gets planned, briefed, chased and shipped for our clients. Holding timelines, briefing the team properly, and making sure nothing quietly stalls.

Both are the same job underneath: you notice what has slipped, you decide what to do, and you close it without being asked.

This is not an assistant job and it is not a coordinator job. You will make real calls every day, and you will be judged on the quality of those calls rather than on how much you got through.

We are building a team of people who decide well without being managed. If you want to be told what to do each morning, this job is not for you.

What we are looking for

  1. You make decisions and you own them, including the ones that go wrong.
  2. You can tell which calls are yours and which are not, and you get that split right in both directions.
  3. You take feedback as information and change, without folding on something you have good reason to believe.
  4. You get better fast. We would rather have someone at seventy percent climbing than someone flat at eighty five.
  5. You spot when something is failing and say so, including when it is our process and not your work.
  6. You write clearly and honestly, especially about problems.

On experience

We do not ask for a number of years and we do not screen on your CV, because we decide on what you do in the trial.

Whatever employment you do list, we verify: employer, dates, title and paid status, evidenced by contract and payslips, in one exchange. You need to have held a full-time job at some point in the last 12 months. Beyond that there is no minimum, and a short history costs you nothing here. Misrepresenting the history you do have is disqualifying. Tell us the true version and you will not be penalised for it.

How the process works, and we tell you all of it now

  1. Application with a short Loom video.
  2. A short written step: your internet speed, your computer, and a few questions in your own words.
  3. Aptitude tests, with a published floor.
  4. A recorded video interview. One take, no re-records. We verify the work history you've told us about.
  5. A short call with the founder.
  6. A paid trial of six to eight weeks doing the real job.

The trial is where the decision actually gets made, including which of the two areas you end up owning. From the first week you will be making calls on live work, and we will tell you straight how each one landed. It is paid from day one: half rate for the first two weeks while you find your feet, full rate from week three onward, and a completion payment when you finish the trial, whether or not we hire you. If we stop early, you are paid for the days you worked.

Requirements

    1. Full time once hired, and this is your only job. During the paid trial you work 4 hours a day with us, 2 of them at a fixed time inside our working day, and you can keep your current job. If you pass, you give notice and join us full time within 30 days.
    2. Reliable internet, at least 30 Mbps down and 5 Mbps up, tested live with us.
    3. Strong written English.
    4. Based in South Africa.
    5. You track your working time with our time tracking tool from day one.

Benefits

1300 USD per month on hire, set by responsibility and demonstrated capability, not by how long you have worked.

Pass your 90-day review and your pay goes up by 50 percent. The 90 days count from the day you start full time.

On top of that:

  1. A one-month annual bonus.
  2. 15 days of paid leave a year, rising with tenure, plus your own country's public holidays.
  3. Paid sick leave.
  4. A health allowance.
  5. A coworking allowance.

Responsibility and pay move quickly here for people who earn them. Authority over decisions that reach a client moves slowly and deliberately, and it is earned on a track record rather than on a good first month. We would rather tell you that now than have you discover it in month two.

Pay

$0.04 per accepted photo. At a typical pace of about 8 seconds per photo, that is about $18 per hour. A 20-minute session of about 150 photos pays about $6.00. Up to 100 photos per upload. Where and when

Open worldwide: the task runs in 100+ countries. Remote, on your own schedule. Independent contractor, piecework; this is not an employment position.

What you need

How to start

title: Product Marketing Manager
description:
What We’re Building

Honeycomb is a service for the near and present future, defining observability and raising expectations of what developer tools can do! We’re working with well known companies like HelloFresh, Slack, LaunchDarkly, and Vanguard and more across a range of industries. This is an exciting time in our trajectory, we’ve closed Series D funding, scaled past the 200-person mark, and were named to Forbes’ America’s Best Startups of 2022 and 2023!
If you want to see what we’ve been up to, please check out these blog posts and Honeycomb.io press releases.

Who We Are

We come for the impact, and stay for the culture! We’re a talented, opinionated, passionate, fiercely inclusive, and responsible group of bees. We have conviction and we strive to live our values every day. We want our people to do what they truly love amongst a team of highly talented (but humble) peers.

How We Work

We are a fully distributed company, which means we believe it is not where you sit, but how you deliver that matters most. We invest in our people and care about how you orient to our culture and processes. At the same time we imbue a lot of trust, autonomy, and accountability from Day 1.

Little more about the team:

Product marketing at Honeycomb is a small team with a wide surface area. We decide how Honeycomb is positioned, what we say at launch, what the sales team brings into a deal, and how an engineer who has never heard of us understands the product in the first two minutes. Because the team is small, the work is broad: in one week you might rewrite a product page, build a competitive one-pager, interview a customer, and run the launch checklist for a new feature.

This role is built for someone early in a product marketing career who wants to systematically improve the customer buying journey. As a product and messaging expert, you will partner with go-to-market teams to drive business impact through sales and marketing campaigns. You will get real ownership of real launches, and you will have senior product marketers, a technical field team, and engineers who like explaining their work close at hand. Our audience is engineers and platform teams, so the bar is accuracy first: we would rather be precise and useful than clever.

What you’ll do in the role:

You will support and execute product marketing across Honeycomb's core products, with a generalist mix of messaging, launches, content, enablement, and competitive work. Expect to start by contributing to pieces of each and to own more of them over your first year.

Responsibilities

  • Messaging and positioning: Write and maintain messaging for features and product areas, from the one-sentence version an engineer reads on a web page to the slide a sales engineer uses in a technical conversation. Keep it accurate and grounded in what the product actually does.
  • Launches: Run launch execution for small and mid-sized releases and support the larger ones. Build the plan, write the assets, coordinate Product, Marketing, Sales Engineering, and Customer Success, and report on how the launch performed.
  • Content: Produce the practical material that helps people evaluate and adopt Honeycomb: blog posts, solution briefs, web copy, demo scripts, FAQs, and customer-facing one-pagers.
  • Sales enablement: Equip the field with what they need to run a good conversation, including pitch narratives, objection handling, battlecards, and release updates. Join customer calls, listen to recorded ones, and fix the material that isn't landing.
  • Competitive and market intelligence: Track the observability market and competitor moves. Maintain competitive assets and keep them current and honest, so the field trusts them.
  • Voice of customer and proof points: Talk to customers and prospects, turn what you hear into case studies, quotes, and proof points, and bring the patterns back to Product and Marketing.
  • Measurement: Help define what success looks like for your work, pull the data, and share what you learn, including the things that didn't work.

What you’ll bring to the role:

  • 2 to 5 years of experience in product marketing, or in a closely adjacent go-to-market role such as content marketing, sales engineering, technical writing, developer relations, or product management, with at least some of it in B2B SaaS.
  • Strong writing. You can take a dense technical explanation and turn it into something short, accurate, and useful, and you can tell the difference between the two yourself.
  • Curiosity about technical products and the patience to learn how they work. You ask engineers questions until you actually understand the answer, and you are comfortable in a product that assumes a technical user.
  • Passion about the team winning: Sales, marketing, and product teams will depend on you to succeed. Their success is your success, but you’re not simply an order taker: you look for the smart solutions and don’t wait to be asked.
  • The ability to run a project across teams without formal authority: setting a timeline, chasing the open items, and telling people clearly when something has slipped.
  • Comfort with ambiguity and a bias toward shipping. Our priorities move, the team is small, and the best work here comes from people who start rather than wait for a brief.
  • Willingness to use data to decide and to evaluate your own work honestly.
  • Demonstrated experience applying AI tooling in your work.

Nice to have

  • Exposure to observability, developer tools, distributed tracing, OpenTelemetry, platform engineering, or reliability and SLO practices. We will teach this, but a head start helps.
  • Experience marketing to engineers as the primary audience.
  • Hands-on familiarity with AI and LLM tooling, including coding agents and MCP-based workflows.
  • Experience with webinars, conference talks, or community programs.
  • Experience working in a fully distributed company.
Base Salary based on level of experience
$125,000—$190,000 USD

What you'll get when you join the Hive:

  • A stake in our success - generous equity with employee-friendly stock program
  • It’s not about how strong of a negotiator you are - our pay is based on transparent levels relative to experience
  • Time to recharge with unlimited PTO
  • A distributed-first mindset and culture (really!)
  • Home office, co-working, and internet stipend
  • Full benefits coverage for employees, with additional coverage available for dependents
  • Up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave, regardless of path to parenthood
  • Annual development allowance
  • And much more...
Please note we cannot currently sponsor or support visa transfers at this time. Additionally, in compliance with applicable law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work.

Phishing and Recruitment Scam Warning:

We take your security seriously. Please be aware that recruitment scams are increasingly common and scammers may create email addresses or websites to impersonate Honeycomb employees. To help protect you:
  • All communications will come from an @honeycomb.io email address
    • We occasionally work with external recruiting agencies. These partners will use legitimate business email addresses—never personal accounts like Gmail or Yahoo.
  • Our recruiting process will never ask you to provide financial or sensitive personal information, including but not limited to:
    • Social security or tax identification numbers
    • Credit card numbers
    • Bank account information

Diversity & Accommodations:

We're committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and equitable workplace—where people of all backgrounds, identities, experiences, and abilities are welcomed, valued, and supported. We recognize that there is no single path to success and embrace nontraditional career journeys and diverse perspectives as key to building stronger, more innovative teams.
We strive to ensure an inclusive experience throughout every stage of our hiring process and are happy to provide reasonable accommodations as needed. If you require accommodations or accessible formats at any point during our hiring process, please let your recruiter know.
As an equal opportunity employer our hiring process is designed to put you at ease and help you show your best work. If there’s anything we can do to improve your experience, we’re always open to feedback.

Privacy Notice:

If you apply for a job at Honeycomb and your application is unsuccessful (or you withdraw from the process or decline our offer), Honeycomb will retain your information after your application for a period of time in accordance with local laws. We retain this information for various reasons, including in case we face a legal challenge in respect of a recruitment decision, to consider you for other current or future jobs at Honeycomb, and to help us better understand, analyze and improve our recruitment processes.
For more information regarding our privacy practices please see the Honeycomb Privacy Notice.
If you do not want us to retain your information, or want us to update it, please contact . Please note, however, that we may retain some information if required by law or as necessary to protect ourselves from legal claims.

title: Lead, Reviews (Math)
description:
Mission

EdReports.org is at the forefront of the curriculum reform movement. By increasing the capacity of educators to identify and demand the highest quality curriculum, EdReports.org is both disrupting a multibillion-dollar market and transforming the way students are taught and ultimately perform. With the firm belief that what is taught matters and that all students deserve high quality materials, EdReports.org publishes free, online, evidence-rich reviews of instructional materials. Explore our organization's core competencies in greater detail here.

Planning to use Artificial Intelligence (AI) for your application, interview prep, or for other means of assistance throughout the hiring process? Click here to review our AI guidance before proceeding.

Purpose of Position

The Lead, Reviews will oversee and support the review of instructional materials within their designated content area, ensuring that reviews are evidence-rich, aligned to EdReports criteria, and meet the needs of educators and curriculum decision makers. The Lead, Reviews will collaborate with content teams and stakeholders to enhance review processes, provide expert guidance, and drive improvements in instruction across the nation.

This specific role will bring deep expertise in K–12 mathematics education to EdReports’ work, with a focus on how students develop mathematical understanding, procedural skills, and the ability to apply mathematics. The Lead will apply expertise in college- and career-ready mathematics standards, instructional shifts, learning progressions, and current research-supported practices to the review of instructional materials and related organizational initiatives. This role is well suited for someone energized by instructional materials and the review process itself, including working with educator-reviewers to examine curriculum closely, collect and analyze evidence, identify patterns, and translate findings into clear, accurate, evidence-rich written reviews. The Lead will balance this detailed individual contributor work with broader content leadership, serving as a cross-functional mathematics expert who strengthens review tools and processes and informs strategic projects and initiatives.

Key Responsibilities & Outcomes

Responsibilities:

  • Lead and support reviews of mathematics instructional materials, ensuring alignment to relevant standards, current research, and EdReports’ high-quality, evidence-based criteria. This role requires flexibility to support reviewer meetings and review activities, including late afternoon and evening availability when scheduled.
  • Apply deep expertise in K–12 mathematics, college- and career-ready standards, instructional shifts, learning progressions, and research-supported instructional practices to accurately analyze instructional materials.
  • Collaborate with internal teams to examine emerging research, trends, and best practices in mathematics education and translate findings into actionable recommendations that support the continuous improvement of instructional materials review practices.
  • Train and support educator-reviewers, ensuring consistent calibration across teams to produce reliable, evidence-rich reviews that meet EdReports’ quality benchmarks.
  • Collaborate across content teams to update and refine mathematics review tools and processes based on research, feedback, and evolving educational trends.
  • Provide expert guidance and coaching to review teams, helping them navigate the review process and build consensus on educational criteria.
  • Exercise independent judgment on complex content and review questions, resolving issues within established review standards and elevating decisions with broader strategic or organizational implications as appropriate.
  • Engage with external stakeholders, including publishers, to communicate the review process.
  • Serve as a thought leader explaining EdReports mathematics review findings to educators, districts, states, partner nonprofits, and other audiences using our resources to select curriculum.
  • Serve as a mathematics subject matter expert across EdReports, partnering cross-functionally to inform organizational projects, strategies, resources, and initiatives.
  • Other relevant duties as assigned to support the organization's strategic goals, with the expectation that all EdReports employees remain flexible and adaptable to evolving responsibilities.

Outcomes:

  • Contribute to the completion of mathematics reviews in line with [current-year] goals and KPIs.
  • Achieve 100% alignment in calibration checks across review teams by the end of each review cycle, ensuring evidence and criteria are consistently applied.
  • Implement three process improvements annually with a goal of reducing review cycle times while maintaining or improving quality.
  • Ensure 100% of reviewers complete required training and demonstrate proficiency through calibration activities and post-training assessments.
  • Spend roughly 10% of time engaging with the Brand Office on thought leadership, events, and external stakeholder education about review processes and outcomes.
  • Collaborate with colleagues on cross-functional strategic and operational initiatives.

Travel

National travel will occur related to organizational needs and for professional learning, as needed. The amount of travel will be monitored to ensure it is appropriate for both the organization and this position.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Passion for EdReports’ mission and vision, our core values, and our commitment to Diversity, Belonging, Inclusion, and Equity;
  • At least seven years of relevant professional experience in mathematics curriculum design, instruction, coaching, research, assessment, program leadership, or a related field, demonstrating deep expertise in college- and career-ready mathematics standards and instructional shifts.
  • Understanding of the K–12 mathematics education political and policy landscape.
  • Ability to analyze complex instructional materials and synthesize evidence into clear, actionable recommendations for diverse stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently lead complex initiatives and influence cross-functional stakeholders toward shared outcomes without relying on formal authority.
  • Demonstrated skill facilitating adult learning, coaching educators or colleagues, and building alignment across groups with differing perspectives or interpretations of evidence.
  • Exceptional written and spoken communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Fluency in Google Workspace and Microsoft Office (including Excel and PowerPoint).
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.
  • Residency in and authorization to work in the United States.

Preferred:

  • Additional expertise supporting Multilingual Learners or Special Populations.
  • K–12 mathematics classroom and coaching experience.
  • Experience with thought leadership, public speaking, and external engagement, including presenting complex ideas to partner organizations, funders, and stakeholders.
  • Experience with Adobe Creative Suite, Salesforce, Canvas, and online learning management platforms.
  • Master’s degree.

Salary

The salary for this position is $102,824 - $139,114 annually. At EdReports, we determine final salaries based on the role's requirements and the candidate's experience and skills, while maintaining equity within our compensation bands. To support fairness and provide opportunities for growth, we typically offer salaries at or below the midpoint of the range. All salary offers are non-negotiable to ensure consistency and equity across the organization.

Benefits

We know the importance of living a fulfilling, healthy life–both professionally and personally. That’s why some of the benefits we offer include:

  • Unlimited Discretionary Time Off (DTO) and Sick Time,
  • 21 days of paid holidays and office closure days in 2026,
  • Monthly Communications Reimbursement,
  • Initial home office and technology setup stipend,
  • EdReports pays for 90% of health care for both the employee and their immediate family, and
  • 401k that new hires become eligible for after six months of employment (includes safe harbor, employer match, etc.).

Work Authorization Requirements

All EdReports employees must reside in and be authorized to work in the United States. EdReports does not sponsor employment visas, and we are unable to consider candidates residing outside the U.S.

Physical Requirements

Work is normally performed in a remote office environment including, but not limited to standing and sitting for long periods of time; and fine-finger and hand manipulation to operate a computer and keyboard. Employee is required to have close visual acuity to perform an activity such as preparing and analyzing electronic information, transcribing, viewing a computer terminal, and extensive reading. This person will travel by car, air, or other transportation (as indicated in the Travel section) and should be able to physically withstand the demands of such travel. Employee may be required to walk for long distances at retreat venues or other relevant sites.

Core Competencies

  • COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY, BELONGING, INCLUSION, AND EQUITY: Actively welcome diverse perspectives, center equity in decision-making, foster authentic and inclusive relationships that promote a sense of belonging, confront biases to build understanding, and continuously build knowledge of systemic inequities to inform behaviors that lead to an inclusive organizational culture.
  • ACCOUNTABILITY: Proficiently organize projects aligned with overarching objectives while proactively addressing challenges; ensure timely and high-quality fulfillment of responsibilities.
  • COMMUNICATION: Effectively engage stakeholders, actively listen to others, convey information for desired results, and adapt style to foster relationships and trust.
  • CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT: Consistently reflect, seek feedback, and apply new insights; identify and implement solutions that enhance individual, team, and overall performance.
  • CORE EXPERTISE: Possess skills, knowledge, and abilities to perform essential duties; keeps knowledge current; utilize multiple points of view to achieve goals and is a subject matter resource for others.
  • ORGANIZATIONAL STEWARDSHIP: Cultivate external relationships, uphold policies, leverage historical insights, actively participate in organizational improvement, and adapt to align with the needs of the organization.

We Value All Voices

EdReports is committed to equal-employment principles and we recognize the value of committed employees who feel they are being treated in an equitable and professional manner. We strive to find ways to attract, develop, and retain the talent needed to meet business objectives, and to recruit and employ highly qualified individuals representing the diverse communities in which we live, work, and serve. As such, all employment decisions at EdReports are based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status, family or parental status, or any other status protected by the laws or regulations in the locations where we operate.

We are also committed to providing access, equal opportunity and reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities in employment, its services, programs, and activities. If you require reasonable accommodation in completing this application, interviewing, completing any pre-employment testing, or otherwise participating in the selection process, please direct your inquiries to our HR department at .

title: Senior Psychometrician
description:
About the Hiring Group

RTI Health Solutions (RTI-HS), a wholly owned subsidiary of RTI International, is an independent and internationally recognized research organization. With offices in the US, UK, Spain, France, and Sweden, we provide healthcare consulting and research expertise to optimize decision making for pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device products across the development and marketing lifecycle. Clients rely on our expertise, quality standards, and integrity to guide their product development and regulatory and market access strategies.

Our various practice areas include Value, Access, and HEOR; Patient-Centered and Outcomes Research; Epidemiology and Biostatistics; Medical Communications; Global Business Operations; and Strategic Consulting and Growth.

We are currently seeking a Senior Psychometrician to joing our Patient-Centered Outcomes Assessment (PCOA) team.

What You'll Do

RTI-HS psychometricians serve both a strategic and technical role within interdisciplinary research teams. They provide scientific leadership on the development, evaluation and application of clinical outcome assessments; guide psychometric and outcomes research strategies for clients, including participating in regulatory interactions; and are responsible designing, implementing and interpreting a variety of technical analyses.

You will be expected to:

  • Provide strategic scientific leadership on psychometric and outcomes research programs, including study design, endpoint selection, regulatory strategy, interpretation of evidence, and client decision-making.
  • Design, oversee, and conduct classical and modern psychometric analyses, interpretation of meaningful within-patient change, and advanced statistical analyses to support the development, evaluation, and regulatory acceptance of clinical outcome assessments
  • Accurately analyze, interpret, and clearly communicate psychometric results to clients within specified deadlines
  • Produce high-quality psychometric analysis plans, technical reports, and manuscripts
  • Lead and contribute to proposals, thought leadership initiatives, methodological innovation, and business development activities that support growth of the PCOA practice.
  • Communicate effectively (via email, telephone, and in-person) with clients and team members

What You'll Need

  • Master’s degree in quantitative psychology, statistics, biostatistics, or related field with at least 10 years of directly related experience, or a PhD and a minimum of 5 years of directly related experience
  • Extensive experience independently preparing psychometric analysis plans and reports of clinical outcome assessments for regulatory review
  • Demonstrated proficiency in SAS and/or R programming (expertise in both strongly preferred), along with experience using latent variable and psychometric modeling software packages.
  • Significant experience related to the psychometric evaluation of outcome measures, including classical psychometric methods (e.g., evaluations of test-retest reliability and internal consistency), exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, and Rasch Measurement and/or Item Response Theory
  • Experience implementing hierarchical linear modeling, repeated measures models, mixture models
  • Demonstrated ability to work well independently and as team leader
  • Excellent analytical and communication skills (both written and oral)
  • Experience supporting regulatory submissions and interactions with health authorities related to clinical outcome assessments, endpoint strategies, psychometric evidence, or patient-focused drug development initiatives.

title: Head of Marketplace
description:
We’re Sharp Performance

Sharp Performance exists so that everyone who answers the call has someone in their corner who has walked in their shoes.

We help first responders and their spouses thrive through confidential coaching from people with similar lived experience. Our coaches have carried the badge, worn the gear, or stood beside someone who did. Through our mobile platform, we connect law enforcement, firefighters, and other frontline professionals with coaches who understand the job because they have lived it.

We’re early-stage and backed by amazing investors. The team is small enough that your work shows up in the rollout, the product, and the customer’s experience within weeks. If building something that matters alongside people who hold a high standard sounds better than a safe seat somewhere else, come build it with us.

The Opportunity

We’re hiring a Head of Marketplace to run the system that connects first responders with the coaches who have walked in their shoes. This role reports directly to the CEO.

Sharp is a two-sided marketplace. On one side are departments and the first responders inside them. On the other are coaches who have lived the job. The Head of Marketplace owns how those two sides come together: the supply forecast that tells us how many coaches to hire and where, the matching process that takes a member from intake to first session, and the numbers that show whether the marketplace is working. Implementations get Sharp in the door and Customer Success keeps departments engaged. You make sure a coach is ready the moment a first responder reaches out.

This is a cross-functional role. You will work closely with Coaching, Product, Marketing, and Customer Success, and you will lead our Operations function: the Lead Product Analyst, all of our data efforts, and BizOps. You set the operating rhythm for the company and bring the numbers to every leadership conversation.

This role is remote within the US, with travel to Carlsbad, CA and to customer departments as the work requires.

What You’ll Own

  • Marketplace Planning: Own supply and demand forecasting. Turn the rollout calendar and department demand into coach capacity targets by discipline (law enforcement, fire, EMS, spouses) and region. Give the Head of Coaching a clear plan to hire against, so no department waits for a coach and no coach sits idle.
  • Matching Process: Own the process that connects first responders with coaches, from intake to first session to rematch. The Head of Coaching owns the coaches, the Head of Product owns the coaching product, and you own how the whole system runs and whether it works. Set the rules, find the bottlenecks, and bring clear requirements to Product.
  • Marketplace Efficiency: Own the metrics that show whether the marketplace works: time to first session, match rate, coach utilization, active coaches, and rematch rate. Report them by department every month, with a plan for every account below target.
  • Data: Own the single source of truth. Metric definitions, dashboards, and board reporting live with you. Lead the Lead Product Analyst and our data efforts so leadership trusts the numbers because you stand behind them.
  • Operations: Lead BizOps and set the company’s operating rhythm, so everyone knows what matters this quarter and why. Set priorities, hire, and hold the standard.
  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Give GTM the supply and cost inputs it needs to set pricing. Give Marketing readiness inputs for launches. Give Customer Success the engagement data it needs to drive renewals.

The Numbers

Two numbers define success in this role. You will set the targets with the CEO in your first 90 days and own them after that:

  • Marketplace liquidity. Time from rollout to first session, match rate (the share of members matched within a set number of days), coach utilization, and active coaches by discipline and region. Reported by department, monthly, with a plan for every account below target.
  • Marketplace quality. Rematch rate, member satisfaction after sessions, and how accurate the supply forecast is against actual demand.

Who Thrives Here

This role is not for everyone. You will thrive if you:

  • Have scaled the provider network or marketplace operations at a telehealth or care marketplace, working with independent (1099) providers, employed (W-2) providers, or both, and can show how you improved time to first appointment, match rate, and provider utilization.
  • Are comfortable with data models but can explain them in simple terms.
  • Make decisions with incomplete information and adjust fast when the data says you were wrong.
  • Prefer ownership over supervision.
  • Care deeply about serving those who serve others.

Why you’ll love working here

Sharp is a small, fast-growing team, and our success starts with the people doing the work. The package is built to support your health, your finances, and your growth:

  • Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance for you and your family.
  • Flexible PTO to recharge and perform at your best.
  • Competitive salary and meaningful equity that reflect the seniority of the role.
  • 401(k) with company match.
  • Unlimited access to the Sharp Performance platform and our coaches.

Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

As a Core AE, you will be helping our largest and most strategic enterprise sized customers consolidate outdated technologies, digitize workflows, and unlock game-changing data insights that will transform their businesses. We are helping the companies that literally keep our lights on, put food on our tables, and build our communities to become safer, more efficient, and more sustainable. Typical sales will be $100k to $500k, and typically involve POCs, multiple stakeholders, managing trials, multi-faceted pricing negotiations, and selling to executives and CXOs.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US in the following states: Texas, Oklahoma, Louisiana, and Arkansas.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • Your mantra is #alwaysbeprospecting: The world of operations is vast. Your customers are often out in the field and the best way to catch them is live on the phone. Samsara’s top reps do constant research to find companies and contacts to expand their pipeline.
  • You have innate curiosity in how businesses work: One day you’ll meet with someone in waste management and the next you may be learning about the inner workings of a food distribution center. Our top sales team members seek to learn the ins and outs of the businesses they support in order to make a larger impact.
  • You are a life-long learner: Samsara sales are complex. You will need to learn about businesses where you previously had little knowledge. The payoff is big but you have to be willing to put in the work.
  • You build genuine relationships with your customers: The industries we serve have relied on pen-and-paper solutions for years and haven’t been met with the type of technology we offer. Our customers value earned trust and human relationships built over time.
  • You want to be with the best: Samsara’s high-performance Sales culture means you’ll be surrounded by the best and challenged to go farther than you have before.

In this role, you will:

  • Develop Executive-Level relationships within strategic, named accounts
  • Own customer engagements end-to-end, from prospecting and qualification to close
  • Demonstrate excellent solution-based sales process in complex sales campaigns
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 5+ years experience in a full-cycle, closing sales role
  • Proven track record of consistent quota over-achievement in complex accounts and $100k+ ARR transactions
  • Experience handling and owning enterprise deal sizes and C-Level relationships
  • Willing and comfortable with strategic outbound prospecting
  • Excellent interpersonal skills and demonstrated ability to thrive in a dynamic, fast paced environment
  • Willing and comfortable traveling to meet customers on a monthly basis

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Experience working with line of business stakeholders (Operations, Finance, IT)
  • Awards for top achievement (President’s club, Winner’s circle, Top 10%)
  • Passion for the world of operations!

The compensation range shown spans approved pay zones for this role. Your primary work location determines the range applicable to you, which may be narrower than the full range displayed.

$222,400—$278,000 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. title: Associate Director, Pro-Vaccine Legal Alliance
description:
Location: Remote

Employment Type: Full-time, Exempt

Compensation: $95,000 per year

Reports To: PVLA Director

About American Families for Vaccines

American Families for Vaccines (AFV) is a national organization leading the pro-vaccine grassroots movement across the country. Our state Families for Vaccines chapters defend strong vaccine policy, fight misinformation, and advocate for evidence-based public health. We work in close partnership with providers, advocates, policymakers, and public health leaders to create healthier communities and protect immunization access for all families.

About the Pro-Vaccine Legal Alliance

The Pro-Vaccine Legal Alliance (PVLA) is a legal strategy and litigation initiative supporting evidence-based vaccine policy across the United States. Working as a project under American Families for Vaccines (AFV), PVLA provides legal analysis, litigation support, and strategic guidance to state advocates, policymakers, and public health leaders.

PVLA aims for high-impact legal infrastructure, not a volume-driven litigation shop. Our work focuses on strengthening public health authority, countering the expansion of non-medical exemptions, and shaping the legal and constitutional framework surrounding vaccine policy.

About the Role

The Pro-Vaccine Legal Alliance Associate Director will serve as a core member of PVLA, supporting state-level vaccine policy through legal research, analysis, and strategic advising. This role is ideal for a new attorney (or recent policy graduate) who is self-directed, comfortable working in a fast-moving policy environment, and motivated by the intersection of law, public health, and advocacy.

This position sits at the center of a rapidly evolving legal landscape. The PVLA Associate Director will help shape how courts, legislatures, and the public understand the legal foundations of vaccination policy, supporting work that has direct implications for public health, equity, and access to care across the country.

The PVLA Associate Director will work closely with the Director to develop litigation memos, provide real-time legal guidance during legislative sessions, support amicus and litigation strategy, and contribute to PVLA’s growing national legal infrastructure. This is a high-autonomy, mission-driven role with significant responsibility and opportunity to shape emerging legal strategy in public health.

Key Responsibilities

Legal Analysis & Strategy

  • Draft memos assessing constitutional claims, legal risk, and strategic opportunities
  • Conduct legal research on vaccine-related litigation, administrative law, and public health authority
  • Support case evaluation and contribute to PVLA’s litigation engagement decisions

Legislative & Policy Support

  • Provide legal review of proposed legislation, amendments, and regulatory actions
  • Draft or review testimony, legal guidance, and policy memos for state partners
  • Support rapid-response legal advising during active legislative sessions

Litigation & Amicus Support

  • Assist in drafting and coordinating amicus briefs and other legal filings
  • Support engagement with outside counsel and legal partners
  • Monitor ongoing litigation and prepare internal updates and summaries

Legal Intelligence & Infrastructure

  • Track legal developments across states and contribute to PVLA’s policy monitoring systems
  • Support development of internal workflows, templates, and legal resources

Collaboration & Communication

  • Work closely with AFV research, advocacy, communications, and state teams
  • Contribute to internal briefings and strategic discussions
  • Support development of public-facing legal explainers or summaries, as needed

Travel Requirement

  • Fully remote position with a nationally distributed team
  • Some travel may be required for key meetings, litigation support, or partner engagement (10% annually)
  • Occasional evening or weekend work during legislative sessions or active litigation

Qualifications

We recognize that strong candidates may bring varied experiences. If you are excited about this work, we encourage you to apply.

Required

  • Experience with public health policy or law, constitutional law or policy, or administrative law or policy
  • Excellent research, writing, and analytical skills
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and respond quickly in time-sensitive contexts
  • Comfort working independently in a remote environment

Preferred Skills (not required)

  • J.D. from an accredited law school in or an advanced health or policy degree (Masters in Health Policy, Policy, or similar)
  • Familiarity with state legislative processes or regulatory frameworks
  • Experience drafting briefs, memos, or policy guidance in a fast-paced environment
  • Interest in public health, science policy, or evidence-based advocacy

Compensation and Benefits

  • Salary:
    $95,000 annually
  • Benefits:
    • Fully paid health insurance for employee, partner and dependents.
    • Generous PTO, paid holidays, and remote work flexibility.
    • Flexible work hours and fully remote work environment with opportunities to travel and engage colleagues in-person a few times per year.
    • 401(k) with employer contribution
    • Short and Long Term Disability, Life insurance, and Parental Leave

***
