title: Junior Quantitative Researcher
description:
Junior Quantitative Researcher

About the role

Deeter Analytics is a privately held investment research and trading firm managing its own capital across public markets. After years of discretionary success, we think we have some unique ways of seeing the market, and we pair sharp human judgment with modern AI to act on them.

A lot of what we trade starts as a hunch at the desk: a pattern that keeps showing up, a relationship that feels like it should hold, a setup someone wants to trust but doesn't yet. We're hiring a Junior Quantitative Researcher to turn those hunches into evidence, and evidence into signals the desk actually uses. You'll take questions from the traders, test them honestly against the data, and come back in plain language: what holds, what doesn't, how strong, since when, and where it breaks. This is not a systematic seat: your models won't trade on their own, and you won't be one factor in an anonymous alpha pool. Your work is done when a trader understands it, trusts it, and acts on it. It's an entry point into a serious seat: as your signals prove out, they get more weight in the book, and you get more scope. The role is full-time and fully remote, US-based, overlapping the desk on US market hours.

What you'll own

  • The question queue. Desk hunches in, answers out. You scope the question, run the study, and come back sometimes same-day with what the data says, at the depth the question deserves.
  • The signal shelf. A growing library of signals and screens the desk trades around (earnings and event setups, positioning and flow extremes, regime and factor context) each with a documented edge, known failure modes, and live tracking against expectation. You retire what decays.
  • The evidence standard. Event studies, conditioning analyses, base rates, and walk-forward checks that hold up: point-in-time data, no leakage, no survivorship, costs counted, multiple-testing restraint. A backtest here is a way to kill an idea, not to sell it.
  • The quant read. The recurring numbers layer under the desk's picture of the market (regime, factor moves, breadth, positioning) feeding the morning picture rather than duplicating it.
  • The research data. Clean, point-in-time datasets (prices, fundamentals, earnings calendars, options and positioning) organized so every number you've ever reported traces back to code and data.
  • AI leverage. Use modern AI tools to test more ideas, read more literature, and write cleaner code than one person otherwise could, and verify what they give you.

Who you are

We hire for demonstrated judgment and how you think, not for pedigree. This is a junior seat, so we don't expect a markets résumé — the best evidence usually comes from wherever you've already done rigorous quantitative work. We look for signs that you are:

  • Rigorous where it counts. You think in base rates, sample sizes, and conditioning; you know what autocorrelation, overlapping windows, and fat tails do to naive statistics, and you'd rather report a small honest edge than a large fragile one.
  • Hypothesis-driven. You start from a mechanism (why would this work, who's on the other side, why hasn't it been arbitraged away) and let the data disappoint you, not the other way around.
  • A translator. Your finished product is a chart and a paragraph a non-quant acts on. If the desk can't understand it, it isn't done.
  • Comfortable finding nothing. "There's nothing there" is a result you deliver without flinching: a clean negative saves the desk real money, and you never dress noise up as signal to give someone the answer they wanted.
  • Genuinely curious about markets. You want to know why prices move. You don't need professional markets experience, you need to care about the answer.
  • Low ego and coachable. You take feedback well, update quickly when the facts change, and care more about the answer than the credit.

How you work

  • At desk speed, without cutting corners. A rough answer today often beats a perfect answer next week; a deep study is worth a month when the stakes justify it. You know which question is which, and you label your answers accordingly.
  • Kill your own results first. Before anyone else sees a number, you've gone hunting for the leak, the regime dependence, and the artifact that would explain it away.
  • Reproducible by default. Versioned data and code; any signal or study can be re-run months later and give the same answer.
  • Signal over noise. You surface the few things that matter, track what you've shipped, and say so plainly when something stops working.
  • AI-native. Fluent with modern AI tools for research, coding, and literature triage, and disciplined about checking their output.
  • Self-directed. You thrive working remotely with low guardrails, managing your own time and flagging what needs attention without being asked.

Core skills

  • Statistics and probability. Regression and its failure modes, hypothesis testing, bootstrap and resampling, thinking clearly about uncertainty in small and messy samples.
  • Python data stack. pandas, NumPy, SQL, and plotting that makes a point; notebooks that read top to bottom, graduating to scripts when a study becomes a signal.
  • Backtest and event-study hygiene. Point-in-time discipline, survivorship and look-ahead awareness, transaction-cost sanity, walk-forward validation, restraint about how many things you tested.
  • Market data. Comfort with prices, returns, fundamentals, and earnings calendars; options or positioning data a plus.
  • ML as a tool, not an identity. Regularized regression and gradient boosting when they beat something simpler, interpretability first. This is a statistics-first seat, not a deep-learning one.
  • Crisp communication. Compressing a study into exactly what a trader needs to know, now.

What we offer

  • A seat inside a live trading operation, with a direct line to the traders who act on your evidence.
  • Fast feedback: when a signal proves out, you watch it get used — and you'll know precisely what your work changed.
  • A well-capitalized firm with a distinctive approach to markets.
  • A deliberate growth path: own the question queue first, then take on a bigger slice of the research agenda as you prove out.

• A small, low-ego, fully remote team.

• Compensation: $120k - $170k + bonus.

title: Country Sales Manager UK & Ireland
description:
Job Description

Job Summary


The Country Sales Manager is accountable for GM Europe’s commercial performance and market execution in the assigned country or market(s), including sales and service performance where applicable. The role translates regional strategy and brand priorities into an integrated country plan, leads the market-facing commercial organisation, and is the main driver of the country Network Strategy, ensuring an effective and efficient network footprint aligned with GM Europe’s direction and local market characteristics.


As a strategic partner and trusted advisor, the Country Sales Manager builds strong relationships with customers and route-to-market partners, supports sales and service objectives, identifies market opportunities and strengthens operational performance. The role also proposes and agrees with the Marketing team the country media and marketing strategy required to support sales and revenue targets. The role sets priorities, deploys resources and makes commercial decisions within agreed governance and delegated authority, working closely with Distribution Managers and HQ functions to align local and regional priorities.


Key Responsibilities


Commercial Strategy and Market Performance


  • Translate GM Europe’s strategy into a clear country plan and own agreed outcomes for market development, sales, service, volume, revenue, profitability and customer experience.
  • Lead the country Network Strategy, ensuring an effective and efficient network footprint aligned with GM Europe’s direction and local market characteristics.
  • Propose and agree with the Marketing team the country media and marketing strategy required to support sales and revenue targets, using customer, market, competitor and partner insight to guide priorities.
  • Develop and monitor business plans with partners and maintain effective forecasting, performance management, reporting and governance routines.
  • Analyse sales performance, market trends and competitive activity to identify opportunities and drive sustainable growth.
  • Set priorities, deploy resources and make commercial decisions within agreed governance and delegated authority.

Customer, Partner and Route-to-Market Management


  • Lead relationships with dealerships, fleet customers, distributors, importers, agents and other route-to-market partners.
  • Manage the applicable route-to-market model, including direct-to-consumer, dealer, distributor, importer, agency and wholesale channels.
  • Where relevant, manage relationships with Independent Aftersales Market stores and other service partners.
  • Set clear expectations for partner performance, capability, customer experience and commercial contribution, and address gaps promptly.
  • Lead partner selection, onboarding, readiness and continuous improvement.
  • Use customer and partner insight to shape market plans and commercial decisions.
  • Represent GM Europe in relevant senior internal and external forums.

Customer Experience, Service and Network Effectiveness


  • Deliver a consistent, customer-first and brand-appropriate experience across all customer and partner touchpoints.
  • Monitor customer satisfaction and feedback, resolve issues and improve customer and partner journeys.
  • Execute the country Network Strategy to improve network coverage, capability, sales and service performance.
  • Support training, compliance and operational readiness across the applicable network.
  • Identify and escalate material customer, service, network and operational risks.

Multi-Brand and Cross-Functional Execution


  • Coordinate local execution of assigned GM brand plans while protecting each brand’s positioning, standards and customer proposition.
  • Support product launches and coordinate aligned marketing and advertising activities across GM and partner networks.
  • Align product, pricing, campaign, retail, distribution, inventory and partner activities, promoting the effective use of data, systems and standard processes.
  • Collaborate with Sales and Distribution Operations, CVO and Strategic Sales Development to improve new- and used-vehicle flows and identify additional sales opportunities.
  • Align country priorities with Marketing, Product, Aftersales, Finance, Logistics, Legal, Compliance, HR, Customer Care and other relevant teams.
  • Lead cross-functional initiatives, clarify decision rights and ensure timely escalation, resolution and communication of issues.

People Leadership and Organisational Effectiveness


  • Lead, develop and motivate the country organisation through clear objectives, coaching, prioritisation and accountability.
  • Build an inclusive, collaborative, customer-focused and performance-oriented culture.
  • Develop the capabilities required by the applicable operating model.
  • Role-model GM values, compliance, safety, integrity and respect in all business and people decisions.

Governance, Compliance and Representation


  • Ensure commercial activities comply with GM policies, applicable law, competition requirements, data-protection standards, internal controls and approved governance.
  • Maintain appropriate documentation and audit readiness.
  • Protect GM and brand interests and escalate material risks or decisions outside delegated authority.
  • Represent GM and its brands at relevant external events and with media and other stakeholders, where appropriate.

Required Experience and Capabilities


  • Experience in a commercial, market, sales, service, network, partner or operations environment.
  • Experience managing complex, customer-facing or partner-led operating models.
  • Strong commercial judgement and the ability to translate strategy into measurable outcomes and disciplined execution.
  • Strong stakeholder management, influencing and negotiation skills.
  • Ability to lead through change, build cross-functional alignment and develop high-performing teams.
  • Data-driven approach to performance management, forecasting, market analysis and decision-making.
  • Sound understanding of governance, compliance, risk management and delegated authority.

Role Evolution and Annual Goals


The Country Sales Manager role will evolve with GM’s business, organisational priorities and operating model. The role holder is expected to adapt to changing operating requirements, ways of working, routes to market, responsibilities and stakeholder arrangements, and to undertake related responsibilities reasonably required to support the business.


Targets, priorities and expectations will be established at the beginning of each year as annual goals. They may be reviewed or revised during the year where business needs, market conditions, organisational priorities or the operating model change, with appropriate notice and in accordance with applicable company policies and law. The role holder is expected to respond constructively and effectively to such changes.


Measures of Success


  • Delivery of agreed commercial, sales, service and customer-experience outcomes.
  • Effective execution of the applicable market and operating model.
  • Strong partner performance, network effectiveness and stakeholder relationships.
  • Consistent, compliant and brand-appropriate market execution.
  • Delivery of financial performance for the assigned country, in addition to sales performance.
  • Improved customer satisfaction and timely resolution of customer and partner issues.
  • Timely, fact-based decision-making, escalation and risk management.
  • A capable, engaged and high-performing country organisation.

Forest Home is a Christ-centered nonprofit camp dedicated to providing life-changing experiences for children, youth, and families. Through outdoor adventures, biblical teaching, and authentic community, we seek to cultivate spiritual growth and lifelong faith in Jesus Christ. We are seeking a passionate and strategic Major Gift Officer to help grow our mission through meaningful donor relationships and impactful giving opportunities.

The Major Gifts Officer is responsible for developing and managing relationships with current and prospective major donors to support Forest Home’s vision, programs, and capital needs. This position will focus on identifying, cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding individuals capable of making gifts of ($10,000+) or more annually.

The ideal candidate will be a committed follower of Jesus Christ with a heart for ministry, a high degree of emotional intelligence, and a proven ability to engage major donors in transformational giving.

The Major Gifts Officer works directly under the direction of the Chief Development Officer in the execution and support of the Forest Home strategies. The Major Gifts Officer is a key member of the development team, responsible for securing and growing significant philanthropic support. In addition to managing their own portfolio of high-capacity donors, the MGO oversees the Charitable Gift Advisor and Annual Fund Coordinator, ensuring a coordinated donor pipeline and an integrated strategy that advances donor relationships at every level.

This is a full-time, remote position working out of a home office. Seasonal travel to Forest Home in Forest Falls is required during the summer months or as needed for donor engagement, as well as regional travel throughout Southern California including but not limited to Orange County, San Diego County, Los Angeles County, Arizona and Nevada.

Forest Home is a Christ-centered nonprofit camp dedicated to providing life-changing experiences for children, youth, and families. Through outdoor adventure, biblical teaching, and authentic community, we cultivate spiritual growth and lifelong faith in Jesus Christ.

Position Summary

The MGO identifies, cultivates, solicits, and stewards individuals capable of giving $15,000 or more annually in support of Forest Home's programs, scholarships, and capital needs.

Reporting to the Chief Development Officer, the MGO manages a portfolio of high-capacity donors and partners closely with the Annual Fund Coordinator to build a coordinated pipeline that moves donors from mid-level to major and planned giving.

The ideal candidate is a committed follower of Jesus Christ with a heart for ministry, high emotional intelligence, and a proven record of inspiring donors toward generous, joyful giving.

Metric

Annual target

Major gift revenue

$3,750,000

Active portfolio

250 major donors and prospects

Donor retention

85–90%

Multi-year pledge conversations (3–5 year commitments)

20–30

15:1 Partnership program growth

New partners at $25,000+

Weekly face-to-face, virtual, and phone meetings

Preferred

Seasonal travel to the Forest Home campus in Forest Falls, CA is required during the summer and as needed for donor engagement and events.

Compensation and Benefits

The salary range for this position is $100,000–$120,000 per year, commensurate with experience and demonstrated fundraising results. You will work alongside our Azure development team to build the SAP integration for an AI-powered invoice booking solution. Your focus will be connecting the Azure application with SAP and ensuring reliable, traceable supplier invoice processing.

  • Support auditability and implement approval checkpoints for automated financial actions.

  • Troubleshoot integration issues and support end-to-end testing.

  • Hands-on development experience with SAP CPI and SAP BTP.

  • Experience integrating SAP with external applications or cloud platforms.

  • Experience handling integration failures, retries, duplicate prevention and transaction consistency.

  • Ability to work independently and collaborate closely with an Azure development team.

  • Working proficiency in English.

Nice to have qualifications

  • Experience with SAP CIM and/or SAP Ariba.

  • Experience integrating SAP with Microsoft Azure services.

  • Familiarity with AI-driven invoice processing or financial automation.

title: Senior HR Operations Specialist
description:
We are seeking a Senior HR Operations Specialist to join our HR Shared Services team. This Tier 2 role provides advanced operational support for complex HR inquiries, transactions, and escalations that require deeper expertise, sound judgment, and cross-functional coordination beyond Tier 1 support.

The Senior HR Operations Specialist is responsible for resolving exception-based and sensitive issues, ensuring consistent application of HR policies and processes, and identifying root causes that reduce rework and improve service delivery. This role partners closely with HR Transformation & Operations, HR Technology, Payroll, Centers of Excellence, and HR Business Partners to strengthen end-to-end process performance.

At Ralliant, this role is critical to stabilizing core HR operations, improving process design, and ensuring the HR operating model functions effectively at scale.

Key Responsibilities

Tier 2 Issue Resolution

  • Resolve escalated cases from Tier 1 that require advanced policy interpretation, exception handling, cross-functional coordination, review of historical transactions or employee records, or elevated judgment and sensitivity.
  • Manage complex issues across payroll, benefits, leave and absence, HR data, and related processes.
  • Own cases end to end, ensuring accurate resolution, timely follow-up, and clear communication with employees, managers, and internal stakeholders.
  • Serve as a trusted escalation point while minimizing unnecessary handoffs to HR Business Partners and Centers of Excellence.

HR Systems, Data & Operational Execution

  • Execute complex HR transactions in core systems (e.g., Oracle, ServiceNow)
  • Analyze and resolve data integrity issues across systems and processes
  • Create, generate, and analyze standard and ad hoc reports to support operational decision-making and issue resolution.
  • Identify root causes of recurring errors, system gaps, and manual workarounds
  • Ensure compliance with established controls, policies, and audit requirements
  • Partner with HR Tech and HRTO to test, validate, and refine system or process changes

Escalation Management & Cross-Functional Coordination

  • Act as the primary owner for Tier 2 cases, coordinating across Payroll, Total Rewards, Employee Relations, Legal, Centers of Excellence, HR Technology, and HR Business Partners as needed.
  • Set clear expectations with employees and managers regarding resolution timelines and next steps
  • Resolve issues effectively, reducing re-escalation, repeat contacts, and case recycling.
  • Escalate to Tier 3 or specialized teams only when appropriate and with complete context, documentation, and recommended next steps.

Process Improvement, Simplification & Automation

  • Identify systemic issues through analysis of case trends, escalations, and rework
  • Translate operational challenges into clear problem statements and improvement opportunities
  • Recommend and support solutions that strengthen controls, simplify workflows and decision points, reduce manual effort and error risk, and enable automation and self-service.
  • Partner with HRTO, HR Tech, and COEs to drive scalable improvements
  • Support process stabilization, redesign initiatives, and continuous improvement efforts (e.g., RBS tools)

Knowledge Management & Tier 1 Enablement

  • Strengthen Tier 1 capability by improving knowledge articles, standard operating procedures, decision frameworks, escalation criteria, and guidance on recurring issues and trends.
  • Reinforce consistent application of HR policies and practices
  • Improve upstream resolution rates by reducing avoidable escalations

Customer Experience & Professional Standards

  • Manage complex and sensitive interactions with professionalism, empathy, and clarity
  • Maintain strict confidentiality and data privacy standards
  • Represent HR as a unified function, ensuring seamless and consistent communication
  • Balance employee experience with operational discipline and policy adherence
  • Model and reinforce Ralliant’s HR operating model through day-to-day execution

What Success Looks Like

  • Timely and accurate resolution of complex Tier 2 cases
  • Measurable reduction in repeat escalations and chronic issue areas
  • Improved quality of Tier 1 inputs, knowledge content, and case handling
  • Reduced defects, rework, and downstream corrections
  • Clear visibility into systemic risks and improvement opportunities
  • Strong, trusted partnerships across HRTO, HR Tech, and functional teams

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business, or related field (or equivalent experience)
  • 3–6 years of experience in HR operations, shared services, payroll, benefits, HR systems, or complex case management in a process-driven environment.
  • Strong experience using HR systems such as Oracle, ServiceNow, Workday, or similar platforms.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage and resolve complex, cross-functional issues
  • Strong analytical thinking and written communication skills
  • Ability to communicate clearly and effectively in English, both verbally and in writing, is essential for success in this role
  • Ability to operate effectively in ambiguous or exception-based scenarios

Key Skills & Attributes

  • Strong operational judgment and structured problem-solving capability
  • Ability to identify root causes and drive sustainable solutions
  • Comfortable working across teams, systems, and processes
  • Clear and composed communicator in high-impact situations
  • Continuous improvement mindset with focus on simplification and scalability
  • Ability to balance employee experience with consistency, controls, and compliance

Why This Role Matters at Ralliant

As Ralliant continues to scale in a post-spin environment, the Tier 2 HR Operations Specialist plays a critical role in:

  • Stabilizing and strengthening core HR operations
  • Reducing escalation volume and dependency on HRBPs and COEs
  • Improving data quality, system reliability, and process consistency
  • Enabling safe and sustainable adoption of automation, self-service, and AI
  • Ensuring the HR operating model is executed effectively in practice
  • This is a critical problem-solving and continuous improvement role focused on ensuring HR services are reliable, scalable, compliant, and consistently aligned to the HR operating model.

Ralliant Corporation Overview

Ralliant, originally part of Fortive, now stands as a bold, independent public company driving innovation at the forefront of precision technology. With a global footprint and a legacy of excellence, we empower engineers to bring next-generation breakthroughs to life — faster, smarter, and more reliably. Our high-performance instruments, sensors, and subsystems fuel mission-critical advancements across industries, enabling real-world impact where it matters most. At Ralliant we’re building the future, together with those driven to push boundaries, solve complex problems, and leave a lasting mark on the world.

title: AVP- Complex Claims Specialist Business Torts
description:
Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That’s the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Job Category

Claim

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$132,800.00 - $219,100.00

Target Openings

1

What Is the Opportunity?

As an AVP, Business Torts Complex Claim Liability Specialist, you are responsible for investigating, evaluating, negotiating, and resolving the most complex and high exposure claims across multiple jurisdictions. Operating with a high degree of autonomy, this role serves as a subject matter expert on complex, litigated, and coverage-disputed claims. You will collaborate and partner closely with business partners, reinsurance, legal counsel, underwriting, and/or leadership to deliver optimal outcomes.

What Will You Do?

  • Directly handle the most severe and complex General Liability Coverage B, Technology Errors and Omissions and 1st and 3rd party Cyber claims from initiation to resolution, ensuring compliance with company policies and industry regulations.
  • Lead end-to-end investigation of high severity complex claims and conduct thorough coverage analysis, draft reservation of rights and coverage disclaimer letters, and/or assess recovery potential.
  • Establish accurate reserves and adjust as needed throughout the claim lifecycle to reflect current and anticipated exposure.
  • Evaluate complex liability, damage issues and/or recovery potential, including large data breach, ransomware, business interruption, errors and omissions, defamation/disparagement, anti-trust, unfair competition and privacy claims.
  • Manage assigned files from inception through resolution; Actively participate in selection of counsel and entire litigation team, where appropriate. Develop and execute claim resolution and litigation strategies.
  • Attend and participate in mediations, arbitrations, pre-trial conferences, and settlement conferences, and negotiate settlements within granted authority levels.
  • Identify and assess risk transfer and/or subrogation opportunities, as needed.
  • Partner closely with and present to underwriting, internal stakeholders, and leadership teams to provide claims intelligence on emerging risks, coverage gaps, and loss trends.
  • Mentor and provide technical guidance to claims professionals.
  • Acquire and maintain relevant Insurance License(s) to comply with state and Travelers’ requirements within three months of starting the job.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Law degree preferred, but not required.
  • Ten years of handling complex General Liability, Cyber and Technology Errors and Omissions litigation and/or claims handling experience.
  • Active adjuster license where required by state law.
  • Experience with claims management systems, with advanced skills in Microsoft Office and enterprise technology systems and platforms.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with the ability to understand, synthesize, interpret, and convey complex information in a simplified manner to multiple stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated ability to make independent decisions and handle complex claims, evaluate severe losses, and negotiate settlements strategically.
  • Exceptional customer service skills; demonstrated ability to manage relationships with key stakeholders while delivering a consistently positive experience.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and organizational skills with the ability to manage a high-volume workload and prioritize effectively.
  • Expert-level negotiation and conflict resolution skills with the ability to apply strategic claim handling practices.
  • Ability to manage stress, navigate difficult situations, and maintain composure and professionalism under pressure while always taking accountability for decisions.
  • Expert level knowledge of insurance principles, policy language, exclusions, and ISO forms with thorough understanding of business line products.
  • Strong understanding of state and federal insurance regulations, fair claims practices legislation, and legal requirements; ability to apply this knowledge to complex claims.
  • Ability to quickly learn from experience and apply it to new situations with speed and flexibility.

What is a Must Have?

  • High School Diploma or GED.
  • Seven years of bodily injury liability, property damage liability, or comparable claim related experience.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members – including spouses, domestic partners, and children – are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences.

In accordance with local law, candidates seeking employment in Colorado are not required to disclose dates of attendance at or graduation from educational institutions.

If you are a candidate and have specific questions regarding the physical requirements of this role, please send us an email so we may assist you.

Travelers reserves the right to fill this position at a level above or below the level included in this posting.

To learn more about our comprehensive benefit programs please visit .

description:
Healthcare organizations are under more compliance pressure than ever, and most are managing it the wrong way: scattered tools, manual tracking, and fragmented records that leave teams exposed and exhausted. Compliance has become someone's second job, not a program anyone is proud to stand behind.

Compliancy Group exists to change that. We are the platform for healthcare compliance programs, consolidating every element of a complete program into one connected system, so organizations can simplify requirements, gain real visibility into where risk lives, operate with confidence, and be genuinely defensible when it matters most. We do not sell a tool and walk away. We build the program with you, combining purpose-built software, proprietary conformance scoring, and ongoing access to compliance advisors, until your organization has the structure, the evidence, and the expertise to lead compliance instead of just survive it. If you are the kind of person who wants to work on something that actually protects patients and providers, you are in the right place.

Audit Manager is our solution for medical billing and coding audits. We’re looking for an Account Executive to grow our Audit Manager business. This role is a rare blend: you understand how medical billing and coding work, and you know how to run a great sales process. You don’t need to be a certified coder, but you need to speak the language of revenue cycle leaders and understand why audit readiness matters to them. If you’ve sold in the revenue cycle space and you’re excited to sell a solution that makes a real difference for providers, we’d love to meet you.

What you’ll do

  • Own the full sales cycle for Audit Manager, from prospecting and discovery through demo, negotiation, and close.
  • Build and manage your own pipeline, self-sourcing a meaningful share through strategic outbound to practice administrators, revenue cycle leaders, compliance officers, and coding managers.
  • Lead discovery conversations that uncover the coding and billing risks behind the immediate need, and connect them to the financial and compliance impact for the organization.
  • Deliver clear, confident demos that show how Audit Manager fits into a customer’s revenue cycle workflow.
  • Partner with our BDR team, sales engineering, and Customer Success to make sure every new client starts strong.
  • Keep your HubSpot activity current and accurate so pipeline and forecast data reflect reality.
  • Stay current on coding and billing trends, payer audit activity, and our competitive landscape so you can speak with authority in every conversation.

What we’re looking for

  • 3+ years of closing experience as an Account Executive, with a track record of hitting quota.
  • Experience selling into healthcare, ideally within revenue cycle management (RCM), medical billing, coding, or healthcare IT.
  • A working knowledge of medical billing and coding concepts (such as CPT, ICD-10, claims, and denials). This doesn’t need to be advanced, but it needs to be real.
  • Strong discovery and demo skills: you ask before you pitch, and you can tailor a demo to what you’ve learned.
  • Experience with deal sizes in the $5K to $75K range and multi-stakeholder buying processes.
  • Comfort with sales tools such as HubSpot, Apollo, Salesloft, or Outreach.
  • A collaborative mindset: you care as much about your teammates’ success as your own.

Bonus points if you have

  • Experience selling for an RCM, coding audit, clearinghouse, or practice management company.
  • A coding or billing background (such as CPC or CCS certification, or hands-on revenue cycle work) before moving into sales.

What Compliancy Group offers

  • Extensive onboarding and ongoing development on both the platform and the sales motion.
  • Comprehensive benefits, including medical, dental, vision, a 401(k) with company match, and unlimited PTO.
  • A remote-first role, with the option to come together in person at key moments.
  • A transparent, collaborative culture that invests in people and takes the work seriously.

Base Salary: $100,000 + uncapped commission, OTE $145-170k

Location: Remote

title: Vice President of Development
description:
ABOUT OUR ORGANIZATION

STEM From Dance equips girls to become the innovators, engineers, and creators the world needs, building creativity, confidence, and skills through the transformative power of dance.

Founded in 2012, we reach girls in more than 30 cities. 76% of our participants report a sense of belonging, against a national average of 35% for girls their age, and 73% report confidence in STEM. We are building toward 20,000 girls by 2028.

Our revenue has grown from $349,000 to $2.7 million. Reaching 20,000 girls a year takes revenue that grows faster still, and a development function the organization owns and can grow with. Building that function is what this role is for.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the Vice President of Development is responsible for the acquisition and growth of STEM From Dance's philanthropic revenue. You would personally build and close the relationships that fund our national growth.

The mandate. More than half of what we raise in a typical year comes from funders who were not supporting us twelve months earlier. Renewing and upgrading our existing base covers part of what we need. The rest has to come from funders who are not with us yet. Your charge is to bring in significant new commitments at six figures and above, and to build a pipeline deep enough that next year's number is achievable before the year begins.

Where your time goes. STEM From Dance has built an infrastructure powered by AI and technology that handles the production side of development: proposal drafting, prospect research, application assembly, and pipeline maintenance, with cross-functional support behind it. That keeps this role on the work that produces revenue. Funder conversations, donor relationships, representing the organization in the room, and the judgment calls about where to aim. We want someone who wants to be out front.

The Vice President of Development sits on the executive team, and the role is built to grow into Chief Development Officer as the development operation does. A dedicated development hire is budgeted for next fiscal year and would report to this role.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • New funder acquisition and major gifts (40%)
  • Major individual giving (20%)
  • Strategy, positioning, and portfolio performance (20%)
  • Board engagement and external representation (15%)
  • Executive leadership (5%)

Requirements

Required Qualifications

  • Track record of personally closing philanthropic or commercial commitments of $100,000 or more.
  • Demonstrated net-new fundraising origination, with a substantial share of funds raised coming from funders personally identified and acquired.
  • Experience building fundraising revenue without relying on an established institution's name and donor base.
  • Direct fundraising experience across at least two of the following funder types: private foundations, corporate partners, and individual major donors.
  • Experience operating effectively in a rapidly growing organization where priorities sharpen and structures are built over time.
  • Sound judgment in deciding which fundraising opportunities to pursue or decline, with accountability for those decisions.
  • Working fluency with AI tools used in fundraising workflows, with the ability to identify incorrect output before it reaches a funder.
  • Experience representing an organization independently in executive-level funder conversations as the most senior person in the room.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience closing major philanthropic or commercial commitments with direct responsibility for making the ask.
  • Experience closing commitments above $250,000.
  • Experience building a major individual giving program from an early stage.
  • Experience at an organization in a comparable growth stage, scaling from a single city to a national footprint.
  • Prior participation on an executive team.
  • Familiarity with investment-level or unrestricted giving methodologies.

Benefits

Compensation & Benefits

  • Remote work with 20% travel, including monthly in-person meetings in NYC.
  • Comprehensive benefits and perks, including:
    • Health insurance (medical, dental, vision)
    • 403(b) retirement savings account
    • Professional Development Stipend
    • 2-week org-wide shutdown at the end of the year
    • Generous PTO and flexible scheduling
    • Annual staff retreats
    • Goals-based bonus

STEM From Dance is committed to building a team that reflects the diversity of the communities we serve. We value and celebrate the unique perspectives, experiences, and contributions of people from all backgrounds, especially those who have been historically underrepresented in STEM and the arts. We strongly encourage applications from candidates of color, women, LGBTQ+ individuals, people with disabilities, and members of other marginalized groups. We believe that diverse voices make us stronger, and we are dedicated to creating an equitable, inclusive, and empowering environment where everyone can thrive.

title: Infrastructure Systems Engineer
description:
We are seeking an Infrastructure Systems Engineer who will join our team in managing all aspects of our infrastructure for both federal government and private sector clients. This role involves designing, deploying, and managing secure AWS environments, implementing AWS best practices, and automating nearly everything we do. Candidates must demonstrate strong experience in infrastructure automation, deep understanding of various flavors of linux, and excellent communication skills.

Key Responsibilities

  1. Cloud Infrastructure & Infrastructure as Code
    • Design, deploy, and manage AWS environments (EC2, ECS, EKS, Lambda, S3, RDS, etc.) using Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools (Terraform/OpenTofu, AWS CloudFormation, or Pulumi).
    • Implement serverless architectures (Lambda, Step Functions)
    • Using configuration management tools (Ansible, Puppet)
  2. CI/CD Pipeline & Automation
    • Build and maintain robust, secure CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, AWS CodePipeline).
    • Develop automation scripts (Python, Bash) and incorporate AI/predictive techniques where feasible to reduce manual coding effort.
    • Embed DevSecOps best practices—security, compliance, and testing—within automated workflows.
  3. Containerization & Orchestration
    • Containerize applications using Docker and manage them on AWS ECS.
    • Optimize container performance and scalability while ensuring efficient resource utilization.
  4. Monitoring, Logging & Alerting
    • Implement and manage monitoring, logging (NewRelic), and alerting solutions to track application health, performance, and security in real-time.
    • Troubleshoot issues proactively to maintain high availability.
  5. Security & Compliance

title: Principal Security Engineer
description:
Who We Are

Imagine Pediatrics is a tech enabled, pediatrician led medical group reimagining care for children with special health care needs. We deliver 24/7 virtual first and in home medical, behavioral, and social care, working alongside families, providers, and health plans to break down barriers to quality care. We do not replace existing care teams; we enhance them, providing an extra layer of support with compassion, creativity, and an unwavering commitment to children with medical complexity.

What You’ll Do

As Principal Security Engineer with Imagine Pediatrics, you will set the technical vision for how we protect our systems, our data, and the children and families who trust us with their care. You will serve as a trusted security advisor to the VP, Information Security and work across the business to make secure the default way we build and run technology, partnering closely with Engineering on DevSecOps strategy and architectural improvements.. You will stay hands-on with our hardest problems while raising the bar for the security team and the engineers around it.

You will:

  • Set the technical vision for the security stack, including endpoint, email, data loss prevention, vulnerability management and penetration testing, network, application, and data security, and ensure it aligns with business and clinical strategy
  • Define long-term cloud and identity security strategy across Microsoft Azure/EntraID and Amazon Web Services (AWS), including privileged access, phishing-resistant MFA, and governance of non-human identities such as AI agents, service accounts, and API keys, shaping secure infrastructure design patterns that influence company-wide technical decisions
  • Lead security architecture review and threat modeling for Care Hub and connected services, including Medplum application-layer controls (FHIR access policies, SMART scopes, Bots, and custom code) and data platforms such as Snowflake
  • Define DevSecOps strategy and standardize security gates across the SDLC and CI/CD pipeline, building on GitHub Advanced Security, OWASP Top 10 practices, software bills of materials, and prioritization of CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities
  • Serve as the senior technical escalation point (including in the on-call rotation) for the most complex and highest-stakes security events and strengthen incident playbooks, ransomware and critical-SaaS exercises, and restoration testing against recovery targets
  • Monitor and advise on the evolving threat landscape facing healthcare including AI-enabled and agentic attacks and its implications for business strategy
  • Ensure the organization can accurately demonstrate its security posture to payors, regulators, auditors, and other third parties, building documentation and evidence pipelines, including AI-assisted ones, that scale with our HITRUST, HIPAA, and NIST compliance requirements.
  • Frame ambiguous, high-stakes security questions for the organization and drive them to well-reasoned, defensible answers delivering decision-ready recommendations, risk rankings, and documented resolution pathways.
  • Ensure precision at the program level by driving guardrails such as automated configuration checks and drift detection, so misconfigurations are prevented systemically rather than caught individually
  • Shape the technical sequencing of our multi-year security roadmap, contribute to quarterly engineering planning, and ensure the security program’s execution aligns with company strategy and the timelines that matter to the business
  • Explore early-stage ideas and proofs of concept to de-risk future security initiatives before they are staffed or scoped
  • Champion thoughtful AI adoption within security to reduce manual effort, and guide how AI tools and AI-enabled products are adopted securely across the company
  • Partner with engineering, product, IT, and clinical stakeholders to embed security into how we design, build, and operate our digital products, translating complex security concepts for non-technical audiences
  • Mentor the security engineering team, coach engineers across technology on security craftsmanship, and shape the team’s learning culture
  • Act as a trusted advisor to leadership, advocating for security engineers while aligning security decisions with business priorities, and demonstrate executive-level composure in high-stakes, ambiguous situations
  • Apply professional discretion and judgement when viewing sensitive and personal data or information in the process of conducting work
  • Other duties as assigned

What You Bring & How You Qualify  

First and foremost, you’re passionate and committed to reimagining pediatric health care and creating a world where every child with complex medical conditions gets the care and support they deserve. You will need:  

  • Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Science, Information Security, Business, Management, or a related field is desired; advanced degree a plus
  • Relevant license or certification(s): CISSP, CCSP, CISM, GIAC (e.g., GCIH, GCLD, GSEC), AWS Certified Security – Specialty, Microsoft Certified: Cybersecurity Architect Expert preferred
  • 10+ years of experience as a Security Engineer, Principal Security Engineer, Security Architect, or similar role(s), with at least 5 years of experience within the healthcare industry.
  • A track record of setting security technical strategy and driving alignment across security, IT, and engineering teams
  • Deep expertise in cloud and identity security architecture across AWS and Microsoft Azure/EntraID
  • Hands-on application and product security experience, including threat modeling, secure SDLC and CI/CD design, and securing healthcare APIs (FHIR, SMART on FHIR); experience with Medplum is a plus
  • Experience leading detection and response programs, including partnering with MDR providers and leading the technical response to serious security incidents and data breaches
  • Extensive experience translating HITRUST and HIPAA Security Rule requirements into technical controls and supporting engagements with auditors, payors, and regulators
  • Experience using Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a transformative technology to enhance and automate security processes, and an understanding of the security risks AI systems introduce
  • Knowledge of IT systems such as AWS, Microsoft Intune, EntraID, CrowdStrike Falcon (EDR/SIEM), GitHub Advanced Security, Snowflake, JAMF, Meraki, and JIRA Service Management
  • Strong collaboration and coaching skills, with demonstrated success developing senior engineers
  • Comfort operating autonomously in ambiguity, exploring early-stage ideas without well-defined requirements
  • Experience working in a fast-paced, hypergrowth, collaborative environment
  • Willingness to participate in an on-call rotation
  • Contributions to the broader security community, such as conference talks, publications, or industry threat intelligence sharing, are a plus

What We Offer (Benefits + Perks)

The role offers a base salary range of $195,000-$225,000 in addition to annual bonus incentive, competitive company benefits package, and eligibility to participate in an employee equity purchase program (as applicable). When determining compensation, we analyze and carefully consider several factors including job-related knowledge, skills and experience. These considerations may cause your compensation to vary.

  • Competitive medical, dental, and vision insurance 
  • Healthcare and Dependent Care FSA; Company-funded HSA
  • 401(k) with 4% match, vested 100% from day one
  • Employer-paid short and long-term disability 
  • Life insurance at 1x annual salary
  • 20 days PTO + 10 Company Holidays & 2 Floating Holidays 
  • Paid new parent leave
  • Additional benefits to be detailed in offer

What We Live By

We’re guided by our five core values:

Our Values:

  • Children First. We put the best interests of children above all. We know that the right decision is always the one that creates more safe days at home for the children we serve today and in the future.
  • Earn Trust. We listen first, speak second. We build lasting relationships by creating shared understanding and consistently following through on our commitments.
  • Innovate Today. We believe that small improvements lead to big impact. We stay curious by asking questions and leveraging new ideas to learn and scale.
  • Embrace Humanity. We lead with empathy and authenticity, presuming competence and good intentions. When we stumble, we use the opportunity to grow and understand how we can improve.
  • One Team, Diverse Perspectives. We actively seek a range of viewpoints to achieve better outcomes. Even when we see things differently, we stay aligned on our shared mission and support one another to move forward — together.

We Value Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging

We believe that creating a world where every child with complex medical conditions gets the care and support, they deserve requires a diverse team with diverse perspectives. We're proud to be an equal opportunity employer. People seeking employment at Imagine Pediatrics are considered without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital or veteran status, age, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, or characteristics (or those of a family member), pregnancy or other status protected by applicable law.

title: Lead Product Designer
description:
Lead Product Designer

Givelify is a fintech-for-good company where brilliant minds come to power the most loved and trusted online and mobile giving app platform. Thanks to over 2 million generous donors, we’ve helped more than 80,000 nonprofits and places of worship raise over $7.5 billion. Together, they’re changing their world with kindness and generosity.

Inc. 5000, the Stevies® Awards, Gartner, Forbes, and many more have recognized our story, innovations, and achievements. Our award-winning team builds products and experiences that put more good into the world. We love to take on big challenges because we know our work matters.

Make an impact at one of the fastest-growing private companies in the U.S. Be part of a talented team of big-hearted individuals, earning competitive pay with excellent benefits.

About your role:

We’re seeking a Lead Product Designer to elevate the quality, strategy, and impact of product design across Givelify’s mobile and web experiences. You’ll drive design excellence, guide cross-functional alignment, and shape end-to-end product vision—from discovery through delivery. In this role, you’ll combine hands-on design leadership with systems-level thinking to create simple, inspiring, and scalable product experiences for our giving community.

The Creative Team:

Givelify’s Creative Team produces the experiences that wow our audiences and users. We consistently deliver world-class design and creativity across the entire business, serving our customers in collaboration with product, technology, marketing, support, and operations. This role reports to the Director of Product Design.

The Lead Product Designer will get to:

  • Drive Product Design Initiatives
    Lead design initiatives, imagine novel solutions, and guide cross-functional teams toward cohesive product outcomes. You move fluidly across the entire design process—from problem framing to high-fidelity prototypes—and elevate complexity into elegant simplicity. You know great design is invisible because it works effortlessly for our giving community.
  • Own End-to-End Design Execution
    Ensure successful delivery of product experiences by driving all phases of design work. From discovery and solution ideation to refined interfaces and engineering handoff, you set the standard for quality, clarity, and completeness.
  • Optimize Design Operations & Efficiency
    Maximize throughput and design velocity by shaping and owning design operations for your scope of work. You establish structure, anticipate needs, remove friction, and scale effective design practices across teams.
  • Quality Elevation & Feedback Culture
    Continuously raise the bar for design excellence by soliciting, synthesizing, and acting on feedback from stakeholders. You model a culture of “feedback is fuel” and know how to extract value from different points-of-view to arrive at quality—strengthening both the work and the team behind it.

To be successful in this role, you’ll also:

  • Apply Human-Centered Design for Major Initiatives
    Shape end-to-end product experiences by driving cross-functional conversations, orchestrating user flows, and guiding teams from concept through launch with a deeply human-centered approach.
  • Lead Cross-Functional Alignment
    Collaborate strategically with Product, Engineering, and senior cross-functional leaders to influence priorities, illuminate trade-offs, and ensure every touchpoint reflects Givelify’s mission and strategic objectives.
  • Drive Insight-Informed Decision Making
    Embed a deep understanding of Givelify’s audiences and business strategy into design decisions, representing the customer perspective at all times to guide product direction and elevate design quality.
  • Advance the Design System & Standards
    Drive growth and adoption of the Givelify Design System—ensuring scalable, consistent, and brand-aligned experiences across platforms while coaching teams on best practices. 
  • KPIs:
    • # of creative cycle days
    • # of replies per cycle

Your experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree  
  • Experience working on a native mobile apps team
  • 5+ years of B2C native mobile app experience
  • Expert level proficiency of Figma, Adobe CC suite and/or other industry standard creative tools
  • A portfolio highlighting some of your best work (please include password)
  • Prototyping: Lofi and Hifi prototypes, you know when to use one over the other and embrace an iterative process. 
  • Languages: English; Spanish a plus 
  • Communication: You can articulate what makes a good vs great design, as well as articulate your design point of view. 
  • Problem solver who requires very little guidance on projects; thrives in a fast-paced environment. 
  • Expert-level applied understanding of formal elements of design, including typography, layout, balance, and proportion. 
  • (Bonus) Research: You are familiar with front-end research (light ethnography) and/or able to facilitate user testing sessions to validate your designs with users. 
  • (Bonus): Remote: Experience working with remote teams. 

Your superpowers:

  • Problem-Solving: Is resourceful and creative in solving complex issues. Uses sound judgment, data, and collaboration. Connects design decisions to brand and business outcomes.
  • Integrity: Demonstrates congruence in thought, speech, and action. Can be trusted to act with courage and to do the right thing. 
  • Collaboration: Fosters productive relationships; values others' opinions, shows appreciation, and seeks to understand different perspectives. 
  • Customer Focus: Adopts a human-centric approach that meets or anticipates customers' needs when developing solutions. 
  • Drive for Results: Can be relied upon to be resourceful & tenacious in achieving key desired results. 
  • Effective Communication: Inspires and aligns through clear, thoughtful dialogue.
  • Mentorship: Invests in the growth and success of fellow designers.

Our culture:

We are a virtual team of award-winning and high-performing professionals who innovate and collaborate to fulfill our mission to instantly connect people to causes that matter most to them so they can change their world with kindness and generosity. Our four keys to success - integrity, heart, simplicity, and wow - fuel our passion to be recognized among the tech industry’s most inclusive and purpose-driven workplaces.

We are steadfast in our conviction to overcome challenges while performing meaningful work alongside some of the most brilliant minds and biggest hearts. It propels our growth as individuals and as a team. We are committed to respecting each other in our workplace, firmly believing diversity is our strength.

At the heart of everything we do are our giving community, our donors and our partner organizations. We lean on research and human-centered design to consistently push the envelope and innovate our products and customer experiences.

We take great pride in providing competitive pay, full benefits to help care for you today and in the future, amazing perks (including flexible PTO), and, most importantly, the opportunity to put passion and purpose front and center.

About Givelify

Givelify is the most loved and trusted online and mobile giving platform. Along with its powerful donation management system, it’s the fastest-growing technology for advancing generosity in the world. We instantly connect people to their heart’s impulse to do good with award-winning products and experiences. A global community of over 2 million generous people supports their favorite churches, places of worship, nonprofits, and causes with over $7.5 billion in donations across more than 80,000 organizations. Givelify leads all giving apps on the App Store and Google Play Store with more than 135,000 verified, authentic reviews with an average 4.9 out of 5-star rating. Learn more at Givelify.com.

title: Service Desk Lead (Senior)
description:
Overview

DecisionPoint seeks a Service Desk Lead to manage daily service-desk operations for the USMEPCOM ENLIST program. This position oversees ticket queues, staffing schedules, escalations, VIP support, service quality, knowledge practices, problem trends, and operational communications.

The Service Desk Lead ensures that incidents and requests are properly received, prioritized, assigned, tracked, escalated, resolved, and documented across all support tiers. The Lead works closely with the Government Service Desk Branch Chief and prepares communications, status information, and recommendations for release through Government-approved channels.

This position also coordinates with Task 2 IT Service Management process owners to align service-desk activities with incident, request, problem, knowledge, access, change, configuration, service-level, and continual-improvement processes. The Service Desk Lead uses ServiceNow data to monitor performance, identify recurring issues, manage workload, and recommend improvements to service quality and customer experience.

This position is remote, with Chicago-area candidates preferred. Participation in after-hours escalation and operational-support coverage may be required.

Note: By applying to this position, you acknowledge and consent to having your resume included in an active competitive government contract bid.

Duties & Responsibilities

The Service Desk Lead will:

  • Lead day-to-day service-desk operations across the USMEPCOM enterprise.
  • Manage incident, service-request, access-request, and problem ticket queues across applicable support tiers.
  • Monitor ticket intake, prioritization, assignment, aging, escalation, resolution, and closure.
  • Develop and maintain staffing schedules, shift coverage, workload assignments, and escalation rosters.
  • Ensure adequate service-desk coverage for established support hours and 24/7/365 operational requirements.
  • Coordinate after-hours support and escalation coverage for mission-impacting incidents.
  • Assign work based on incident priority, technician qualifications, availability, workload, and service-level commitments.
  • Monitor queue volumes, backlogs, response times, resolution times, reassignment rates, reopen rates, and other service-quality measures.
  • Identify tickets at risk of missing service-level targets and coordinate corrective or escalation actions.
  • Lead daily queue reviews, shift handoffs, operational briefings, and workload-balancing activities.
  • Coordinate priority and VIP support and provide status through dashboards, email updates, or in-person briefings as required.
  • Ensure VIP incidents and requests receive timely attention, clear ownership, appropriate escalation, and professional communication.
  • Prepare service notifications, outage messages, planned-maintenance communications, and customer updates for review and release through the Government Service Desk Branch Chief.
  • Ensure contractor personnel follow Government-approved communication and escalation procedures.
  • Serve as the primary operational liaison between service-desk personnel, the Government Service Desk Branch Chief, Task 2 process owners, and technical support teams.
  • Coordinate with field support, engineering, cybersecurity, application, network, system-administration, and vendor teams to resolve escalated incidents.
  • Coordinate service-desk activities with incident, request, problem, knowledge, access, change, configuration, service-level, and continual-improvement processes.
  • Use ServiceNow to manage queues, assignments, escalations, dashboards, reports, knowledge articles, and operational records.
  • Ensure tickets contain accurate categorization, prioritization, assignment, troubleshooting notes, customer communications, resolution details, and closure codes.
  • Confirm that resolved incidents and requests are validated with customers and properly closed.
  • Review escalated and recurring incidents to identify patterns, known errors, emerging risks, and potential service problems.
  • Initiate or recommend problem records when incident frequency, impact, or complexity warrants formal analysis.
  • Support problem-management activities by gathering incident history, technical evidence, business impact, workarounds, and resolution data.
  • Coordinate with problem owners to document known errors, workarounds, and approved solutions in the Known Error Database or knowledge repository.
  • Oversee the development, review, approval, publication, and maintenance of service-desk knowledge articles.
  • Ensure technicians use approved knowledge content and provide feedback when articles are incomplete, inaccurate, or obsolete.
  • Conduct quality reviews of tickets, communications, knowledge articles, and customer interactions.
  • Develop coaching and corrective actions to address documentation, process, technical, or customer-service deficiencies.
  • Track customer satisfaction and recommend improvements to service delivery and user communications.
  • Analyze incident and request trends and provide recommendations for technical, procedural, staffing, training, or knowledge improvements.
  • Produce operational reports and dashboards covering ticket volume, backlog, service levels, VIP support, escalations, recurring incidents, and service quality.
  • Provide service-desk statistics, accomplishments, risks, issues, trends, and corrective actions for Monthly Status Reports and program reviews.
  • Support Daily System Status Reports with current incident, event, outage, and operational information.
  • Maintain service-desk procedures, escalation matrices, staffing plans, shift-handoff checklists, communication templates, and operating guides.
  • Support service-desk readiness for transitions, releases, maintenance activities, major events, and operational changes.
  • Mentor service-desk personnel and provide guidance on troubleshooting, ticket management, escalation, documentation, and customer communication.
  • Recommend automation, workflow, dashboard, knowledge, and reporting improvements within ServiceNow.
  • Perform other service-desk leadership duties necessary to maintain reliable enterprise IT support.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Candidates must meet all of the following requirements:

  • Active Secret clearance or higher.
  • Associate’s or bachelor’s degree in information technology or a related field.
  • Minimum of six years of relevant experience in enterprise IT support, service-desk operations, end-user support, or a related technical environment.
  • Experience coordinating service-desk operations.
  • Experience using ServiceNow.
  • Experience managing ticket queues, technician assignments, escalations, or operational-support schedules.
  • Experience supporting incident, request, problem, knowledge, or service-level management processes.
  • Ability to analyze operational data and identify ticket, service-quality, workload, and problem trends.
  • Ability to prepare clear operational reports, customer communications, dashboards, and leadership updates.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience communicating during priority incidents.
  • Strong leadership, customer-service, organizational, and problem-solving abilities.
  • Ability to support after-hours escalations or operational events when required.

Preferred Qualifications

The following qualifications are preferred but are not required:

  • CompTIA A+ certification.
  • ITIL v4 Foundation certification.
  • Additional ITIL practice-management or service-management training.
  • ServiceNow Certified System Administrator certification.
  • Experience supporting federal or Department of Defense service-desk operations.
  • Experience leading a multi-tier enterprise service desk in a 24/7/365 environment.
  • Experience coordinating support for geographically dispersed users and remote locations.
  • Experience managing VIP or executive-level technical support.
  • Experience developing ServiceNow reports, dashboards, workflows, or queue-management views.
  • Experience with knowledge management and Known Error Database practices.
  • Experience conducting ticket-quality reviews and developing technician coaching plans.
  • Experience supporting major incidents, outage communications, root-cause analysis, and corrective actions.
  • Familiarity with ITIL incident, request, problem, knowledge, access, change, configuration, service-level, and continual-improvement practices.

Skills and Competencies

  • Service-desk operations leadership.
  • Queue, schedule, workload, and escalation management.
  • ServiceNow ticketing, reporting, and dashboard capabilities.
  • Incident, request, problem, and knowledge management.
  • Service-level monitoring and performance analysis.
  • VIP and priority customer support.
  • Clear and audience-appropriate operational communication.
  • Customer-service quality and continuous improvement.
  • Technician mentoring, coaching, and performance feedback.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • Ability to remain organized during high-volume or mission-impacting events.
  • High attention to detail and consistent follow-through.

Our Equal Employment Opportunity Policy

  • EEO and Affirmative Action Policy: DecisionPoint Corporation is an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. It is the policy of DecisionPoint Corporation to provide equal employment opportunity in accordance with all applicable Equal Employment Opportunity/Affirmative Action laws, directives and regulations to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other protected status under Federal, State or Local laws.
  • Pay Transparency Policy: In accordance with Presidential Executive Order 13665, DecisionPoint Corporation will not discharge or in any other manner discriminate against employees or applicants because they have inquired about, discussed, or disclosed their own pay or the pay of another employee or applicant. However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with the contractor's legal duty to furnish information.
  • Authorization to Share Resume and Personal Information: By expressing your interest and submitting your resume for this position, you authorize DecisionPoint Corporation to share your resume, as well as personal information included on the resume, with its subsidiaries, affiliates and teaming partners for the purpose of considering you for this position and other available positions requiring comparable skills, education and experience. Should DecisionPoint Corporation. or its affiliates and teaming partners wish to initiate pre-employment discussions, you will be asked to complete an employment application and related employment documents.
