title: Materials Science Tutor
location: Australia, Canada, India, United Kingdom, United States
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

In this role, you will help enhance Grok by providing high-quality data annotations, labels, and inputs focused on materials science. You will draw on your expertise in areas such as energy materials, semiconductors, nanomaterials, metals and alloys, biomaterials, polymers, ceramics, and glasses to evaluate model outputs, identify errors in structure-property reasoning or processing assumptions, and produce clear, rigorous analyses and explanations. Your work will help train Grok to distinguish flawed or inadequately justified materials science analyses from those that are scientifically accurate, well-grounded, and practically insightful.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Use proprietary software applications to annotate and label data for designated projects.
  • Support the delivery of high-quality, accurate, and well-curated datasets that meet project standards.
  • Collaborate with technical teams to develop and train new tasks, contributing to the successful implementation of innovative technologies and initiatives.
  • Work closely with technical staff to improve the design, functionality, and efficiency of annotation tools and workflows.
  • Advance materials science research by guiding AI models in solving complex scientific problems and supporting scientific discovery and practical applications.
  • Select and solve problems across various subfields of materials science aligned with your expertise, providing detailed solutions and critically evaluating AI-generated responses.
  • Interpret, analyze, and execute tasks accurately in accordance with established guidelines and project requirements.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Master’s or PhD in materials science, physics, chemistry, chemical engineering, or a highly related field.
  • English proficiency at CEFR C1 level or higher.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Specialized expertise in one or more subfields of materials science, including but not limited to energy materials, semiconductors, nanomaterials, metals and alloys, biomaterials, polymers, elastomers, ceramics, glasses, or other interdisciplinary materials-related fields.
  • Advanced expertise in materials science demonstrated through multiple publications in reputable, peer-reviewed journals or relevant patents, preferably including one or more first-author publications.
  • Strong research skills and the ability to navigate scientific literature, specialized databases, and online information resources.
  • Excellent communication, interpersonal, analytical, and organizational skills.
  • Strong reading comprehension and critical-thinking skills, with the ability to exercise sound independent judgment when working with limited information.
  • A strong interest in technological advancement, scientific progress, and innovation.
  • Previous experience in AI tutoring, AI model evaluation, or related applications of artificial intelligence.
  • Teaching or tutoring experience in academic or professional settings.
  • Experience in technical writing, science journalism, scientific communication, or other professional writing roles.

LOCATION AND OTHER EXPECTATIONS:

  • This is a remote role which may be performed from the following countries:
    • United States
    • United Kingdom
    • Canada
    • Australia
    • India
  • This role may be offered as a full-time or part-time position, depending on role / business needs and candidate availability. Full-time positions are preferred and require working standard business hours in your local time zone.
  • Positions are typically offered as fixed-term employment contracts of 6 months. Extensions or conversion to a permanent role may be available based on business needs.
  • For US-based candidates, please note that we are unable to hire in Wyoming and Illinois at this time.
  • We are unable to provide visa sponsorship.
  • Travel to a SpaceXSI site may be required.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

US-based candidates: $45/hour - $75/hour depending on factors including relevant experience, skills, education, geographic location, and qualifications. International candidates: Information will be provided to you during the recruitment process.

Benefits vary based on employment type, location, and jurisdiction. Benefits for eligible US-based positions include health insurance, 401(k) plan, and paid sick leave. Specific details and role-specific information will be provided to you during the interview process.

title: Cybersecurity Presales Intern - GPSU/Heartland (Tulsa)
description:
GuidePoint Security provides trusted cybersecurity expertise, solutions and services that help organizations make better decisions and minimize risk. By taking a three-tiered, holistic approach for evaluating security posture and ecosystems, GuidePoint enables some of the nation’s top organizations, such as Fortune 500 companies and U.S. government agencies, to identify threats, optimize resources and integrate best-fit solutions that mitigate risk.

Overview

As part of the GPSU program, we are seeking a Cybersecurity Presales Intern to support GuidePoint Security's Heartland region. In this role, you will get hands-on experience in three core areas: certification and technical foundations, presales and client engagement, technical delivery and writing, and vendor knowledge. Experienced practitioners will mentor you directly on real work, not simulations. You don't need prior experience in this exact role, but you do need technical aptitude, a habit of learning on your own, and real curiosity about cybersecurity.

You must be pursuing or have recently completed a Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, or a related field. We will also consider Associate's degree candidates who show self-study and lab work. Non-traditional backgrounds are welcome to apply, including career changers, military veterans, and self-taught candidates, as long as they show equivalent knowledge. You will work with the Heartland presales team, shadowing senior consultants on client engagements and attending internal presales and delivery meetings to learn the business. This internship is a pathway to full-time employment. Candidates who show competence and cultural fit may receive a full-time offer, with a growth path to Pre-Sales Cybersecurity Technical Advisor and a long-term path toward CISSP-level certifications and senior advisory roles.

Responsibilities

  • Certification & Technical Foundation
    • Build a certification foundation with company-sponsored exam vouchers, including Security+, Network+, CySA+, and cloud certifications
    • Complete hands-on lab work to strengthen skills in networking, operating systems, cloud, and security
    • Take part in CTF platforms such as HackTheBox and TryHackMe to build practical offensive and defensive skills
    • Gain exposure to SIEM, vulnerability scanning, and endpoint security tools in lab and real-world settings under mentorship
  • Presales & Client Engagement
    • Shadow senior consultants on real client engagements, gaining early exposure to professional security consulting
    • Attend internal presales and delivery meetings to learn how GuidePoint scopes, sells, and delivers solutions
    • Practice explaining technical concepts to non-technical audiences in client-facing settings under mentorship
    • Support the preparation of presales materials, demos, and technical discussions alongside the Heartland team
  • Technical Writing & Vendor Knowledge
    • Practice technical writing, including executive summaries and findings reports
    • Build vendor-specific product knowledge aligned to GuidePoint's technology partnerships
    • Research and document how partner solutions map to common client security challenges
    • Document lab work, engagement observations, and lessons learned to support your own growth and the team's knowledge base

Qualifications

  • Pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, or a related field. Associate's degree candidates with self-study and lab work, and non-traditional backgrounds with equivalent knowledge, will be considered
  • Foundational knowledge of networking, including TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, HTTP/S, subnetting, VLANs, firewalls, and routing basics
  • Exemplifying leadership tendencies, such as leading student organizations or industry clubs
  • Comfort navigating both Windows and Linux, with command-line proficiency
  • Understanding of core security concepts, including the CIA triad, authentication vs. authorization, encryption basics, and common attack vectors (phishing, malware, ransomware, social engineering)
  • Basic understanding of at least one major cloud provider (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and the shared responsibility model
  • A habit of self-directed learning, shown through home labs, CTFs, blogs, or personal projects
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences
  • Coachable and open to feedback. You don't need to be right, you need to get it right.
  • A self-starter who looks for work without being told, and has a collaborative, team-oriented mindset
  • Professional maturity: punctual, reliable, responsive, and presentable in client-facing settings

Preferred Qualifications

  • Active participation in cybersecurity communities (meetups, BSides, DEFCON, Discord/Slack groups)
  • Any existing certifications (CompTIA ITF+, A+, Network+, Security+)
  • Exposure to a SIEM, vulnerability scanner, or endpoint security tool, even in a lab environment
  • Basic scripting ability (Python, PowerShell, or Bash)
  • Previous customer-facing experience of any kind (retail, help desk, tutoring, etc.)

Internship Details and Expectations

This is a part-time, remote paid internship ($20/hr) that runs for 12 weeks from January 11 - April 2, 2027, with an optional in-person onboarding in Tampa FL during the first week. There is the potential for full-time employment at the end of the internship. During this internship, interns are expected to:

  • Be located near Tulsa, OK, or be willing to relocate there for follow-on full-time hire
  • Be physically located within the United States for the entire internship
  • Work 20-29 hrs/wk during standard business hours supporting the Central Time Zone
  • Have a personal computing device and high-speed internet access during working hours

This position is not available for candidates living in the following states: Alaska, California, Hawaii, New Mexico, New York, Oregon, Washington and Wyoming.

The below perks are for those that join GuidePoint Security for full-time employment only.

We use Greenhouse Software as our applicant tracking system and Zoom Scheduler for HR screen request scheduling. At times, your email may block our communication with you. Please be sure to check your SPAM folder so that you don't miss updates on your application.

Why GuidePoint?

GuidePoint Security is a rapidly growing, profitable, privately-held value added reseller that focuses exclusively on Information Security. Since its inception in 2011, GuidePoint has grown to over 1,300 employees, established strategic partnerships with leading security vendors, and serves as a trusted advisor to more than 6,200 customers.

Firmly-defined core values drive all aspects of the business, which have been paramount to the company’s success and establishment of an enjoyable workplace atmosphere. At GuidePoint, your colleagues are knowledgeable, skilled, and experienced and will seek to collaborate and provide mentorship and guidance at every opportunity.

This is a unique and rare opportunity to grow your career along with one of the fastest growing companies in the nation.

Some added perks….

  • Remote workforce primarily (U.S. based only, some travel may be required for certain positions, working on-site may be required for Federal positions)
  • Group Medical Insurance options: Zero Deductible PPO Plan (GuidePoint pays 90% of the premium for employees and 70% for family plans (spouse/children/family) or High Deductible Health Plan with HSA (GuidePoint pays 100% of the employees premiums and 75% for family plans (spouse/children/family). If you choose the High Deductible / HSA plan, GPS will contribute in 4 equal quarterly installments: ($850 per EE annually / $1750 per family annually (includes spouse/children/family options)
  • Group Dental Insurance: GuidePoint pays 100% of the premium for employees and 75% of family plans
  • 12 corporate holidays and a Flexible Time Off (FTO) program
  • Healthy mobile phone and home internet allowance
  • Eligibility for retirement plan after 2 months at open enrollment
  • Pet Benefit Option

title: Director, Global AI Security & CISO Initiatives (Remote, Remote, US)
description:
Job ID: 18432

Alternate Locations:

Newell Brands is a leading consumer products company with a portfolio of iconic brands like Graco®, Coleman®, Oster®, Rubbermaid®, Sharpie® and Yankee Candle® - and 24,000 talented teammates around the world. Our culture is built on values in action: Integrity, Teamwork, Passion for Winning, Ownership, and Leadership. We work together to win, grow, and make a real impact—supported by a high-performing, inclusive, and collaborative environment where you can be your best, every day.

Job Overview

Newell Brands is seeking a strategic, highly collaborative, and execution-focused Director, Global AI Security & CISO Initiatives, to serve within the Office of the Chief Information Security Officer. This individual will be a trusted advisor and operational partner to the CISO, helping to translate Newell Brands’ information security strategy into coordinated action across the enterprise.

The Director will lead the overall operating rhythm of the Information Security organization, drive strategic planning/project management, and ensure that the CISO’s priorities are effectively communicated and executed. The role will connect strategy, governance, financial management, talent, communications, and program delivery while fostering strong partnerships across Information Technology, (IT) Legal, Internal Audit, Privacy, Human Resources, Finance, Newell Brands operating segments, Information Security, and leadership.

The successful candidate will combine business acumen, cybersecurity knowledge, executive presence, sound judgment, and disciplined execution. This position requires someone who can move comfortably between long-term strategy and day-to-day operations, bring clarity to complex issues, and influence outcomes without relying solely on formal authority.

The role focuses primarily on Strategy & Execution (40%), Office of the CISO Operations (30%), and Cybersecurity Capabilities Measurement (30%).

Strategy & Execution

  • Partner with the CISO and Information Security leadership team to execute the CISO’s strategy, roadmap, priorities, and annual objectives.

  • Translate strategic priorities into measurable initiatives, milestones, accountabilities, and outcomes.

  • Identify dependencies, risks, resource constraints, and execution gaps across the security portfolio, escalating issues and facilitatingtimely decisions.

  • Lead high-priority initiatives and special projects on behalf of the CISO, particularly those that cross organizational or functional boundaries.

  • Ensure Information Security priorities remain aligned with Newell Brands’ business objectives, transformation agenda, risk appetite, and Information Technology strategy.

Office of the CISO Operations

  • Establish and manage the operating rhythm for the Office of the CISO, including leadership meetings, strategy sessions, business reviews, planning cycles, and executive updates.

  • Develop agendas, decision materials, action logs, and follow-up mechanisms that improve leadership-team effectiveness and accountability.

  • Prepare the CISO briefings for executive meetings, Board and committee engagements, regulatory discussions, business reviews, and other critical interactions.

  • Coordinate the flow of information into and out of the CISO’s office, ensuring that decisions, commitments, and priorities are clearly communicated.

  • Provide visibility into security spending, resource allocation, vendor commitments, and expected business outcomes.

  • Partners with InfoSec service tower owners on their budgets and manages the overall InfoSec budget: monthly financial performance, forecasting, etc.

  • Support portfolio management across security programs, projects, services, and technology investments.

  • Help evaluate investment proposals and ensure resources are directed toward the organization’s highest priority risks and strategic objectives.

  • Partner with security leaders to define and monitor key performance indicators, key risk indicators, strategic outcomes, and program health measures.

  • Develop concise, decision-oriented presentations and communications that translate complex cybersecurity matters into business and risk terms.

  • Monitor progress against the Information Security roadmap and facilitate corrective action when initiatives are at risk.

  • Promote consistent methods for prioritization, decision-making, and accountability across the information security organization.

Cybersecurity Capabilities Measurement (30%)

  • Coordinate Information Security’s support for Newell Brands’ Quantum Leap AI program and other enterprise transformation initiatives.

  • Working with the Cyber Risk Partners, help ensure cybersecurity considerations are incorporated into AI initiatives from the outset.

  • Track security commitments and dependencies associated with AI adoption and emerging technologies.

  • Through deep analysis of Newell’s current information security capabilities, as well as viable market options, identify opportunities to use artificial intelligence and automation to enhance security detection, prevention, analysis, and operational efficiency.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in cybersecurity, information technology, business administration, risk management, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.

  • Eight or more years of progressive experience in cybersecurity, technology, security strategy and execution, or a related field.

  • Demonstrated experience supporting senior executives and leading complex, cross-functional initiatives in a large enterprise environment (globally).

  • Strong understanding of cybersecurity strategy, governance, and common security operating models.

  • Proven ability to translate complex technical and risk information into clear business implications and executive-level communications.

  • Experience with strategic planning, performance management, financial planning, portfolio management, or organizational operations.

  • Exceptional written, verbal, presentation, facilitation, and interpersonal skills.

  • Strong analytical judgment, organizational discipline, and attention to detail.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, navigate ambiguity, and deliver high-quality work under tight deadlines.

  • Professional certifications such as Certified Information Systems Security Professional, (CISSP) Certified Information Security Manager, (CISM) or equivalent.

  • Proven experience using AI tools, including major large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, and Claude.

  • Demonstrated discretion and experience handling highly confidential information.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in business administration, cybersecurity, information systems, or a related field.

  • Experience working in a global consumer products, manufacturing, retail, or similarly complex multinational organization.

  • Experience developing materials for Boards of Directors, executive committees, auditors, or regulators.

  • Previous experience in cybersecurity strategy, transformation, or security leadership role.

The remote base pay range for this position is from $150,400 to $188,000. Salary will be based on prior experience related to the skills required for this position.

Newell Brands (NASDAQ: NWL) is a leading global consumer goods company with a strong portfolio of well-known brands, including Rubbermaid, Sharpie, Graco, Coleman, Rubbermaid Commercial Products, Yankee Candle, Paper Mate, FoodSaver, Dymo, EXPO, Elmer’s, Oster, NUK, Spontex and Campingaz. We are focused on delighting consumers by lighting up everyday moments. Newell Brands and its subsidiaries are Equal Opportunity Employers and comply with applicable employment laws. EOE/M/F/Vet/Disabled are encouraged to apply.

description:
Lumen is the trusted network for the AI‑powered world, connecting people, data, and applications through our expansive fiber network and connected ecosystem. We enable secure, high‑performance connectivity across cloud, edge, and AI workloads for enterprises, governments, and communities.

At Lumen, you’ll work on infrastructure customers rely on today and build for what’s next, where performance, security, and resilience matter.

This is a high accountability environment where bold ideas drive real innovation for our customers, partners, and industry. The work is challenging, expectations are clear, and trust is built into how we operate. If you’re ready to take ownership, deliver meaningful impact, and help shape the future of AI‑ready connectivity, join us today.

The Role

Black Lotus Labs has an opening for a Senior Lead Threat Analyst that will leverage Lumen’s unique visibility to hunt, investigate, and scale discovery of evolving malicious threats, provide mission-relevant intelligence, and support mitigations on large networks. Our global visibility into one of the world’s largest and most interconnected IP backbones, combined with our computing cluster and analytic platforms, presents exciting opportunities to integrate machine learning, graph analytics, automation, and approved AI-enabled tools as we find new ways to hunt for threats across the internet. Black Lotus Labs has detected and disrupted key evolving threats at an internet scale for years.

This position will work alongside Black Lotus Labs advanced security researchers, data engineers, malware reverse engineers, data scientists, and our customers to tackle evolving threats accelerated by technologies like our Hadoop ecosystem (HBase, HDFS, Spark, Kafka, AirFlow), Elasticsearch and Redis clusters, Docker using Docker Swarm, malware environment, a network of honeypots, and modern AI-assisted research and development capabilities.
This is a close-knit, experienced, amazingly smart team that you can be a part of and help build out.

This position requires an active TS/SCI security clearance w/ CI Poly.

Location

The Main Responsibilities

  • Research latest threat attacker tools, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) with a goal of automating detection.
  • Work with cyber operators, when requested, to conduct in-depth investigations on cyber threat activity and provide mitigation guidance.
  • Automate investigations through Python scripting and data analysis using visualization in Jupyter Notebooks and Grafana
  • Build and maintain trust relationships with other intelligence teams, law enforcement, and other outside groups.
  • Support customer RFIs on incidents and emerging threats.

  • Scripting experience with Python and familiarity with distributed computing.
  • Extensive experience hunting threat actors and developing algorithms and techniques to identify new threats from large data sets.

  • Strong analytical thinking and ability to quickly pick up new methods, tools and programming languages.

  • Demonstrable knowledge of several of the following areas: cybersecurity concepts, network protocols, firewalls, IDS/IPS systems, cyber threat hunting, malware analysis tools and techniques, cyber threat intelligence, common threat actor TTPs, application security concepts, cloud security fundamentals.
  • Ability to rapidly develop proficiency in unfamiliar technical domains through foundational analytical skills, self-directed learning, and effective use of AI-assisted research and problem-solving tools.

Well experienced candidates may also have the following skills:

  • Previous work experience with Department of Defense (DoD), Intelligence Community, or other government agencies (e.g., DHS, DOE, VA, etc.)
  • Experience with Spark and distributed computing
  • Experience developing automation and analysis in Python-based environments.
  • Ability to work with others in providing direction and assisting in learning new topics.
  • Experience using generative AI, AI-assisted coding, retrieval-augmented analysis, or agent-based workflows in cyber research, threat hunting, or intelligence production.

    Preferred:
  • Proficient in analyzing NetFlow data to identify unusual patterns and potential security threats.
  • Interest in conducting trend analysis to uncover patterns and emerging threats, enabling proactive defense strategies.
  • Demonstrated ability to responsibly leverage AI-enabled tools within a regulated or mission-focused environment while maintaining data protection requirements, analytical integrity, and human accountability for findings and recommendations

title: Discipline Undecided
description:
The Discipline Undecided path is for candidates early in their careers who have not yet committed to a specific technology discipline. You are not expected to arrive with a declared specialty — this path is designed for you to discover it here. TEECOM is growing — multiple teams across the US, UK, and India are actively hiring to grow their teams.

When you apply here, you will go through an adapted assessment designed for earlier-career candidates. Your assessment evaluates your foundational aptitude, learning orientation, and technical baseline — not discipline-specific depth.

Entry into this path is at the Designer I level. If you already have meaningful professional experience in a specific discipline — ICT/Telecom, Security, AV, Wireless, or another — apply to that discipline directly. This path is for candidates without deep experience in any single discipline who are ready to learn.

Discipline Undecided at TEECOM

    TEECOM pairs new hires with experienced mentors across multiple practice areas, giving them direct exposure to real project work in ICT/Telecom, Security, AV, Wireless, BIM/Production, and other disciplines before they choose a primary specialty. Your discipline emerges from what you discover at TEECOM — not from a decision you have to make before your first day.

    Work at the Designer I level focuses on learning through doing: applying discipline fundamentals, supporting engineering and production teams, and building your technical foundation through hands-on project experience and structured mentorship. You will work closely with your mentor — an experienced engineer or discipline lead who will guide your development, assign your work, and help you grow.

    Those who demonstrate strong capability and choose a discipline typically advance to Designer II with a clear specialization.

What We're Looking For

    We are looking for early-career candidates who are curious, coachable, and treat “I don’t know yet” as a starting point — not a stopping point.

    • Recent graduate or early-career professional with exposure to technology systems, AEC, or a related technical field
    • Foundational technical aptitude — you can read drawings, learn tools quickly, and ask good questions
    • Genuine curiosity about how technology systems work in buildings and facilities
    • Degree in any four-year engineering discipline, computer science, technology management, or a related technical field — or equivalent hands-on experience
    • Engineer-In-Training (EIT) or equivalent preferred
    • No declared discipline specialty required
    • Eagerness to learn from mentors and grow through real project work

TEECOM is a fully remote consulting firm. We hire across all US states, the UK, and India. Our projects span the globe — some roles involve international travel, so share your comfort level with your recruiter.

If you're ready to learn your discipline by doing real work alongside experienced engineers, apply here.

title: Senior Manager, RevOps (Sales Ops)
description:
Ketch is redefining responsible data use for the AI era. Thousands of brands rely on our software to responsibly collect, control, and activate compliant, clean data across their enterprise ecosystem. The Ketch Data Permissioning Platform simplifies privacy and consent operations, increases revenue from advertising, data, and AI initiatives, and builds trust with customers and partners. Unlike legacy tools that stop at cookie banners, Ketch governs how data is actually used across a company’s entire stack, with no-code setup that gets customers live in weeks, not quarters.

As privacy regulations expand across the globe and AI transforms how companies use data, the demand for what Ketch has built has never been greater. Data privacy sits at the intersection of law, technology, and consumer trust, making it one of the most exciting and fastest-moving fields in software today.

Why Join Us?

At Ketch, we’re serious about our values of passion, growth, grit, collaboration, and integrity. We’re a 65-person, Series B company backed by top-tier investors, and we’re looking for people who want to do the best work of their careers while shaping how the world handles data responsibly. We’re a rapidly growing, fast-paced, mission-based organization filled with a passionate, close-knit team all operating at the top of their game.

Benefits and Perks

  • Competitive medical, dental, and vision coverage, with 100% of premiums paid for US-based full-time employees

  • Unlimited PTO, with employees encouraged to take at least 15 days a year

  • 10 paid company holidays

  • Paid parental leave

  • Remote-friendly with flexible scheduling built around core collaboration hours

  • Commuter benefits for office-based employees

About The Role

You’ll work hand-in-hand with GTM leadership and the sales team and will partner regularly with Finance, Legal, and Marketing to help optimize the deal cycle. You’ll own Sales Operations end-to-end: the deal desk, pricing strategy and approvals, pipeline and forecast infrastructure, and the reporting and analysis that helps Sales leadership run the business. You will report directly to the VP of Revenue Operations/SMB Sales, and you two will partner closely on the broader revenue operations agenda.

At Ketch, operations sits at the intersection of systems, process, and data: you’ll design systems that minimize manual processes wherever reasonable – building for scale rather than an automation that gets torn out in six months. Those systems capture the data needed to analyze GTM processes, and those analyses drive the next round of process and systems improvements.

AI is changing what a lean operations team can accomplish. Rather than building out separate ops leads, system admins, and pods of analysts, we are looking for one exceptional operator who works with AI to cover that ground: streamlining systems improvements and building AI-powered tools that put data and analysis directly in the hands of Sales leaders.

This is a remote role within the United States.

Responsibilities

Deal Desk & Pricing:

  • Own the deal desk. Structure, review, and shepherd non-standard deals from quote through approval, and be the person Sales calls when a deal does not fit the standard shape. Keep the approval path fast and predictable, and make the standard shape the easy one to sell.

  • Own pricing strategy and operations: packaging, price books, discount guardrails, approval thresholds, and the quote-to-close mechanics that enforce them. Analyze realized discounting, win rates by price point, and deal shape to recommend pricing changes, and build the case for them with data.

  • Partner with Finance and Legal on contract terms, order forms, and revenue recognition inputs so the deal desk speeds deals up rather than slowing them down.

Pipeline, Forecast & Reporting:

  • Own pipeline hygiene, stage definitions, and the forecast cadence. Give Sales leadership a forecast they trust and can defend, and the reporting to see where it is drifting before quarter end.

  • Build the reporting and self-serve dashboards Sales leaders, managers, and reps use daily: pipeline coverage, conversion by stage and segment, velocity, quota attainment, activity-to-outcome linkage, and territory performance.

ABOUT THE COMPANY

Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE: RSG) is a leader in the environmental services industry. We provide customers with the most complete set of products and services, including recycling, waste, special waste, hazardous waste and field services. Our industry-leading commitments to advance circularity and support decarbonization are helping deliver on our vision to partner with customers to create a more sustainable world.


In 2025, Republic’s total company revenue was $16.6 billion, and adjusted EBITDA was $5.3 billion. We serve 13 million customers and operate more than 1,000 locations, including collection and transfer stations, recycling and polymer centers, treatment facilities, and landfills.


Although we operate across North America, the collection, recycling, treatment, or disposal of materials is a local business, and the dynamics and opportunities differ in each market we serve. By combining local operational management with standardized business practices, we drive greater operating efficiencies across the company while maintaining day-to-day operational decisions at the local level, closest to the customer.


Our customers, including small businesses, major corporations and municipalities, want a partner with the expertise and capabilities to effectively manage their multiple recycling and waste streams. They choose Republic Services because we are committed to exceeding their expectations and helping them achieve their sustainability goals. Our 42,000 team members understand that it's not just what we do that matters, but how we do it.


Our company values guide our daily actions:

  • Safe: We protect the livelihoods of our colleagues and communities.
  • Committed to Serve: We go above and beyond to exceed our customers’ expectations.
  • Environmentally Responsible: We take action to improve our environment.
  • Driven: We deliver results in the right way.
  • Human-Centered: We respect the dignity and unique potential of every person.

We are proud of our high employee engagement score of 86. We have an inclusive and diverse culture where every voice counts. In addition, our team positively impacted 5.1 million people in 2024 through the Republic Services Charitable Foundation and local community grants. These projects are designed to meet the specific needs of the communities we serve, with a focus on building sustainable neighborhoods.


STRATEGY

Republic Services’ strategy is designed to generate profitable growth. Through acquisitions and industry advancements, we safely and sustainably manage our customers’ multiple waste streams through a North American footprint of vertically integrated assets.

We focus on three areas of growth to meet the increasing needs of our customers: recycling and waste, environmental solutions and sustainability innovation.

With our integrated approach, strengthening our position in one area advances other areas of our business. For example, as we grow volume in recycling and waste, we collect additional material to bolster our circularity capabilities. And as we expand environmental solutions, we drive additional opportunities to provide these services to our existing recycling and waste customers.


Recycling and Waste

We continue to expand our recycling and waste business footprint throughout North America through organic growth and targeted acquisitions. The 13 million customers we serve and our more than 5 million pick-ups per day provide us with a distinct advantage. We aggregate materials at scale, unlocking new opportunities for advanced recycling. In addition, we are cross-selling new products and services to better meet our customers’ specific needs.


Environmental Solutions

Our comprehensive environmental solutions capabilities help customers safely manage their most technical waste streams. We are expanding both our capabilities and our geographic footprint. We see strong growth opportunities for our offerings, including PFAS remediation, an increasing customer need.

Sustainability Innovation

Republic’s recent innovations to advance circularity and decarbonization demonstrate our unique ability to leverage sustainability as a platform for growth.


The Republic Services Polymer Center is the nation’s first integrated plastics recycling facility. These innovative sites process rigid plastics from our recycling centers, producing recycled materials that promote true bottle-to-bottle circularity. We also formed Blue Polymers, a joint venture with Ravago, to develop facilities that will further process plastic material from our Polymer Centers to help meet the growing demand for sustainable packaging. We are building a network of Polymer Centers and Blue Polymer facilities across North America.


Our customers are increasingly looking for decarbonization solutions, and we are leveraging our network of landfills to meet that need. Republic is committed to harnessing landfill gas, a natural byproduct of decomposing waste, and converting it to energy. Republic has partnered with renewable gas developers to construct Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) plants at our landfills, expanding beyond the 77 projects we currently have to make progress towards our goal to beneficially reuse 50% more biogas by 2030 (2017 baseline year).

title: Associate Director, Analytical Development
description:
Who We Are:

Cogent Biosciences is a publicly traded biotechnology company focused on developing novel precision therapies to treat a broad range of patients with unmet medical needs. Cogent’s lead program, bezuclastinib, is designed to selectively and potently inhibit exon 17 mutations found within the KIT receptor tyrosine kinase, including KIT D816V. KIT D816V is responsible for driving a rare and serious condition called Systemic Mastocytosis, and exon 17 mutations are also found in patients with gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST), a type of cancer with strong dependence on oncogenic KIT signaling. Bezuclastinib has exhibited promising initial data across all three trials: APEX in AdvSM, SUMMIT in NonAdvSM and PEAK in GIST, including an encouraging safety profile across 600+ patients in single agent and combination dosing.

The Role:

The Associate Director, Analytical Development, is responsible for leading analytical activities across Cogent’s development portfolio and commercial product. This role within CMC will partner closely with Regulatory CMC, Quality, and external CDMOs to ensure analytical data, reports, methods, specifications, and regulatory-supporting documentation are accurate, phase-appropriate, and aligned with program objectives. The successful candidate will provide technical leadership in the review, interpretation, and communication of analytical results while ensuring high-quality documentation supports development, commercialization, and global regulatory submissions.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the preparation, review, and approval of analytical reports, data summaries, protocols, specifications, methods, and other CMC technical documentation.
  • Review analytical data packages supporting release testing, stability studies, drug substance, intermediates, and drug product manufacturing activities.
  • Partner closely with Regulatory CMC, Quality, and external CDMOs to ensure timely delivery of analytical documentation and reports.
  • Support analytical method development, validation, qualification, transfer, and lifecycle management activities across development and commercial programs.
  • Author, review, and manage technical documents including analytical methods, validation protocols and reports, specifications, trend reports, and regulatory submission documentation.
  • Coordinate analytical reporting activities for drug substance and drug product stability programs and ensure data are accurately documented and communicated.
  • Support the preparation and review of CMC sections for regulatory submissions, responses to health authorities, and other regulatory filings.
  • Participate in analytical investigations related to deviations, OOS, OOT, and laboratory events, ensuring documentation meets quality and regulatory expectations.
  • Collaborate with external laboratories and CDMOs to ensure analytical deliverables are scientifically sound, compliant, and aligned with program timelines.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on analytical reporting processes, data integrity, document quality, and operational efficiency.

Qualifications:

    • PhD in Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Chemical Engineering, or a related scientific discipline with 8+ years of relevant industry experience, OR Master's degree with 10+ years of experience, OR Bachelor's degree with 12+ years of experience.
    • Experience in analytical development, analytical reporting, CMC technical writing, or related pharmaceutical development functions.
    • Strong understanding of small molecule analytical development, method validation, method transfer, stability testing, specifications, and control strategies.
    • Demonstrated experience authoring, reviewing, and approving technical documents including analytical methods, protocols, reports, and regulatory-supporting documentation.
    • Experience reviewing analytical data generated by CDMOs, CROs, and external testing laboratories.
    • Working knowledge of analytical techniques such as HPLC/UPLC, GC, dissolution, spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, wet chemistry, particle size analysis, and related pharmaceutical characterization methods.
    • Familiarity with ICH, FDA, EMA, and other global regulatory requirements related to analytical development and CMC documentation.
    • Strong scientific writing, data interpretation, problem-solving, and project management skills.
    • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to effectively communicate complex technical information to diverse audiences.
    • Proven ability to work effectively within a cross-functional matrix organization and build strong relationships with internal stakeholders and external partners.
    • Highly organized with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced biotech environment.

    Preferred Qualifications

    • Experience supporting late-stage development or commercial programs.
    • Experience contributing to IND, NDA, MAA, or other global regulatory submissions.

$185,000 - 215,000 USD

Target Bonus: 20%

Boulder, CO: Our Boulder location is home to Cogent’s discovery research organization and a key scientific hub with strong leadership based on site. Situated in the greater Denver-Boulder biopharmaceutical corridor, this office plays a central role in advancing our discovery efforts and pipeline.

title: Associate Director, Clinical Pharmacology (USA - Remote, US)
description:
Bausch + Lomb (NYSE/TSX: BLCO) is a leading global eye health company dedicated to protecting and enhancing the gift of sight for millions of people around the world—from the moment of birth through every phase of life. Our mission is simple, yet powerful: helping you see better, to live better.

Our comprehensive portfolio of over 400 products is fully integrated and built to serve our customers across the full spectrum of their eye health needs throughout their lives. Our iconic brand is built on the deep trust and loyalty of our customers established over our 170-year history. We have a significant global research, development, manufacturing and commercial footprint of approximately 13,000 employees and a presence in approximately 100 countries, extending our reach to billions of potential customers across the globe. We have long been associated with many of the most significant advances in eye health, and we believe we are well positioned to continue leading the advancement of eye health in the future.

This is an exciting time at Bausch + Lomb as we build our industry leading pharmaceutical and consumer pipeline. Over the course of the Company’s history, Bausch + Lomb has always stood at the forefront of cutting-edge scientific and technological optical advancements, and today, Bausch + Lomb is more focused than ever on developing and offering new treatments to meet unmet eye health needs. This role will enable our aspiration of the Bausch + Lomb mission of helping people see better to live better. This is an opportunity for a highly motivated translational scientist to be a key scientific contributor to building a best-in-class pharmaceutical and consumer pipeline.

Responsibilities:

Scientific role that contributes through translational nonclinical PK, PK/PD, ADME, clinical pharmacology and pharmacometrics in establishing Bausch + Lomb as the leader in eye health scientific innovation.

Technical Excellence

  • Leads clinical pharmacology, PK, PD, and pharmacometrics activities across multiple programs spanning the Rx ophthalmic pipeline (e.g., dry eye, glaucoma, retinal disease, ocular surface disease) and consumer eye health pipeline.
  • Contributes to action plans that best meet drug development business objectives, including candidate selection, first-in-human strategy, dose selection and justification, special population strategy, and life-cycle management.
  • Provides overall clinical pharmacology timelines and deliverables to inform portfolio prioritization and resourcing decisions.
  • Negotiates with other functional areas on project outcomes and deliverables to balance conflicting demands of time, cost, and quality/performance.
  • Contributes to development of departmental goals and influences strategic PK/PD decisions for the department.

Scientific and Technical Accountability

  • Evaluates technical and scientific aspects of projects, including ocular and systemic PK, ocular bioavailability and distribution, PK/PD modeling, exposure–response analysis, population PK, PBPK, and quantitative systems pharmacology where applicable.
  • Designs and oversees nonclinical PK, TK and clinical pharmacology studies, including first-in-human, ocular PK, drug–drug interaction, QT/QTc, hepatic/renal impairment, pediatric, and bioequivalence/bridging studies relevant to ophthalmic products.
  • Applies scientific expertise to interpret clinical and nonclinical data and clearly communicates implications to management, including go/no-go recommendations.
  • Maintains up-to-date knowledge of PK/PD data analysis, modeling and simulation methods and software (e.g., NONMEM, Monolix, Phoenix WinNonlin/NLME, R, Simcyp, GastroPlus, MATLAB).

Regulatory Strategy and Submissions

  • Reviews study protocols and reports including for regulatory filings and anticipates regulatory questions.
  • Leads authoring of pharmacokinetics and clinical pharmacology sections of regulatory documents including IND/CTA, IB, briefing packages, pre-IND/EOP2/pre-NDA meeting materials, NDA/BLA/MAA/505(b)(2), DMFs, and periodic safety updates.
  • Leads responses to health authority questions and represents Pharmacokinetics and Clinical Pharmacology in agency interactions.
  • Ensures alignment with ICH, FDA, EMA, and other applicable guidance for ophthalmic and systemic products.

Team Member Activities

  • Identifies issues and supports issue resolution; conducts risk assessments and helps develop contingency plans; assures projects remain aligned with strategic objectives.
  • Provides scientific and strategic consultation to R&D, Regulatory, and all levels of management on critical development decisions.
  • Identifies and develops process improvement initiatives and reviews recommendations with management for approval and sponsorship.
  • May conduct due diligence assessments for in-licensing, acquisition, and partnership opportunities; summarizes pharmacokinetic and clinical pharmacology findings and represents the function on due diligence teams.
  • Communicates and presents key pharmacokinetics and clinical pharmacology information and strategy to management, regulatory agencies, external peers, scientific advisory boards, and KOLs.

Requirements:

Education and Experience

  • PhD in Pharmaceutical Sciences, Clinical Pharmacology, Pharmacometrics, Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacology, Biomedical Engineering, or related discipline with typically 6+ years of relevant experience.
  • Experience with PK, PBPK, PK/PD, pharmacometrics or systems pharmacology, and/or drug metabolism and transporters. Ophthalmic drug development, topical/ocular PK, or ocular pharmacology experience is strongly preferred.

Technical and Functional Knowledge

  • Demonstrated leadership in PK/PD, biopharmaceutics, and pharmacometric activities from planning through implementation and completion across multiple projects.
  • Experience across a range of development phases (discovery support through Phase 3 and life-cycle management); experience with 505(b)(2), ANDA bridging, or OTC/consumer product pathways is advantageous given the Rx and Consumer pipeline.
  • Working knowledge of pharmaceutical drug development processes, ICH guidelines, and FDA/EMA clinical pharmacology expectations, including ophthalmic-specific guidance.
  • Proficiency with modeling and simulation tools (e.g., NONMEM, Phoenix WinNonlin/NLME, Monolix, R, Simcyp, GastroPlus).

Communication and Team Skills

  • Communicates openly and honestly with all colleagues.
  • Connects unrelated concepts and generates original or unique ideas.
  • Influences colleagues to achieve cross-functional alignment.
  • Manages conflict and difficult conversations in a constructive, transparent way.
  • Expert in industry best practices & trends with the ability to drive change.
  • Exceptional influencing, partnership, and collaboration skills to solve scientific and business problems and drive results.
  • Experience in the selection and oversight of vendors.
  • Knowledge of the cGMP practices and compliance requirements.
  • Excellent written, presentation, and verbal communication skills.

title: Electrical Hazard Support Representative
description:
About Ting Labs

We’re on a mission to save lives and property, leading the next wave in smart home technology and fire prevention with Ting. This intelligent sensor and concierge service monitors a home’s electrical network to detect electrical hazards that often lead to the most devastating and catastrophic fires. While on the job preventing fires inside a home, Ting also helps monitor the electrical grid, contributing to increased community fire safety and reduced environmental impact that comes with fire reduction. We’re steadfastly addressing the long-underserved realm of electrical fire prevention with leading-edge technology and embarking on the next stage of our growth. Visit for more information.

About the Role:

The Electrical Hazard Support Representative manages a high volume of calls, texts, and emails with homeowners whose Ting monitoring system has identified an electrical fire hazard. This role combines customer communication with technical troubleshooting, analyzing Ting data while guiding homeowners through established troubleshooting procedures.

Representatives work closely with homeowners and engineers, gathering information, identifying patterns, documenting findings, and supporting electrical hazard investigations. The role requires strong communication, critical thinking, attention to detail, and the ability to manage frequent customer interactions while interpreting technical information.

We’re looking for motivated individuals who are eager to learn, enjoy problem-solving, and want to support Ting’s mission of preventing electrical fires. No degree or specific technical background is required. Experience in customer service, technical support, or call centers is a plus, along with familiarity with customer management and ticketing systems.

Strong candidates communicate clearly, stay organized, take initiative, and follow through consistently. Above all, we value a willingness to learn, analytical thinking, and a genuine commitment to helping homeowners.

Job Duties:
  • Technical Troubleshooting and Analysis: Analyze electrical monitoring data, identify patterns, and investigate electrical hazards using established procedures and technical tools. Apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills to evaluate findings and determine appropriate next steps.
  • Customer Communication and Phone Support: Spend a significant portion of the workday speaking directly with customers over the phone to gather information, walk through troubleshooting steps, and explain technical findings. Additional communication includes text messages and email.
  • Signal and Pattern Recognition: Learn to interpret graphical data, recognize electrical hazard signals, and identify unusual patterns or changes that may indicate electrical issues within a customer's home.
  • Investigation Support and Escalation: Complete initial troubleshooting activities and assist engineers with more complex electrical investigations. Gather additional information, conduct follow-up calls, and help move investigations toward resolution.
  • Documentation: Maintain accurate and detailed notes of customer conversations, troubleshooting steps, and findings to ensure engineers and other team members can continue investigations efficiently without repeating previous steps.
  • Teamwork: Collaborate with engineers, team leads, and other technicians to investigate potential electrical hazards, share observations, ask questions, and contribute to problem-solving.
  • Continuous Improvement: Participate in ongoing technical training, develop troubleshooting and analytical skills, and help identify opportunities to improve procedures, documentation, and team efficiency.
  • Work Schedule and Travel: Work remotely with flexibility to accommodate rotating schedules, including nights, weekends, and holidays. Occasional travel may be required for in-person training and team meetings.
Requirements:
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to explain technical information clearly and professionally through phone calls, text messages, and email.
  • Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret information, recognize patterns, and follow structured troubleshooting procedures.
  • Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage a high volume of customer interactions while maintaining accurate documentation.
  • Self-motivated, adaptable, and comfortable working independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced remote environment.
  • Willingness to learn new technical concepts and systems. Previous experience in customer service, technical support, or electrical troubleshooting is a plus but not required.
What We Offer:
  • Competitive salary + equity.
  • The ability to make, own and carry out decisions.
  • Health, dental, and vision insurance.
  • 401(k) with match.

Ting Labs is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status.

Opportunity Overview

As a Senior ML / AI Engineer at Teradyne, you will design, build, and operationalize the machine learning and AI solutions that power our IT organization, and you will prepare the team—technically and operationally—to own the AI solutions Teradyne develops internally. Reporting to the Enterprise AI/Data Product Manager within the Enterprise Architecture and Data organization, you will bridge solution development and production ownership, ensuring our AI solutions are reliable, governed, and sustainable long after they are first built.

This is a deeply technical, hands-on role spanning classical machine learning and modern generative and agentic AI. You will develop ML/AI solutions requested by the IT organization—predictive and classification models, GenAI assistants, RAG workflows, and intelligent automation—and engineer the MLOps/LLMOps practices, pipelines, and playbooks that allow the team to operate and continuously improve them. You will work across our enterprise AI stack—primarily Microsoft Azure (Azure AI Foundry and Microsoft Copilot Studio), Anthropic Claude, and Google Vertex AI and Snowflake Cortex AI—grounding solutions in trusted enterprise data and integrating with enterprise systems through MCP servers and secure APIs. Your work ensures Teradyne’s AI investments move from experimentation to durable, production-grade capabilities.


ML/AI Solution Development for IT

  • Partner with the AI Enablement Team and the IT organization to translate business problems into ML/AI solutions—predictive and classification models, GenAI assistants, RAG workflows, and intelligent process automation.
  • Design, develop, train, evaluate, and deploy end-to-end ML and generative AI solutions using Azure AI Foundry, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Google Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex AI.
  • Build and integrate AI agents with enterprise data sources, APIs, and MCP servers, grounding models in proprietary Teradyne data through embedding and retrieval pipelines.
  • Apply rigorous experimentation, model selection, and evaluation to deliver solutions that are accurate, performant, and fit for purpose.

Business Outcome: Deliver high-value, production-ready ML/AI solutions that solve real IT and business problems and demonstrate measurable impact.


Operationalizing & Owning Internally Developed AI Solutions

  • Own the transition of internally developed AI solutions from build to production, defining and certifying the release-readiness in accordance to standard set by the AI Platform Operations Team.
  • Implement full model lifecycle management—versioning, model registry, retraining, promotion, and deprecation—so solutions remain accurate and maintainable over time.
  • Define drift, degradation, and retraining criteria for deployed models and agents, and drive tuning and remediation of the underlying solution for the AI Platform Operations Team to execute scheduled retraining and registry operations against these criteria.
  • Partner with the AI Platform Operations Engineer, providing the technical input—model and agent behavior, dependencies, failure modes—needed for the run-books, on-call processes, and handoff standards they own and author.

Business Outcome: Ensure internally developed AI solutions are durable, well-owned, and continuously improved rather than one-off builds.


MLOps / LLMOps Engineering & Automation

  • Engineer reusable, multi-environment MLOps/LLMOps pipelines using Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions to automate the full lifecycle from training and evaluation to deployment.
  • Build CI/CD, testing, and infrastructure-/configuration-as-code for models, prompts, and agents to make releases repeatable, testable, and auditable.
  • Leverage tooling such as Azure Machine Learning, MLflow, and model/feature registries to standardize experimentation, tracking, and deployment.
  • Establish automated evaluation and regression testing (including offline and online evaluation) for both predictive and generative solutions.
  • Design MLOps/LLMOps pipelines for the AI Platform Operations Team to operate in production once deployed, ensuring pipelines are supportable, observable, and handoff-ready.

Business Outcome: Provide standardized, automated delivery pipelines that increase speed, quality, and reliability of AI solution releases.


Team Technical & Process Readiness

  • Establish the technical standards, reference patterns, and reusable frameworks the team needs to build and operate AI solutions consistently.
  • Define and document the processes and playbooks—development, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and support—that prepare the team to own AI solutions end-to-end.
  • Mentor and upskill engineers on ML/AI, MLOps/LLMOps, and agentic AI practices, raising the overall capability and readiness of the team.
  • Champion adoption of best practices and lessons learned across projects to mature the team’s AI operating model.

Business Outcome: Ensure the team is technically and process-ready to own and scale AI solutions with confidence and consistency.


Responsible AI, Governance & Reliability

  • Implement responsible AI practices and technical guardrails for data handling, model usage, and safe, compliant AI behavior.
  • Apply AI security controls to models, agents, and RAG workflows, mitigating risks such as prompt injection and unauthorized data access.
  • Build observability, logging, and audit trails for AI solutions to support explainability, compliance, and troubleshooting.
  • Monitor solution performance, quality, reliability, and cost, and drive continuous improvement against defined metrics.

Business Outcome: Reduce AI risk and improve trust, compliance, and reliability across Teradyne’s deployed AI solutions.


All About You

We seek individuals who share our passion and determination. Our commitment to customer success drives us to go the extra mile. If you’re ready to join us in this mission, take a closer look at the minimum criteria for the position.

  • 8–10 years of experience in ML/AI or software engineering, including at least 3 years building and operating production ML/AI systems and recent hands-on experience with generative and agentic AI.
  • Bachelor’s or advanced degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, or a related field.
  • Strong proficiency in Python and SQL, and experience with ML frameworks such as scikit-learn, PyTorch, or TensorFlow.
  • Hands-on experience building and deploying ML and generative AI solutions with one or more enterprise AI platforms: Azure AI Foundry, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Anthorpic Claude, Cursor, Google Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex AI.
  • Proven MLOps/LLMOps experience—multi-environment pipelines, CI/CD (Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions), Azure Machine Learning, MLflow, and model lifecycle management.
  • Experience with agentic AI orchestration frameworks, RAG, vector databases and embeddings, prompt engineering, and integration via MCP servers and APIs.
  • Experience transitioning AI solutions from development into production ownership, including monitoring, drift detection, retraining, and support.
  • Strong knowledge of model evaluation and testing, AI observability, responsible AI, AI security, and governance frameworks.
  • Multicloud experience with Microsoft Azure as primary and Google Cloud as secondary, integrating with enterprise data on Snowflake and Microsoft Fabric.
  • Poven ability to mentor and upskill teams, fostering a culture of innovation and learning.
  • Strong collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to work across technical and business teams.
  • Analytical mindset with a focus on delivering measurable business outcomes.


Compensation: The base salary range for this role is $133,900-$223,900. This range is a good faith estimate, and the amount of base salary will correspond with experience and skill set. This range can also fluctuate depending on demand and location.

title: Software Engineer, External Integrations & Data
description:
Software Engineer, External Integrations & Data

Location: Remote Canada

Employment Type: Full-time

Level: Senior Software Engineer

About the company

Our Series A client is transforming the building supply industry through innovative technology. Their integrated commerce platform enables independent building suppliers to streamline operations, enhance customer service, and deliver exceptional digital buying experiences. By connecting sales, accounts receivable, operations, and customer engagement into one seamless solution, they help their customers operate more efficiently and drive growth.

Their team is made up of curious, entrepreneurial problem-solvers who thrive in a fast-paced environment. They value innovation, collaboration, and ownership, with a shared focus on building practical solutions that create meaningful impact for their customers and the industry as a whole.

About the Role

We’re looking for a resourceful Software Engineer who thrives on solving problems where the path forward isn’t always obvious. You’ll work on building systems that interact with external platforms, services, and data sources — particularly in situations where official APIs are limited, unavailable, or insufficient for the job.

This role is ideal for an engineer with experience in web scraping, reverse engineering, or building integrations with third-party systems that weren’t necessarily designed to be integrated with.

You’ll help us connect to external sources, extract and normalize messy or unstructured data, and turn it into reliable, structured information that can power modern AI-driven applications. We’re looking for someone who enjoys figuring out how things work under the hood, navigating undocumented systems, and building robust solutions to complex technical challenges.

What You’ll Do

  • Build integrations without traditional APIs: Develop systems that interact with external websites, platforms, and services when official APIs are unavailable, incomplete, or too restrictive.

  • Develop data acquisition pipelines: Collect, extract, and transform data from diverse external sources, including HTML pages, dynamic web applications, documents, and unstructured content.

  • Reverse engineer external systems: Analyze network requests, browser behavior, page structures, and undocumented interfaces to understand how external systems operate.

  • Build scraping and automation tools: Use technologies such as browser automation, HTTP clients, headless browsers, and custom extraction logic to retrieve data reliably.

  • Clean and normalize messy data: Transform inconsistent, duplicated, incomplete, or poorly structured data into clean, standardized formats suitable for downstream applications and AI workflows.

  • Build resilient systems: Design integrations that can handle changing page layouts, evolving external systems, rate limits, authentication flows, and unexpected failures.

  • Leverage AI for data processing: Explore ways to use LLMs and other AI techniques to extract, classify, enrich, validate, and structure data from unstructured sources.

  • Improve reliability and scalability: Implement monitoring, retries, validation, error handling, and automated testing to ensure integrations remain dependable over time.

  • Collaborate across engineering and product: Work with other engineers to turn ambiguous requirements and unfamiliar external systems into practical, maintainable solutions.

What We’re Looking For

  • Professional software engineering experience building production-quality applications, integrations, or data pipelines.

  • Experience with at least one of the following:

    • Web scraping or large-scale data extraction.

    • Reverse engineering or working with undocumented interfaces.

    • Building integrations with third-party platforms that lack robust APIs.

    • Extracting, transforming, and cleaning data from inconsistent external sources.

  • Strong proficiency in a language such as Python, TypeScript, or JavaScript.

  • Experience working with HTTP, REST concepts, HTML, DOM structures, JSON, .Net C# and network requests.

  • An understanding of authentication, cookies, sessions, pagination, rate limiting, and other challenges associated with external integrations.

  • Experience designing maintainable software that can adapt when external systems change.

  • Strong debugging and analytical skills, with the ability to investigate unfamiliar systems and work through ambiguous technical problems.

  • A pragmatic, resourceful mindset and a willingness to experiment, prototype, and find creative solutions.

What Success Looks Like

  • You can take an unfamiliar external platform and figure out how to retrieve the information we need, even when there isn't a straightforward API.

  • You can turn inconsistent, dirty, or unstructured external data into clean, usable, structured datasets.

  • You build integrations that remain reliable even as external systems evolve.

  • You can move from investigation and proof of concept to production-ready software without sacrificing maintainability.

  • You consistently find practical solutions to problems that don't have an obvious playbook.

The Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is a software engineer who enjoys the investigative side of engineering. They might have built scrapers, reverse-engineered web applications, developed browser automation, or created integrations with platforms that weren't designed to expose their data.

They don't necessarily need experience in every area listed above. We're more interested in someone who has demonstrated the ability to figure out how external systems work, access and interpret data, and build reliable software around systems they don't control.

This is not simply a traditional API integration role. It's an opportunity for an engineer who enjoys working at the intersection of external systems, data acquisition, data quality, and AI

Leadership, compliance and budget

  • Build, lead and mentor a team of scientists; set objectives, manage performance and foster a culture of scientific rigor and data integrity.
  • Ensure externally conducted regulated bioanalysis complies with GLP, GCP, ICH M10 and Bausch + Lomb quality, data governance and EHS policies, and that internal non-GLP work operates to documented data-quality standards with non-GLP data clearly identified wherever reported.

title: Training Specialist
description:

About the role and about You:

Great support starts with great training. When our members hit a snag, our Community Support team gets them back into Watopia and helps them make the most of their Zwift experience. To help support our frontline agents, we’re hiring a hands-on Training Specialist to build and maintain the training they rely on.

Our training program already has a strong foundation: a structured new hire curriculum, an established design framework, and experienced subject matter expert trainers who facilitate instructor-led training. In this role, you’ll keep that program accurate and effective as Zwift evolves. When products, processes, or policies change, you’ll revise new hire training and build and deploy update training to match. When the team identifies a need for refresh training, you’ll build it. When something new and complex launches, you’ll be a crucial part of supporting it.

You’ll be a part of our Content & Learning team, who own training, user-facing self-service content, and the internal knowledge enabling Zwift’s support team. In this role, you’ll also be the subject-matter expert in Seismic, our learning management system, ensuring we’re maximizing the benefits of the tool, keeping groups and enrollments clean, tracking completion and assessment results, and partnering with our BPO partners to close gaps.

You’re organized, dependable, and easy to work with. You take direction well, own your work from start to finish, and partner effectively with your teammates. You know when to hold firm on accuracy and when to flex on format or timing. You’re comfortable working outside a defined box: you pick up new tools, figure things out on your own, take on new work as the team’s needs change, and handle shifting priorities with ease. You use AI thoughtfully, knowing where it speeds up work and where human validation is essential.

What you’ll do:

  • Develop new eLearning and instructor-led training (including exams and certifications) to support product launches and updated policies and procedures, while keeping existing training current.
  • Build and deploy refresh training when the team identifies a need, indicated by QA results, Customer Effort Scores, or related performance data.
  • Host train-the-trainer sessions to prepare subject matter expert (SME) trainers for seasonal new hire classes and update training rollouts.
  • Run regular audits of training materials with SMEs to catch inaccurate, outdated, or missing information.
  • Build and sustain strong working relationships with SME trainers, partner teams, and BPO leaders, rooting feedback in curiosity and respect while openly receiving it in return.
  • Own Seismic (our LMS): managing distribution groups, reporting on completion and assessment results, and working with BPO leaders to close gaps. Explore unused and emerging features, while recommending ones worth adopting.

What we’re looking for:

  • 2+ years of instructional design, training, or learning and development experience.
  • Experience building eLearning, instructor-led training, and assessments using ADDIE or a similar model, with tools such as Articulate or Camtasia.
  • Familiar with Kirkpatrick or a similar model for measuring training effectiveness.
  • Experience as an LMS administrator using tools like Seismic (formerly Lessonly), Docebo, or equivalent, including user groups, enrollments, and reporting.
  • Experience facilitating virtual training, including train-the-trainer sessions, ideally with globally distributed or BPO teams.
  • Flexibility with an eagerness to support your team beyond training when priorities shift, whether for a short-term need or a longer-term change in focus.

Bonus points:

  • A passion for cycling, running, or fitness.
  • Experience supporting both internal and BPO (outsourced) contact center teams.
  • Familiarity with Zwift, gaming, the software industry, or fitness technology.
