description:
About the Role

Abnormal was built to spot what everyone else misses. The same instinct should power how we run our business.

As Director, Revenue Systems & Analytics, you'll own the technology and the truth behind Abnormal's go-to-market engine. Reporting to Ted Noble, VP of GTM Operations, you'll lead the strategy, roadmap, and team behind our marketing, sales, and customer success tech stacks, and you'll build the executive-level analytics that show how the whole revenue machine actually performs, from first touch to renewal and expansion. This is a role for a restless builder: someone who sees a disconnected stack or a siloed dashboard as an invitation to redesign it, and who wants to help make Abnormal the #1 AI-native company, starting with how we go to market.

The scale is real and growing fast. Abnormal closed FY26 at roughly $380M in ARR, growing about 50% year over year, with more than 5,000 customers and over 30% of the Fortune 500 trusting us to protect their people. As we expand from email security into a broader behavioral AI platform, the motions get more complex: more products, more buying journeys, more handoffs between Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success. Your systems and your numbers will be what keeps all of it connected, and what lets leadership see clearly where growth is coming from next.

What You Will Do

  • Own the GTM tech stack end to end. Lead strategy, architecture, and roadmap across the marketing, sales, and customer success technology ecosystems, treating them as one connected revenue platform rather than three separate toolsets.
  • Build a roadmap that drives growth. Align every system investment to company strategy and revenue goals, prioritizing ruthlessly based on impact to pipeline, conversion, retention, and expansion.
  • Lead with an AI-first approach. Define how AI and agentic workflows show up across the GTM stack, from automating manual work to surfacing insights reps and leaders can act on. Set the standard that AI accelerates decisions without sacrificing accuracy, auditability, or trust in the data.
  • Make revenue analytics the single source of truth. Lead the Revenue Analytics function and build and maintain executive-level dashboards that show true end-to-end performance across the full customer lifecycle, so leaders from the CEO down are working from the same numbers.
  • Break down silos. Design metrics, definitions, and reporting that cut across Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success, uniting every team around the shared goal of growth instead of functional scorecards.
  • Govern data like it matters. Partner closely with Data and Finance on data quality, governance, and metric definitions so GTM reporting reconciles cleanly and holds up in board and executive settings.
  • Manage the stack as a business. Own GTM software strategy, vendor relationships, budget, and renewals, consolidating where it makes sense and investing where it moves the needle.
  • Build and lead the team. Hire, develop, and lead a high-performing team of systems, data, and analytics professionals, including people leaders, and grow the next generation of leaders within GTM Operations.
  • Be a strategic partner to GTM leadership. Work hand in hand with Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, Finance, IT, and Security leaders to translate business priorities into systems and insights, and bring a clear point of view on what the data says about where to go next.

Must Haves

  • 10+ years of experience in GTM systems, revenue operations, or revenue analytics at a high-growth B2B SaaS company, with at least 5 years leading teams.
  • Proven track record owning a multi-function GTM tech stack (marketing, sales, and customer success) and delivering a strategic roadmap tied to revenue outcomes.
  • Deep expertise in Salesforce as the core system of record, plus hands-on experience with a cloud data warehouse and BI platform for executive reporting.
  • Experience building executive and board-level dashboards that connect the full funnel, from pipeline generation through bookings, retention, and expansion.
  • Strong command of GTM metrics and definitions (pipeline, conversion, ARR, net and gross retention, forecast) and the credibility to defend them in front of senior leaders.
  • Demonstrated experience bringing AI and automation into GTM systems and workflows, with sound judgment about where it helps and where it adds risk.
  • Experience managing software budgets, vendor negotiations, and stack rationalization.
  • Exceptional cross-functional leadership: the ability to align Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, Finance, and IT around shared priorities and shared numbers.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience with tools in our ecosystem, such as Marketo, Gainsight, Gong, Snowflake, Sigma, Workato, and Highspot.
  • Background in cybersecurity or another technical, enterprise-focused category.
  • Experience scaling GTM systems and analytics through a multi-product or platform expansion.

Actual compensation will be determined based on several non-discriminatory factors including skills, experience, qualifications, and geographic location.
In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for bonus or incentive compensation, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package.

title: Project Manager, Business Transformation
description:

The Algolia platform turns a company's products, content, and business rules into data that humans, applications and AI agents can act upon. The result is trusted customer experiences with stronger conversions for measurable business impact.

We're looking for a Project Manager to lead individual workstreams within our broader business transformation program. You will help support the implementation, development and iteration of workstreams within a program within the overall business transformation strategy. You'll be responsible for planning, executing, and delivering projects that improve how the business operates - spanning process redesign, systems implementation, and organizational change; while working closely with the Transformation Lead and business stakeholders to ensure outcomes stick.

  • Own the end-to-end delivery of assigned projects: scope, schedule, budget, risk, and quality

  • Liaise with stakeholders to define the scope, timeline, resources required and define any risk management plans
  • Define clear roles and responsibilities of the participating team members within each initiative
  • Lead multiple project streams with successful turnarounds to achieve timelines
  • Identify risks, prepare contingency and recovery plans in the event of project delays
  • Develop strategies to ensure efficient resource planning and allocation in alignment with the team's strategy
  • Apply change management processes to manage stakeholders’ expectations throughout the life cycle of a project, specifically managing changes to a project (added feature/requirements, extended deadline, added budget)

YOU MIGHT BE A FIT IF YOU HAVE:

  • 6+ years of project management experience, ideally including business transformation, process improvement, or systems implementation projects
  • 6+ years of experience in managing multiple end-to-end project life cycles
  • Preferred experience in Business Transformation projects and implementation experience working with multiple teams to focus on driving financial and operational results including behavioral changes such as design change strategy, assessing stakeholder impact, and organizational readiness
  • Identify project risks, prepare contingency and project recovery plans

  • Strong leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills
  • Based in US Eastern Time

What Success Looks Like in the First 6 Months

  • Fully onboarded onto a few active transformation workstreams

$129,500—$160,000 USD

Algolia’s flexible workplace model is designed to empower all Algolians to fulfill our mission to power search and discovery with ease. title: Senior EPMS Design Engineer
description:
Serverfarm is a leading developer and operator of data centers with over 750+ locations and key customer relationships in 45 countries. We're revolutionizing how data centers operate across North America, Western Europe, and Israel, serving the world's leading technology and hyperscale companies. With Manulife Investment Management's acquisition in 2023 and our award-winning InCommand platform we're positioned for explosive growth as AI adoption and cloud migration drive unprecedented demand for data center capacity.
A career at Serverfarm means being at the forefront of digital infrastructure innovation, where your work directly impacts how the world's data is managed and secured. As we target 4x growth over the next four years, you'll have unprecedented opportunities to take on new challenges, develop cutting-edge skills, and grow your career across our expanding global operations.
Join our team of innovators and help shape the future of sustainable data centers while building a career without boundaries.

We are seeking a Senior EPMS Design Engineer who thinks in terms of scalable, mission-critical systems and high-reliability operational architectures. As a senior member of the Controls Design Engineering (CDE) team, you will own the technical development, design standardization, and system integration of Electrical Power Monitoring Systems (EPMS) across our global fleet.

In this role, you will bridge the gap between electrical design concepts, controls engineering, and operational reality. You will serve as the primary owner for global EPMS specifications, network architectures, and control logic—ensuring that our critical power infrastructure (including switchgear, generators, UPS lineups, and distribution units) delivers robust telemetry, fault visibility, and automated power monitoring for hyperscale environments.

Key Accountabilities

    • Design & Architecture Governance: Author and maintain detailed EPMS design deliverables, including network architecture diagrams, Sequences of Operation (SOO), Basis of Design (BOD) documents, input/output (I/O) points lists, and project scopes of work (SOW).

    • Standards & Specifications: Own and maintain company-wide Division 25 (Integrated Automation) and Division 26 (Electrical) EPMS specifications, standardized drawing templates, and telemetry schemas.

    • Engineering Document & Drawing Reviews: Review detailed MEP design drawing packages—with a deep focus on electrical single-line diagrams, three-line diagrams, and control schematics—to ensure complete EPMS coverage, redundancy, and metering alignment.

    • Submittal & Long Lead Equipment (LLE) Audits: Review electrical equipment manufacturer submittals (switchgear, UPS systems, PDU/RPP units, generators, ATS) to ensure factory-installed meters, protection relays, and gateways comply with communication and telemetry standards.

    • Vendor & Bid Coordination: Create detailed EPMS vendor scopes of work, review technical proposals during contractor bidding, evaluate control system integrators, and manage technical Requests for Information (RFIs) to drive down scope gaps and change orders.

    • Hardware & Communications Architecture: Specify control panel requirements, PLC hardware lineups, and communication protocols (Modbus RTU/TCP, BACnet/IP, and TCP/IP), ensuring optimal bus capacity and network segmentation.

    • Cross-Functional Integration: Define integration strategies linking EPMS to industrial PLCs, Building Management Systems (BMS), Branch Circuit Monitoring Systems (BCMS), and cloud telemetry brokers (e.g., MQTT / Sparkplug B architectures).

    • Testing & Quality Assurance: Participate in Factory Witness Tests (FWTs) and Equipment Qualification Tests (EQTs) to validate point mapping and EPMS device functionality on first-of-kind electrical assemblies.

    • Commissioning & Construction Support: Conduct QA/QC audits on active builds, supporting commissioning agents through L1–L5 testing phases, point-to-point checkout validation, and final "As-Built" package reviews prior to Ready For Service (RFS) handoff.

    • Operational Root-Cause Support: Serve as a subject matter expert (SME) to diagnose complex system anomalies, including Loss of Visibility (LOV), Loss of Resilience (LOR), or power metering discrepancies.

Required Skills

    • Experience: 5+ years of direct experience in Electrical Power Monitoring Systems (EPMS) design, engineering, or systems integration within data centers or mission-critical facilities.

    • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electrical Engineering Technology, Mechatronics, or commensurate industry/military experience in lieu of degree.

    • Engineering Documentation: Demonstrated expertise in generating and interpreting electrical single-line diagrams, control network schematics, sequences of operation, control panel layouts, and Bills of Materials (BOM).

    • Protocols & Industrial Networks: Strong working knowledge of industrial communication protocols including Modbus (RTU and TCP), BACnet (MS/TP and IP), and Ethernet TCP/IP networking.

    • System Knowledge: Hands-on design fluency with PLC-based EPMS architectures, Branch Circuit Monitoring Systems (BCMS), and power metering hardware.

    • Specifications: Demonstrable experience authoring or interpreting CSI Division 25 and Division 26 specifications.

Preferred Skills

    • 7+ years of progressive engineering experience within hyperscale or colocation data center infrastructure.

    • Deep understanding of critical data center electrical infrastructure, including medium/low voltage switchgear lineups, static transfer switches (STS), UPS lineups, transformers, power distribution units (PDUs), and utility/generator paralleling logic.

    • Familiarity with cloud data aggregation models and modern telemetry brokers (e.g., MQTT, Sparkplug B, Inductive Automation Ignition).

    • Experience participating in L1–L5 commissioning cycles, Integrated System Testing (IST), and Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT).

Work Location & Travel Expectations

    • Location: Flexible; preferences include primary operational hubs (Georgia, Texas, or Arkansas).

    • Travel: Up to 25% travel to global data center construction sites, equipment manufacturing facilities for Factory Witness Testing (FWT), and corporate functions.

Why Talkspace?

Talkspace is the world’s leading online therapy company, serving over 2 million users looking to begin their wellness journey through tele-health. According to the World Health Organization, close to 1 billion people worldwide live with a mental disorder, and on average more than 75% with mental, neurological, and substance use disorders receive no treatment for their condition at all. Additionally, one-third of the world’s population – 2 billion people – live in countries that spend less than 1% of their health budgets on mental health. Therapy is an universal need and it's our mission here to change the world by cultivating an intentional space for people to feel supported through quality care that is simple and accessible.

Combining our passion for innovation along with our desire to help others overcome the stigma behind “getting help,” we are transforming the way patients find the right care provider, making an otherwise impossible feat easily conquerable. Our network of licensed, accredited, and board-certified clinicians are increasing access to mental health for our members through a myriad of high quality therapy services: anytime and for a fraction of the price. Dedicated to our mission, we are looking for candidates that want to bring their talents into a diverse “for purpose” space. If you’re equally as passionate about making quality mental healthcare accessible to all then Talkspace is the right place for you!

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

Talkspace welcomes and celebrates talent from all backgrounds, perspectives, and walks of life to foster an innovative and diverse workforce. We encourage you to apply, even if you don’t meet every qualification or if your path has been nontraditional — such as not completing a formal degree program, taking a career break, or having a prior criminal record — if you believe you could make a great addition to this team. Come as you are and learn about the exciting opportunities on our team.

Individuals seeking employment at Talkspace are considered without regard to race, color, religious creed, sex, national origin, citizenship status, age, physical or mental disability, sexual orientation, marital, parental, veteran or military status, unfavorable military discharge, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state or local law.

How do we define Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging at Talkspace?

Diversity

Diversity encompasses the unique attributes of our employees as individuals. We value and embrace the richness arising from their varied backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences, which include, but are not limited to, age, ability, ethnicity, gender, race, and cultural background.

Equity

Equity refers to a fair and impartial workplace, aiming to ensure equal growth and advancement opportunities for all employees. This involves amplifying underrepresented voices, addressing unconscious biases, and providing inclusive, culturally competent mental health care.

Inclusion

Inclusion signifies the practice of granting equal access to opportunities and resources for all employees, particularly those who might otherwise be excluded or marginalized. It ensures that everyone feels a sense of belonging, value, support, and respect as an individual.

Belonging

Belonging reflects the affinity and positive relationships that develop among employees from diverse backgrounds when businesses actively promote diversity, equity, and inclusion in the workplace.

title: Business Intelligence Analyst / Data Engineer
description:
Why Join GEICO?

At GEICO, we offer a rewarding career where your ambitions are met with endless possibilities.

Every day we honor our iconic brand by offering quality coverage to millions of customers and being there when they need us most. We thrive on relentless innovation to exceed our customers' expectations while making a real impact on local communities nationwide.

Founded in 1936, GEICO is a member of the Berkshire Hathaway family of companies and one of the largest auto insurers in the United States. When you join our company, we want you to feel valued, supported, and proud to work here. That's why we offer the GEICO Pledge: Great Company, Great Culture, Great Rewards, and Great Careers.

Overview:

The Business Intelligence Analyst III / IV is responsible for designing, developing, and supporting enterprise business intelligence and visual analytics solutions that enable data-driven decision-making. This role transforms complex data into meaningful reports, dashboards, semantic models, and analytical solutions that support operational and strategic business outcomes.

The associate partners with business stakeholders, technology teams, and data engineering partners to deliver scalable visual reporting solutions, establish semantic modeling standards, and translate advanced analyses into clear recommendations. Microsoft Power BI is the primary business intelligence platform for this role; however, the associate is expected to remain agile and use Apache Superset or other visualization tools when they are better suited to the business need.

As a member of an agile team, the incumbent contributes to solution design, development, testing, deployment, optimization, production support, report certification, and modernization of enterprise reporting assets. The role focuses on business intelligence and visual analytics rather than primary ownership of source-data engineering or Power BI tenant administration.


Level Expectations :


Business Intelligence Analyst III: Designs end-to-end BI solutions, including semantic and metric layers, data models, reports, and dashboards. Applies advanced analytical and statistical techniques to move reporting from descriptive insight toward diagnostic analysis of performance drivers and customer behavior, while introducing predictive approaches where appropriate. Works independently with minimal guidance, leads solution components, partners with stakeholders to frame analytical questions, and provides technical guidance to peers.

Business Intelligence Analyst IV: Leads the design of complex, reusable BI solutions and serves as a technical lead for reporting and analytics initiatives. Balances regular delivery responsibilities with leadership of cross-functional projects, establishes semantic modeling and reporting standards, reviews technical designs, influences BI architecture and tooling decisions, and mentors analysts and developers across levels.


Responsibilities:


  • Design end-to-end business intelligence solutions, including semantic and metric layers, dimensional data models, reports, dashboards, scorecards, and visual analytics products.
  • Develop, maintain, and optimize Power BI semantic models, reports, dashboards, and analytical solutions using DAX, Power Query, and enterprise reporting standards.
  • Apply advanced analytical and statistical techniques to identify trends, performance drivers, customer behaviors, and opportunities for operational improvement.
  • Translate descriptive reporting into diagnostic insight and introduce predictive approaches where appropriate to the business question and available data.
  • Partner with stakeholders to frame analytical questions, evaluate findings, and translate complex analyses into clear, compelling recommendations.
  • Establish, document, and promote semantic modeling standards, reusable design patterns, visualization standards, and reporting best practices.
  • Support report certification by validating solution quality, consistency, usability, maintainability, performance, documentation, and adherence to established standards.
  • Publish and support Power BI solutions through Power BI Service, including Workspaces, Apps, Deployment Pipelines, and semantic model refresh processes.
  • Optimize report and semantic model performance, refresh reliability, storage-mode selection, and overall user experience across BI platforms.
  • Assess the downstream impact of design choices involving Import, DirectQuery, composite models, Row-Level Security, refresh strategies, and available Power BI capacity.
  • Evaluate visualization technologies and select Power BI, Apache Superset, or other appropriate tools based on business need, scalability, maintainability, and user experience.
  • Use Snowflake and other approved enterprise data sources to deliver reliable, scalable reporting and analytics solutions.
  • Coordinate with data engineering and technology partners to ensure source data is available, reliable, understandable, and usable for reporting.
  • Document report definitions, calculations, assumptions, semantic models, technical designs, and support procedures.
  • Lead improvements to reporting processes, including automation of recurring outputs and reduction of manual effort.
  • Support report migration and modernization initiatives, including conversion of legacy reporting solutions to modern BI platforms and reusable semantic model architectures.
  • Perform testing, validation, deployment, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, performance tuning, and post-implementation support.
  • Participate in agile planning, backlog refinement, estimation, status reporting, and cross-functional delivery coordination.
  • Provide technical guidance to team members through design, DAX, query, and solution reviews.
  • Business Intelligence Analyst IV: Serve as technical lead for complex reporting and analytics initiatives, lead cross-team projects, review technical designs, and mentor analysts and developers across levels.

Qualifications:

  • Advanced experience designing, developing, deploying, and supporting business intelligence solutions using Microsoft Power BI or comparable enterprise visualization platforms.
  • Strong proficiency with DAX, semantic modeling, dimensional modeling, Power Query, data visualization, and enterprise BI architecture.
  • Experience publishing and supporting Power BI solutions through Workspaces, Apps, Deployment Pipelines, and semantic model refresh processes.
  • Advanced SQL knowledge, including the ability to write, troubleshoot, and optimize complex queries used in reporting and analytics solutions.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate complex technical and analytical concepts for technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Strong analytical, quantitative, problem-solving, organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively within an agile delivery environment.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver reliable solutions with minimal guidance.
  • Must have the following experience:
  • Business Intelligence Analyst III: 4-7 years of relevant business intelligence, analytics, reporting, semantic modeling, or data visualization experience.
  • Business Intelligence Analyst IV: 7-10 years of relevant business intelligence, analytics, reporting, semantic modeling, or data visualization experience.
  • Experience developing enterprise dashboards, reports, semantic models, and visual analytics solutions.
  • Experience partnering with stakeholders to define business questions, gather requirements, assess findings, and deliver actionable reporting solutions.
  • Experience working with enterprise data platforms and large-scale datasets.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Microsoft Certified: Power BI Data Analyst Associate (PL-300).
  • Microsoft Power BI administration certification or equivalent demonstrated knowledge of Power BI administration concepts.
  • Strongly preferred experience with Microsoft Fabric features such as Lakehouses, Warehouses, Dataflows Gen2, Data Pipelines, Notebooks, Real-Time Intelligence, and related capabilities.
  • Strongly preferred experience using Snowflake as a primary enterprise data source for reporting and analytics.
  • Experience with Apache Superset or other business intelligence and visualization platforms, with the ability to select the appropriate visual tool for the business use case.
  • Experience developing or supporting Apache Airflow workflows.
  • Experience with Power BI Project (PBIP) formats and collaborative development of Power BI assets.
  • Experience using Git-based version control, including branching, pull requests, code reviews, and collaborative development workflows.
  • Knowledge of Power BI administration and architecture concepts, including capacity management, storage modes, licensing, workspaces, tenant considerations, governance, and performance optimization.
  • Understanding of performance and capacity considerations involving DirectQuery, Import mode, composite models, incremental refresh, and Row-Level Security (RLS).
  • Experience using AI-assisted development tools such as Cursor, Claude, GitHub Copilot, or similar platforms to generate or refine scripts, troubleshoot solutions, create documentation, support testing, and accelerate analytics delivery.
  • Working knowledge of Python, scripting, or related programming concepts, with emphasis on effectively reviewing, validating, and applying AI-generated code.
  • Experience supporting report certification, semantic modeling standards, and reporting modernization initiatives.
  • Experience with Azure DevOps or a comparable agile work management and delivery platform.
  • Property and Casualty insurance, claims analytics, finance analytics, or enterprise reporting experience.

Annual Salary

$109,675.00 - $172,200.00

The above annual salary range is a general guideline. Multiple factors are taken into consideration to arrive at the final hourly rate/ annual salary to be offered to the selected candidate. Factors include, but are not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the role, the selected candidate’s work experience, education and training, the work location as well as market and business considerations.

GEICO will consider sponsoring a new qualified applicant for employment authorization for this position.

description:
ISTA Personnel Solutions is a dynamic and fast-growing BPO company. We are not a recruitment agency. We operate as a dedicated extension of our clients' teams, delivering high-quality service with precision, efficiency, and a personal touch.

We are looking for an After Hours Care Coordinator to join our client's After Hours Department, supporting a U.S.-based home care agency that provides in-home care for elderly and vulnerable clients. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment, stays calm and decisive under pressure, and is confident making sound judgement calls when there is no one else available to ask.

Working Hours:

Approx. 28 hours per week(subject to operational requirements and may change)

  • Sunday: 18:00 – 04:00 SAST Monday
  • Monday: 00:00 – 04:00 SAST Tuesday
  • Friday: 00:00 – 04:00 SAST Saturday
  • Saturday: 18:00 – 04:00 SAST Sunday

Please note: Training will be approximately one month, and training hours will differ from the regular working schedule. Full schedule flexibility is required, as you may be asked to provide additional coverage during busy periods or when colleagues are on leave.

PLEASE NOTE

  • Public Holidays: This role requires working on both South African and U.S. public holidays (compensation for SA public holidays in accordance with the BCEA).
  • Internet Requirements: A fixed fibre line with a minimum speed of 25 Mbps (upload & download) and wired Ethernet capability is mandatory. Applicants without a fixed fibre line cannot be considered.
  • Power Backup: Reliable backup is required to manage load shedding or outages. Applicants without a power backup cannot be considered.
  • Work Environment: Fully remote.
  • Working Style: This is a lean, largely solo role. You will often be the only person on shift, so you must be comfortable making independent decisions without real-time support.

Responsibilities

  • Monitor the phone line and the company's chat/texting platform for caregiver call-outs, emergencies, and no-shows.
  • Source replacement caregivers when a shift cannot be covered, starting with available caregivers closest to the client and arranging a longer-term replacement where required.
  • Ensure vulnerable clients are never left without coverage, including asking the current caregiver to stay on until a replacement is in place.
  • Follow up by phone on call-outs received by text, keeping the focus on getting the client covered rather than on policy technicalities.
  • Escalate promptly to a manager when a replacement cannot be found immediately, and act on any further instructions.
  • Notify clients of caregiver call-outs and confirm caregiver schedules 1–2 hours before the start of each shift.
  • Respond to caregiver and client queries within the scope of after-hours support, tailoring your response to the client's living situation (e.g. a care facility with on-site nursing staff versus a private home).
  • Use sound judgement on situations not covered in training, always putting client safety first, then policy, then business considerations.
  • Conduct initial intake calls for prospective clients interested in services.
  • Accurately document all interactions and update caregiver schedules within the system.
  • Prioritise urgent, time-critical tasks during busy periods, and use quieter periods for administrative catch-up, documentation, and system familiarisation.
  • Balance caregiver concerns with client and business needs, defaulting to client care when trade-offs are required.
  • Assist with administrative projects and other after-hours support tasks as needed.

Requirements

  • Fluent in English with clear, professional communication skills.
  • Proven experience in a client-facing support, service, or coordination role.
  • Strong independent judgement and critical thinking, with comfort handling ambiguity and situations not covered by training.
  • Calm, decisive communicator who can make a call and direct next steps to caregivers, supervisors, and clients.
  • Strong multitasking, prioritisation, and organisational skills.
  • Comfortable working independently with minimal supervision.
  • Resourceful and able to solve problems effectively under pressure.
  • Compassionate, dependable, and highly responsible, with the ability to balance empathy with a clear focus on client care.
  • Ambitious with a strong work ethic.
  • Full schedule flexibility, including weekends, and adaptability to changing schedules and operational requirements.
  • Excellent computer and telephone skills.

Advantageous

  • Previous staffing, scheduling, dispatch, or healthcare/home care industry experience.
  • Experience working in a largely solo or remote role.

If you are not contacted within 14 working days, please consider your application unsuccessful.

title: Director of Training (BCBA)
description:
Director of Training (BCBA)

Turn your expertise into organization-wide impact.

We’re seeking an experienced Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) to lead our company-wide training strategy and delivery, combining clinical expertise, instructional design, and leadership development to strengthen how our teams learn and grow.

In this hands-on leadership role, you’ll design and facilitate engaging training sessions, develop scalable learning programs, and partner with department leaders and subject matter experts to support clinical excellence, operational effectiveness, and employee development across the organization. From onboarding and clinical training to leadership development and compliance, you’ll help shape how our teams learn, grow, and succeed.

This is an opportunity for a BCBA passionate about developing people, leading trainings, and creating meaningful organizational impact beyond direct clinical service delivery.

This position is primarily remote, with a preference for candidates based in Plano, Texas. We’re also open to qualified applicants residing in California, Idaho, Nebraska, or Iowa. Candidates must be comfortable traveling onsite as needed to facilitate training and support teams across the organization.

What You’ll Do

Lead the Training Vision

  • Develop and execute a company-wide training strategy aligned with organizational goals, clinical excellence, and operational priorities.
  • Establish consistent training standards and learning experiences across departments, roles, and locations.
  • Identify opportunities to strengthen existing programs and build scalable solutions that support organizational growth.

Build Engaging, Effective Learning Experiences

  • Oversee the development of training content, curricula, resources, and learning pathways from onboarding through ongoing professional development.
  • Lead training initiatives across Clinical, Operations, and other business functions, ensuring content is practical, relevant, and role-specific.
  • Incorporate adult learning principles, instructional design best practices, and innovative learning tools to make training engaging and effective.
  • Leverage technology, digital learning platforms, and emerging AI-enabled workflows to improve accessibility, consistency, and efficiency.

Develop Leaders and Strengthen Teams

  • Create and oversee leadership and management development programs that equip employees to lead with confidence and accountability.
  • Partner with department leaders and subject matter experts to identify skill gaps and translate business needs into actionable training.
  • Support the development of training facilitators, trainers, and internal subject matter experts to strengthen knowledge-sharing across the organization.

Measure Impact and Drive Continuous Improvement

  • Establish clear metrics to evaluate training effectiveness, learner engagement, competency development, and business impact.
  • Use feedback, performance data, and operational insights to continuously improve training programs.
  • Ensure training documentation, compliance requirements, and learning standards are consistently maintained.
  • Build systems that support accountability, reinforce learning, and promote the practical application of new skills.

What You’ll Bring

  • A Master’s degree in Applied Behavior Analysis or a related field.
  • An active Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) certification.
  • At least 3 years of BCBA experience.
  • At least 3 years of progressive experience leading training, learning and development, or organizational development initiatives.
  • Experience designing and delivering training across multiple roles, departments, and/or locations.
  • Strong knowledge of adult learning principles, instructional design, competency-based training, and program evaluation.
  • Experience working with learning management systems, digital training platforms, and technology-enabled learning solutions.
  • The ability to translate complex information into clear, engaging, and actionable learning experiences.
  • Strong leadership, communication, collaboration, and project management skills.
  • A continuous-improvement mindset and an interest in leveraging AI and emerging technologies to enhance learning and development.
  • The ability and willingness to travel onsite as needed to deliver training and support teams.

What Success Looks Like

In this role, you’ll help create a more connected, consistent, and effective learning culture across Accel Therapies. Your work will strengthen onboarding, elevate leadership development, improve employee readiness, and equip teams with the knowledge and skills they need to deliver high-quality services.

You won’t simply maintain training programs — you’ll help define how learning happens across the organization.

Ready to Make an Impact?

If you’re a BCBA and learning leader who enjoys building systems, developing people, and turning big-picture strategy into meaningful action, we’d love to hear from you.

title: Senior Engineer- Agentic Development
description:
FICO (NYSE: FICO)is a leading global analytics software company, helping businesses in 100+ countries make better decisions. Join our world-class team today and fulfill your career potential!

The Opportunity


FICO builds the analytics and decisioning technology behind some of the highest-stakes decisions in the world economy including the FICO Score, the standard measure of consumer credit risk in the US, and FICO Platform, an API-first applied intelligence platform delivering real-time decisions across fraud detection, credit risk, regulatory compliance, marketing, and customer engagement. This is mission-critical, low-latency, heavily regulated software where auditability and controlled change are non-negotiable. This role sits at the point where that technology is being built and operated in an agentic-first way. As coding agents take on an increasing share of the software lifecycle, the engineer's role shifts from hand-writing code to directing, specifying, and verifying the output of a fleet of specialised agents, working through a structured harness of guides, feedback loops, guardrails, and shared context that transforms raw model capability into production grade engineering. The successful candidate will bring the engineering judgement that agents cannot replicate: the ability to define what good looks like, encode it with sufficient precision for agents to achieve it, and recognise when they have not, applying that judgement to architecture, correctness, trade-off analysis, and the design of the work itself.


What You’ll Contribute

  • Collaborate with Product teams to translate early stage ideation into structured Proof of Concepts, establishing clear technical feasibility and scope.
  • Produce detailed specifications and acceptance criteria that enable coding agents to generate correct, maintainable, and well-architected output, taking full ownership of the resulting code through to deployment.
  • Apply rigorous quality standards to all agent generated output, ensuring it meets the same level of scrutiny as hand written code within a regulated decisioning context.
  • Operate effectively within the agentic harness, utilising established guides, including AGENTS.md files, architectural rules, and reference documentation alongside automated sensors such as linters, fitness tests, verification loops, and LLM-as-judge reviewers.
  • Identify the root cause of recurring agent errors and work with the harness team to implement systemic controls, ensuring the same class of failure cannot recur across the codebase.
  • Maintain the accuracy and currency of repository documentation, specifications, and contextual knowledge, treating these as a shared system of record for both human engineers and agents.
  • Apply focused technical judgement to architecture decisions, edge case analysis, latency and integration risk, auditability requirements, and any determination that falls outside the appropriate scope of agent autonomy.

What We’re Seeking

  • Demonstrable experience in software engineering within large, complex codebases, with a strong foundation in software architecture, testing practices, and long-term maintainability.
  • Practical experience working with AI coding agents such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, or Cursor with a clear understanding of their capabilities, limitations, and appropriate use within a production engineering workflow.
  • The technical judgement to critically evaluate agent generated output, identify subtle errors or architectural weaknesses, and make informed decisions about when to intervene in the agent workflow.
  • The ability to communicate technical requirements with precision, producing specifications and definitions of done that are unambiguous, testable, and actionable by both agents and engineering colleagues.
  • A disciplined approach to verification, instinctively questioning correctness, building appropriate checks and test coverage, and applying particular rigour in regulated and mission-critical delivery contexts.
  • A results-oriented approach to delivery, with accountability for the quality and correctness of shipped work rather than volume of code produced.
  • Familiarity with relevant technologies including Python, SQL, JavaScript/TypeScript, AWS or Azure, Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, ML model deployment, or real-time decisioning systems.
  • Experience with spec-driven development, context engineering, or agent orchestration in a team environment is a significant advantage, as is knowledge of regulated or audited software delivery processes and controlled change management.
  • A background in decisioning, credit risk, fraud detection, analytics, optimisation, or data engineering would be advantageous; candidates who can also articulate a considered approach to human-AI collaboration including delegation boundaries, human oversight, and earning autonomy through demonstrated quality will be of particular interest.

Our Offer to You

  • An inclusive culture strongly reflecting our core values: Act Like an Owner, Delight Our Customers and Earn the Respect of Others.
  • The opportunity to make an impact and develop professionally by leveraging your unique strengths and participating in valuable learning experiences.
  • Highly competitive compensation, benefits and rewards programs that encourage you to bring your best every day and be recognized for doing so.
  • An engaging, people-first work environment offering work/life balance, employee resource groups, and social events to promote interaction and camaraderie.


Why Make a Move to FICO?

At FICO, you can develop your career with a leading organization in one of the fastest-growing fields in technology today – Big Data analytics. You’ll play a part in our commitment to help businesses use data to improve every choice they make, using advances in artificial intelligence, machine learning, optimization, and much more.

FICO makes a real difference in the way businesses operate worldwide:

• Credit Scoring — FICO® Scores are used by 90 of the top 100 US lenders.

• Fraud Detection and Security — 4 billion payment cards globally are protected by FICO fraud systems.

• Lending — 3/4 of US mortgages are approved using the FICO Score.

Global trends toward digital transformation have created tremendous demand for FICO’s solutions, placing us among the world’s top 100 software companies by revenue. We help many of the world’s largest banks, insurers, retailers, telecommunications providers and other firms reach a new level of success. Our success is dependent on really talented people – just like you – who thrive on the collaboration and innovation that’s nurtured by a diverse and inclusive environment. We’ll provide the support you need, while ensuring you have the freedom to develop your skills and grow your career. Join FICO and help change the way business thinks!

Business Unit

Actimize Professional Services

Reports to

Strategic Services Sales Leader

Location

London, United Kingdom

Scope

EMEA; senior individual contributor focused exclusively on unattached, post-license strategic services sales into existing customers

Domain

Financial Crime and Compliance, including AML and Fraud

The Services Portfolio

This role exclusively covers unattached services sold to Actimize customers following the software license sale. It does not include implementation or other services sold as part of, or attached to, a new license transaction.

The focus is on identifying whitespace, expanding existing engagements and creating new strategic services opportunities across:

  • Large-scale, multi-year transformational programmes in Financial Crime and Compliance
  • Transformational consulting and advisory
  • Business and technical managed services, including business-as-usual (BAU) engagements

How will you make an impact?

Own account and territory growth planning.

Develop actionable services growth plans for priority EMEA accounts by analysing the installed base, identifying whitespace, mapping executive stakeholders and translating client priorities into focused opportunity plans.

Generate and shape demand.

Lead client workshops, executive briefings and value-discovery sessions that surface unmet needs, create urgency and shape new consulting, transformation and managed services opportunities independent of new license transactions.

Understand the client agenda.

Engage credibly with senior business, technology, operations and compliance stakeholders, speaking the language of financial institutions and translating their Financial Crime and Compliance challenges into clear service outcomes.

Architect complex, high-quality deals.

Construct large, strategic and often multi-year services propositions, defining the value case, scope, delivery model, commercial structure, pricing and roadmap while maintaining accountability for margin, delivery risk and overall deal quality.

Lead pursuits to closure.

Own the end-to-end sales cycle for complex services deals, from early discovery and qualification through proposal, negotiation and signature, maintaining momentum and executive alignment throughout.

Partner with the regional sales organisation.

Work alongside account executives and regional sales leaders on aligned account strategies: account teams retain ownership of the overall client relationship and software agenda, while this role leads the origination, shaping and closure of unattached post-license services opportunities, with shared executive engagement and coordinated account governance.

Expand existing relationships and engagements.

Develop durable relationships with client executives, uncover adjacent needs and extend the value and scope of current engagements by positioning Actimize as a trusted strategic services partner.

Develop thought leadership and repeatable propositions.

Bring relevant market, regulatory and operating-model insights to clients and work with consulting, product and delivery teams to create differentiated, repeatable services propositions that respond to common client needs.

Mobilise Actimize.

Build trust with internal leaders across Professional Services, software sales, product, pre-sales, delivery, legal, finance and partners to secure the expertise and sponsorship required to shape and position winning deals.

Maintain post-sale continuity.

Remain engaged through mobilisation and key executive checkpoints to ensure the value proposition sold is translated into measurable client outcomes, delivery risks are surfaced early and future expansion opportunities are identified.

Drive commercial discipline.

Maintain a high-quality pipeline and accurate forecast, apply rigorous qualification and opportunity governance, and make sound decisions on competitive strategy, commercials, margin, contractual position and delivery risk.

Create market impact.

Establish a visible presence quickly, independently build a point of view on priority accounts, and translate strategic insight into practical opportunity plans that strengthen Actimize’s position as a Financial Crime and Compliance services partner.

Experience and Capabilities

  • Typically 8–15 years of relevant experience, including proven success independently originating and selling complex, high-value consulting-led, transformation or managed services engagements into existing large financial-institution customers outside a new software license sale. Equivalent depth of experience and demonstrated capability will also be considered.

  • Strong knowledge of Financial Crime and Compliance, including the priorities and pain points facing financial institutions across areas such as AML, fraud, sanctions, KYC and financial crime operations.

  • A background in Financial Crime and Compliance consulting is highly desirable, combined with demonstrable commercial success and a strong sales mindset.

  • Demonstrated ability to construct and close large, strategic, multi-stakeholder services deals, including value proposition, commercial modelling, negotiation and contracting.

  • Practical familiarity with fixed-price, time-and-materials, managed services and outcome-based commercial models, including the ability to assess pricing, margin, risk allocation and delivery implications.

  • Proven experience building account-level services growth plans, identifying whitespace, mapping stakeholders and independently converting insight into qualified opportunities and sustainable pipeline.

  • Excellent communication and executive presentation skills, with the ability to simplify complex issues, influence decisions and create urgency with senior client and internal stakeholders.

  • Outstanding relationship management skills and a track record of building trust across client organisations and internal cross-functional teams.

  • Strong commercial acumen, disciplined opportunity management and a consistent record of progressing and closing complex deals while protecting margin, delivery feasibility and deal quality.

  • Experience working across EMEA markets and navigating culturally diverse, matrixed organisations.

Measures of Success

  • Achievement of annual services bookings, revenue and margin targets.

  • Building and maintaining the required level, quality and mix of qualified pipeline coverage against target.

  • Creation of new, independently originated services opportunities from identified account whitespace.

  • Conversion of priority opportunities into large, strategic or multi-year engagements with strong commercial and delivery fundamentals.

  • Development and active progression of actionable services growth plans for priority EMEA accounts.

  • Forecast accuracy, disciplined opportunity progression and timely escalation of commercial or delivery risks.

  • Effective collaboration with regional account teams and successful post-sale handover and continuity through mobilisation and executive checkpoints.

You will have an advantage if you also have:

Personal Profile

  • A confident, credible and highly visible communicator who can make an impact quickly.

  • Client-centric and naturally consultative, with the curiosity to uncover the real business problem and the judgement to shape a compelling response.

  • Commercially sharp, resilient and accountable, with a strong closing orientation and the confidence to lead complex negotiations.

  • Collaborative and low-ego, able to build internal followership and bring diverse specialists together around a winning deal strategy.

  • A self-starting hunter with the strategic discipline to create structure in ambiguity, proactively open doors and independently generate cross-sell and upsell opportunities, taking ownership from whitespace identification to signed engagement.

What’s in it for you?

Learn more about the Benefits at NICE.

Join an ever-growing, market-disrupting, global company where the teams – comprised of the best of the best – work in a fast-paced, collaborative, and creative environment! As the market leader, every day at NICE is a chance to learn and grow, and there are endless internal career opportunities across multiple roles, disciplines, domains, and locations. title: Head of AI Enablement & Transformation

Head of AI Enablement & Transformation

Voice Systems Engineering (VSE) is a dynamic organization driven by innovation and a shared passion for positively impacting people's lives. We operate multiple brands and businesses, including Psychic Source, Plasma Futures and Soundbed, all focused on mind and body wellbeing, with our flagship brand, Psychic Source, leading the way.

Our vision at VSE centers on the belief that when talented individuals unite, possibilities become limitless. Rooted in a remote-first environment, we've cultivated a culture that embraces diversity, equity, work-life balance, and a true sense of belonging.

For over three decades, VSE has used technology to connect people with expert, caring guidance. We are an established, profitable company, and this year we made a deliberate decision to rebuild the way we work around AI rather than simply adding it to what we already do. Many AI projects are already underway across the business, and the whole company comes together every week to focus on AI adoption. We are now looking for the person to bring that work together and lead it.

We are seeking a passionate, hands-on and experienced Head of AI Enablement & Transformation to turn that commitment into everyday practice across the company. This is a builder's role rather than an advisory one. You should be comfortable prototyping and shipping generative AI agents, automations and the tooling that lets non-engineers use them safely, and equally comfortable teaching a team of roughly forty-five people, most of them non-technical, to apply these tools in their own jobs. You will own the stack, the guardrails and the numbers. You will not have a team reporting to you; the impact of this role comes from forty-five people who can do things they could not do before, working through AI champions across the business, the tools you build and the sessions you run. VSE runs on Holacracy, and this role sits in our General Company Circle, our most senior leadership team, with clearly defined domains that are yours to decide: the tooling stack and its vendors, the skills library and agent registry, and the scorecard and its targets.

Your first priority will be consolidation rather than expansion: bringing the work already underway into one coherent, well-governed program, deciding what to standardize on and what to retire, and putting the right guardrails in place before adding anything new. For the right person, this is the part that determines whether everything that follows succeeds, and the path from this role to real company-wide impact is unusually short.

If you're our new Head of AI Enablement & Transformation, you will look forward to engaging in activities such as:

  • Building and shipping AI capabilities: prototypes, agents, evaluation frameworks, and the pipeline that allows a non-engineer to deploy something safely. You will write code most weeks.

  • Leading hands-on enablement across the company: a weekly working session you run, role-specific playbooks, office hours, and a network of AI champions in every function, with adoption measured in actual use rather than attendance.

  • Redesigning core workflows around what AI makes possible, in partnership with the teams that do the work, rather than automating the steps that already exist.

  • Owning the AI scorecard: publishing weekly results including the metrics that missed, setting targets, and being transparent when a target changes and why.

  • Deciding the tooling stack: evaluating models, platforms, agent frameworks and vendors; running proofs of concept; making build-versus-buy calls; and avoiding tool sprawl.

  • Building the guardrails first: a graduated autonomy model that agents earn on evidence, traceability from every output back to its prompt and approver, a permissions and data-classification model that holds, and acceptable-use policy developed with Legal, HR and IT as partners from week one.

  • Managing the use-case pipeline from intake through prioritization, pilot, rollout and maintenance, and retiring at least one initiative each quarter, openly and with the reasoning, including your own.

  • Protecting the quality of what we ship: validating outputs against sources, retesting after model and tool updates, and defining where human oversight is required.

  • Looking after the team: one scorecard metric asks the team whether AI is making them more capable or just more pressured. Two consecutive weeks of decline pauses the rollout of new AI initiatives, and you are the one expected to call it.

Required Skills & Experience – You Should Have:

  • A track record of personally building and shipping agentic AI systems, automations or LLM-powered tools that people actually use, within the last twelve months.

  • At least 7 years in technology, operations, product, consulting or transformation roles, including at least 2 years of applied generative AI work.

  • Fluency with the current LLM ecosystem: prompting, agents, tool use, evaluation, retrieval, workflow orchestration and the major model providers, along with the judgment to tell a stakeholder when an idea will not work.

  • Scripting or coding ability sufficient to prototype, integrate via APIs, and troubleshoot without waiting on an engineering team.

  • Demonstrated success rolling out AI or automation across a non-technical workforce, with measurable gains in adoption, quality or efficiency.

  • Experience establishing governance, responsible-AI or data-handling policies in a live operating environment.

  • Excellent facilitation, coaching and communication skills: equally credible with engineers and with a customer care representative whose week you are trying to make easier.

  • Comfort owning a capability end to end, with direct accountability for results and without a team reporting to you.

Desired Skills:

  • Experience in a platform technology business, a two-sided marketplace, or an online B2C company. Industry background is not a requirement.

  • Experience consolidating scattered AI pilots or tools into one coherent, governed platform.

  • Familiarity with low-code automation platforms, data pipelines, and BI tooling.

  • Experience working in Holacracy or another self-management framework.

You don't need a background in our industry, but you do need to care about what we do. Our customers are real people reaching out at real moments in their lives, and the trust we have built with them over more than thirty years is the asset you will be working with.

At VSE the well-being of our people comes first, and we have nurtured a culture that focuses on health and wellness, personal growth, and social responsibility. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment of belonging for all employees and applicants. We are an equal opportunity employer.

We offer an unlimited vacation policy and flexible work schedule, so you can prioritize your needs for whatever season of life you are in. Our comprehensive insurance programs include medical, dental, vision, and life. VSE employees also have access to a "wellness wallet" that will reimburse them for gym memberships, workout equipment, mindfulness apps, healthy food boxes, ergonomic workspace tools, and more.

We prioritize investment in our people by offering a tuition reimbursement program and plenty of opportunities to continue learning. We also help you plan for your future and beyond by offering a 401k match and access to expert financial advice.

Please know that showing us things you have built or led yourself will be part of our hiring process. We don't just want to hear about your work; we want to see it. That might be a tool, an agent, a workflow or a short walkthrough of a project, along with what it does and what you learned along the way. If some of your work can't be shared because it belongs to a previous employer, that's understood, and we'll ask you to walk us through what you can.

This is a remote based position. You can learn more about life and work at VSE by visiting us here.

title: Senior Factoring Underwriter & Credit Specialist
description:
About the Role: We are seeking an experienced Senior Factoring Underwriter & Credit Specialist with direct, hands-on expertise in accounts receivable (A/R) factoring. In this role, you will lead the credit evaluation, risk structuring, and day-to-day portfolio oversight of invoice factoring facilities for high-growth e-commerce, CPG, and B2B wholesale businesses.

This role is specifically tailored for an expert who understands the operational, legal, and credit nuances of invoice factoring. Beyond analyzing classic financial statements, you will evaluate debtor creditworthiness, verify invoice authenticity, establish debtor credit limits, manage dilution risk, and ensure proper perfection of security interests (comprehensive UCC lien searches, UCC-1 filings, Notices of Assignment, and tri-party lockbox accounts). You will also collaborate cross-functionally with Product, Operations, and Risk teams to automate factoring workflows and shape the next generation of our working capital platform.

What You'll Do:
  • Factoring Credit Underwriting: Underwrite prospective client factoring facilities and establish credit limits on individual account debtors using credit agency reports (D&B, Experian, CreditSafe), payment trends, trade references, and financial statements.
  • UCC Search Analysis & Lien Perfection: Thoroughly read, interpret, and evaluate UCC lien searches, tax lien reports, and judgment filings; identify senior or conflicting security interests (blanket liens, inventory lenders, equipment PMSIs); and coordinate lien releases, terminations, subordination agreements, and intercreditor deeds to guarantee a first-priority position on factored accounts receivable.
  • Invoice Verification & Collateral Analysis: Review and verify invoices, purchase orders, bills of lading, and proof of delivery prior to funding; assess debtor concentration, aging trends, and customer dispute risk.
  • Dilution & Reserve Management: Model and monitor dilution factors (chargebacks, trade discounts, returns, co-op advertising offsets) to set appropriate advance rates and reserve holdbacks.
  • Legal & Perfection Controls: Oversee UCC-1 financing statement filings, continuous lien maintenance (amendments/continuations), Notice of Assignment (NOA) deliveries, and lockbox/account control agreements (DACA).
  • Portfolio & Debtor Monitoring: Track ongoing portfolio collections, remittance trends, daily lockbox reconciliations, aged accounts receivable, unapplied cash, and early warning signs of borrower or debtor distress.
  • Product Collaboration: Partner directly with Product, Engineering, and Risk Operations teams to translate manual factoring operations, lien checking, and verification logic into scalable, automated fintech software features.
  • AI-Driven Efficiency: Leverage AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) to accelerate credit memo generation, extract data from complex debtor agreements, and streamline verification audit trails.
What You’ll Need:
  • Direct Factoring Experience (Mandatory): Minimum of 3+ years of direct, hands-on commercial accounts receivable (A/R) factoring underwriting experience (recourse or non-recourse) within a commercial finance company, factoring house, bank factoring division, or specialized fintech. (Note: Standalone MCA, revenue-based financing, or general unsecured lending experience will not satisfy this requirement.)
  • UCC Lien Analysis & Perfection Expertise: Proven ability to read and interpret complex UCC lien search reports, identifying prior blanket liens, purchase money security interests (PMSIs), tax liens, and active encumbrances to structure lien releases, subordination agreements, and intercreditor deeds under UCC Article 9.
  • In-Depth Debtor Analysis: Demonstrated track record in evaluating Account Debtor risk, setting debtor-level credit limits, and handling credit insurance policies.
  • Verification & Operational Rigor: Thorough understanding of invoice verification methodologies, assignment procedures, lockbox structures, and dispute resolution.
  • Financial & Analytical Skills: Strong credit fundamentals, including balance sheet and P&L analysis, cash-flow modeling, and detailed A/R aging schedule dissection.
  • Fintech & Product Orientation: Desire to modernize legacy factoring processes and work alongside engineering teams to build automated underwriting and verification workflows.
  • Tech & AI Proficiency: 1+ years of practical experience using Generative AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) to optimize analytical and administrative workflows, along with proficiency in MS Excel/Google Sheets, SQL, and core factoring software platforms.

Candidate Experience Benchmark: Directly Qualifying Experience
(Required)Non-Qualifying Experience
(Does Not Meet Role Scope)
  • 3+ years of direct commercial invoice factoring underwriting (recourse and/or non-recourse).
  • Account Debtor credit underwriting and setting debtor credit lines.
  • Invoice verification, pre-advance audits, and confirmation calls/estoppels.
  • Notice of Assignment (NOA) management and dominion of funds via lockboxes.
  • Detailed Dilution analysis (returns, allowances, credit memos, co-op deductions).
  • Reading, interpreting, and clearing comprehensive UCC lien search reports, identifying prior blanket liens, PMSIs, and tax encumbrances.
  • Merchant Cash Advance (MCA) underwriting based solely on bank statement cash flows or credit card receivables.
  • Revenue-Based Financing (RBF) or daily/weekly ACH repayment products.
  • Broad Asset-Based Lending (ABL) relying strictly on blanket borrowing bases without invoice-level debtor verification.
  • Consumer credit or unsecured small-business term lending.

Job Description:

Role Overview

The Senior Manager, Information Security Risk Management (ISRM) Acquisitions & Divestitures (A&D) Cybersecurity, Pre-Close, reports directly to the Director, ISRM A&D Cybersecurity, Pre-Close and serves as a hands-on Deal Lead for cybersecurity due diligence across mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, licensing arrangements, minority investments, and strategic partnerships.

This role is responsible for leading deal-level cybersecurity assessments, translating diligence evidence into clear risk insights, identifying material technical and regulatory concerns, and supporting risk-informed transaction decisions before close. The Senior Manager brings strong technical depth across enterprise cybersecurity and technology domains and is expected to evaluate target-state environments, challenge assumptions, troubleshoot complex issues, and define practical mitigation recommendations.

The Senior Manager partners with Corporate Development, Legal, Privacy, Finance, Technology Services, ISRM capability and policy owners, business technology leaders, external advisors, and transaction teams to ensure cybersecurity risks, enterprise requirements, and Day 1 security priorities are understood, documented, escalated, and transitioned to post-close execution teams.

Key Responsibilities

  • Deal Lead for Pre-Close Cybersecurity Due Diligence: Serve as the primary ISRM A&D cybersecurity lead for assigned transactions, coordinating diligence activities, managing assessment timelines, tracking evidence needs, and ensuring findings are clearly documented for deal teams and leadership.
  • Technical Risk Assessment & Analysis: Evaluate target environments across security architecture, identity, network, endpoint, cloud, application security, data protection, vulnerability management, incident response, third-party risk, and cyber resilience to identify material risks, control gaps, remediation needs, and integration or separation implications.
  • Diligence Execution & Evidence Review: Lead cybersecurity questionnaire review, management meeting preparation, outside-in assessment coordination, documentation analysis, follow-up inquiries, advisor engagement, and consolidation of evidence into practical risk conclusions.
  • Transaction Risk Decision Support: Translate technical findings into business-relevant recommendations that inform risk acceptance, contractual protections, closing conditions, Day 1 priorities, remediation cost considerations, integration dependencies, and post-close commitments.
  • Stakeholder Coordination & Escalation: Partner with Corporate Development, Legal, Privacy, Finance, Technology Services, ISRM capability owners, business technology teams, external advisors, and deal sponsors to align expectations, resolve open questions, and escalate material risk issues through the Director and appropriate governance channels.
  • Pre-Close Readiness & Handoff: Translate diligence findings into structured Day 1 objectives, minimum security expectations, TSA considerations, risk register entries, dependency tracking, and handoff materials for post-close integration or separation execution.
  • Process, Playbook & Reporting Improvement: Contribute to the continuous improvement of diligence playbooks, questionnaires, risk taxonomies, scoring methods, templates, dashboards, reporting routines, intake workflows, and evidence standards to improve consistency and speed across the portfolio.
  • Team Leadership & Knowledge Sharing: Provide guidance to managers, analysts, advisors, and cross-functional contributors supporting assigned deals while promoting accountability, mentoring, lessons learned, and consistent use of approved A&D cybersecurity methods.

Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Security, Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Business, or a related discipline.
  • Advanced degree (MBA, MS, or equivalent) preferred.

Required Experience & Skills

  • 8+ years of progressive experience in cybersecurity, information risk management, technology delivery, security architecture, M&A transaction support, due diligence, integration or separation, or related disciplines.
  • Demonstrated experience leading or materially supporting cybersecurity due diligence, acquisition assessments, divestiture assessments, third-party security reviews, or complex risk assessments in time-sensitive business environments.
  • Strong technical background across security architecture, identity and access management, cloud and infrastructure security, endpoint security, network security, application security, data protection, vulnerability management, incident response, logging and monitoring, third-party risk, and cyber resilience.
  • Ability to analyze fragmented or incomplete diligence evidence, identify risk themes, ask effective follow-up questions, troubleshoot technical ambiguity, and separate material transaction risk from routine operational findings.
  • Experience translating technical cybersecurity findings into business-focused recommendations, risk narratives, remediation priorities, Day 1 considerations, contractual inputs, and post-close handoff requirements.
  • Working knowledge of privacy, legal, regulatory, and enterprise security obligations relevant to healthcare, MedTech, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, or other regulated global environments.
  • Strong understanding of recognized cybersecurity frameworks and standards, including NIST Cybersecurity Framework, ISO 27001, NIST 800-series publications, GDPR, HIPAA, and other applicable requirements.
  • Experience coordinating multiple workstreams, stakeholders, vendors, advisors, and deadlines across concurrent deals or complex programs.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate technical risk, business impact, unresolved assumptions, and decision needs to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Demonstrated ability to operate with confidentiality, urgency, sound judgment, and professionalism in ambiguous, high-pressure transaction environments.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience serving as a cybersecurity Deal Lead or workstream lead for acquisitions, divestitures, licensing transactions, minority investments, strategic partnerships, or joint ventures.
  • Experience developing or operating A&D cybersecurity diligence playbooks, questionnaires, control libraries, risk-scoring methods, issue logs, decision records, RACI models, and handoff criteria.
  • Experience performing outside-in cyber assessments, threat exposure reviews, breach history analysis, vendor risk analysis, or technical architecture reviews in support of transaction diligence.
  • Experience partnering with Corporate Development, Legal, Privacy, Finance, Technology Services, business technology teams, IMO/SMO functions, ISRM capability owners, external advisors, and managed service providers.
  • Experience in regulated healthcare, pharmaceutical, MedTech, manufacturing, life sciences, or similarly complex global environments.
  • Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, CISA, CCSP, CCSK, or equivalent credentials preferred.

Leadership Expectations

  • Operates as a technically credible, business-oriented cybersecurity leader who can balance transaction speed, deal confidentiality, regulatory obligations, technical risk, and enterprise security expectations.
  • Acts with ownership as the cybersecurity Deal Lead for assigned transactions, driving clarity, accountability, issue resolution, and timely escalation through the Director and governance channels.
  • Maintains security by design through practical technical challenge, sound risk judgment, disciplined documentation, and partnership with ISRM policy and capability owners.
  • Improves repeatability by contributing to standardized diligence methods, templates, reporting, automation, metrics, and lessons learned across the A&D cybersecurity portfolio.
  • Builds trust with stakeholders through concise communication, transparent risk framing, collaborative problem solving, mentoring, and high-quality execution.

AIR is seeking a Communications Specialist to develop and implement strategic communications initiatives that translate complex research and technical content into clear, engaging products for diverse audiences. The role encompasses content strategy, writing, digital communications, stakeholder engagement, project management, and team coordination. This position will be primarily staffed within AIR's Education Systems & Policy program, with opportunities to support projects across early childhood, PK-12, postsecondary education, workforce development, and adult learning.

Candidates hired for the position may work remotely within the United States (U.S.) or from one of our U.S. office locations. This does not include U.S. territories.

About AIR:

Founded in 1946 and headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, the American Institutes for Research (AIR) is a nonpartisan, not-for-profit organization that conducts behavioral and social science research and delivers technical assistance to address some of the most pressing challenges in the United States and globally. We generate evidence and apply data-driven solutions that expand opportunities and improve lives for all.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the development and implementation of strategic communications and dissemination plans that advance project goals and increase the visibility and impact of AIR's education work.
  • Serve as a trusted communications advisor to education project teams and clients, providing guidance on messaging, audience engagement, and outreach strategies.
  • Translate complex research, policy, and technical content into clear, accessible, and audience-centered communications products including infographics, videos, and short briefs.
  • Lead integrated communications campaigns and dissemination activities across digital, social, web, multimedia, and event platforms.
  • Oversee editorial planning, content development, and communications workflows to ensure high-quality, accessible deliverables.
  • Analyze communications metrics and audience data to assess performance and recommend strategies for continuous improvement.
  • Coordinate communications activities across multidisciplinary teams and manage multiple project priorities simultaneously.
  • Contribute to business development efforts, including proposal development, communications planning, and strategic growth initiatives.

Education, Knowledge, and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree with a minimum of 5 years of experience in Communications, Journalism, Public Relations, Public Policy, or a related field; or a Master's degree with a minimum of 4 years of experience in Communications, Journalism, Public Relations, Public Policy, or a related field.
  • Experience supporting external clients, managing small teams, and working in a shared services model.

Skills

  • Demonstrated ability to think strategically and align communications approaches with organizational, client, and project objectives.
  • Knowledge of dissemination and communication strategies that promote awareness, understanding, and use of research and evidence-based practices.
  • Strong consulting and relationship-management skills, including experience working with diverse stakeholders and client-facing teams.
  • Excellent writing, editing, and presentation skills, with the ability to convey complex information clearly and effectively to varied audiences.
  • Strong analytical skills and experience using audience, web, and communications performance data to inform planning.

  • Proficiency with digital communications platforms, content management systems, analytics tools, and accessible communications technologies used to create, disseminate, and evaluate communications products.
